**Rejected input diagnostic fully parses DOC** — `src/bin/jubarte.rs:2740-2754`

The CLI calls the reader even when already refusing the input, only to generate a conversion hint.

```
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {
        // Only a .doc that converts gets the hint; an encrypted document
        // or another OLE file would be sent to a command that fails.
        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
            format!(
                "; a .doc converts with: jubarte convert {} -o {}",
                path.display(),
                path.with_extension("docx").display()
            )
        } else {
            String::new()
        };
        return Err(format!("{refused}{hint}"));
```

#### Reachability

A caller supplying an untrusted legacy DOC piece table. Victim must process the supplied file; no privileged configuration is needed. legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown and doc_to_docx are public byte APIs. CLI convert also dispatches legacy input; no privileged configuration is required. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Public `legacy_doc::read`, `doc_to_docx` and `doc_to_markdown` accept caller bytes; native `convert` detects compound-file input and invokes this path. The shared CLI read_document refusal-hint branch also invokes legacy_doc::read before returning its unsupported-input message. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Public legacy_doc::read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and native CLI conversion process caller-supplied .doc. read_document also invokes full legacy read merely to generate a refusal hint. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Public legacy_doc::read/doc_to_docx and native CLI conversion/refusal hints invoke the vulnerable reader before DOCX limits.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author Supplier of untrusted input processed by a library consumer Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: legacy document supplier Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: An untrusted legacy document author. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Document supplier

- **Entry point:** legacy_doc::read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI conversion Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: legacy_doc::read and native convert

- **Outcome:** loss of availability of the parsing process Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Host process denial of service

Preconditions:
- Victim invokes the affected public API with attacker-controlled document input.
- Victim accepts and processes the supplied Word 97-2003 document.
- Victim reads/converts or invokes a CLI document path on the attacker-controlled legacy DOC.
- Structurally readable unencrypted OLE/FIB/piece table with valid reused offsets.

Existing controls:
- Physical stream bounds remain enforced; they do not bound logical expansion.
- Sector traversal is bounded and source offsets use checked arithmetic/bounds checks.
- Logical CP continuity does not prevent repeating the same physical source bytes.
- DOCX ZIP budgets do not govern legacy expansion before conversion creates a DOCX.

Limitations:
- Memory-safe reads remain bounded; no arbitrary code execution or confidentiality impact is established.

#### Severity

**Medium** — An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): high
- **Rationale:** Host process memory exhaustion.
- **Why:** Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Resource exhaustion of the embedding process, without established data access or execution. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Allocation failure can terminate the processing host.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): medium
- **Rationale:** Supported format and ordinary public parsing paths; no unusual configuration.
- **Why:** The triggering structure and values are document-controlled and not rejected by existing guards. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Compact valid physical mappings permit several orders of magnitude logical expansion. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Requires victim ingestion; actual shared deployment unknown.

#### Remediation

Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget. Replace full legacy parsing used only for diagnostic refusal hints with a cheap bounded probe, or apply the same logical/work budgets before that parser runs.

Tests:
- Aliased physical text pieces exceeding a small logical-character budget must refuse before StoryChar allocation.
- Preserve legitimate shared/fast-save pieces within the configured budget; cover maximum ccp_text and cumulative metadata budgets.
- Use small repeated physical aliases with a deliberately small decoded budget; assert typed refusal before expanding beyond it.
- Retain valid aliases, split UTF-16 surrogate handling and continuity/error cases.
- Use a small physical text stream with many increasing CP ranges sharing FC backing; assert a budget error before materialization.
- Retain tests accepting legitimate short FC aliases and refusing decreasing CPs, gaps and out-of-range physical references.
- A compact valid compound file with repeated FC pieces and excessive logical CP coverage must be refused before expansion.
- Boundary-sized permitted stories and legitimate reused text pieces should import successfully.
- CLI conversion must apply the same logical expansion budget as direct library calls.
- A valid piece table with increasing CPs but many references to one short physical range must return a resource-limit error before allocating proportional to its claimed story.
- Preserve legitimate repeated/fast-save pieces within the configured decoded-text limit.
- Reject compact piece tables whose repeated physical spans exceed the logical-character/work budget.
- Preserve legitimate fast-saved pieces and reject excessive logical stories before allocation.
- Repeated physical ranges cannot exceed the logical-character/decoded-output budget.
- Valid fast-save piece reuse remains supported within bounds.
- Provide many increasing logical piece ranges sharing a physical range; require a logical-character budget refusal before StoryChar growth.
- Assert adversarial small-input amplification is refused within active resource limits.
- Cover the inclusive accepted limits and preserve legitimate document behavior.
- Refuse repeated-span documents whose cumulative decoded story exceeds an explicit small test budget.
- Validate the logical budget before allocating StoryChar state.
- Keep valid physical span reuse supported below the budget.
- Use many contiguous logical pieces reusing a small physical byte range and assert refusal before record expansion.
- Cover checked cumulative length accounting, non-main-story ranges and both compressed and UTF-16 text.
- Use a small logical-character budget with repeated physical ranges and verify typed refusal before expansion.
- Cover exact budget boundary, legitimate reused text ranges, surrogate pairs and native CLI refusal-hint behavior.
- Add deterministic bounded-input regression coverage around the broken control; for filesystem staging use isolated integration cases with pre-existing symlink entries and verify unrelated files remain unchanged.
- Use a small deterministic document with extreme semantic values or alternate valid OPC paths and assert controlled refusal or complete selected sanitization before expensive processing.
- Reject repeated-fc pieces above a small configured logical budget while preserving legitimate fast-saved DOC files.
- Ensure CLI unsupported-input diagnostics do not fully materialize legacy text.

Preventive controls:
- Budget logical processing work and representation expansion, and bind preflight validation to the actual consumer's selected input.
- Give legacy parsing the same explicit admission-budget contract as DOCX parsing, including logical output work.

### [2] Converting cyclic Markdown drawing payloads can terminate the host process

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Direct static trace shows accepted input, unchecked dependency indexes and unconditional recursive re-entry; no deployment or runtime reproduction is assumed. |
| Category | Uncontrolled recursion |
| CWE | CWE-674 |
| Affected lines | src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs:1970-1974, src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs:1397-1408, src/markdown/write.rs:4188-4198, src/markdown/package.rs:1703-1712, src/markdown/write.rs:59-110 |

#### Summary

An attacker-supplied Markdown image with a `drawing:` payload can encode a dependency pointing back to itself. `markdown_to_docx` accepts the flat JSON graph and recursively materializes it without cycle detection, exhausting the stack or memory before conversion returns.

#### Root Cause

Markdown image destinations are decoded into `Drawing` objects and stored by `picture()`. `package::assemble` routes them through `PartRelate::drawing()` to `materialize()`. The dependency graph is attacker-defined flat JSON; `dep_part()` bounds only each index and uses a name set for collision avoidance. It has neither an active-index set nor a traversal budget, so an in-range self edge or mutual cycle never returns.

**Flat payload graph is deserialized without graph validation** — `src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs:1397-1408`

The attacker controls the base64 JSON and its flat dependency indexes; the JSON nesting limit does not validate graph cycles.

```rust
pub(crate) fn decode(dest: &str) -> Result<Drawing, String> {
    let encoded = dest
        .strip_prefix("drawing:")
        .ok_or_else(|| "not a drawing: destination".to_string())?;
    use base64::Engine;
    let bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
        .decode(encoded)
        .or_else(|_| {
            base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE.decode(encoded.trim_end_matches('='))
        })
        .map_err(|e| format!("drawing payload is not base64: {e}"))?;
    serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|e| format!("drawing payload is not its JSON: {e}"))
}
```

Any valid in-range dependency is passed to dep_part, including an attacker-defined self-referential node.

#### Validation

Confirmed public `markdown_to_docx` -\> `read` -\> `picture` -\> `package::assemble` -\> `PartRelate::drawing` -\> `materialize` -\> `dep_part`. A drawing with simple valid XML, no boxes, a root relation to dependency 0 and dependency 0 referring to itself bypasses box checks and repeatedly enters the same function.

Validation method: static source trace

- **Status:** validated

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Bounds checks reject out-of-range dependency indexes, but do not reject valid cyclic indexes.
- check_box_regions returns success for empty boxes and does not inspect dependency graphs (drawing.rs:1569-1576).
- Output-name collision handling and post-recursion byte deduplication cannot stop recursion.

Limitations:
- No application code or vulnerability-triggering input was executed.

#### Dataflow

Markdown image destination -\> base64 decode -\> serde Drawing graph -\> document.drawings -\> assembly -\> materialize -\> recursive dep_part cycle

- **Source:** attacker-controlled Markdown

- **Sink:** unbounded native call stack and intermediate names/XML allocations

- **Outcome:** conversion host exhaustion or termination

#### Reachability

Reachable through public Rust markdown_to_docx and its Python/WASM wrappers; CLI creation also forwards text to it. Requires the victim to process attacker-provided Markdown, with no control over victim configuration required.

- **Attacker:** untrusted Markdown author

- **Entry point:** markdown::markdown_to_docx; Python markdown_to_docx; WASM markdown_to_docx

Preconditions:
- A host converts attacker-provided Markdown.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A compact input deterministically reaches unbounded recursion in a public conversion API. Impact is availability of the processing host; shared-service exposure depends on the caller deployment.

Process isolation and strict CPU/memory budgets constrain impact; an exposed shared conversion service increases operational impact.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Denial of service in the processing process; no read/write escape or code execution established.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Flat small cyclic graph passes local type and index checks.

#### Remediation

Validate drawing dependency graphs before materialization. Reject cycles and excessive traversal depth/work, and memoize materialized indexes so shared dependencies are not repeatedly expanded.

Tests:
- Assert self cycles and two-node cycles return structured errors without recursion.
- Assert deeply nested and exponentially shared acyclic graphs obey an explicit work budget.
- Preserve valid shared dependency round trips.

#### Summary

With docprops enabled, scrub removes metadata only from three conventional filenames. A document using alternate package relationship targets can retain creators, editors, dates, company/manager or custom properties while scrub returns success. The custom-properties branch additionally skips relationship/content-type removal when docProps/custom.xml is absent, leaving an active relationship to a relocated target such as metadata/private.xml.

#### Root Cause

`scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization. Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Sensitive metadata is selected by physical conventional filenames rather than its authoritative package relationships/content type. Structural before/after validation checks only newly introduced findings; it does not certify that selected privacy fields were removed. The assigned remediation includes supported Strict relationship variants and coexistence of conventional and relocated targets.

**Properties scrub resolves fixed paths only** — `src/scrub.rs:357-384`

Alternate core/app/custom property targets are left intact; custom cleanup only runs when the conventional file exists.

```rust
fn scrub_properties(pkg: &mut PartFs) {
    if let Some(mut core) = Part::load(pkg, CORE) {
        let names = [
            XName::get("creator", DC),
            XName::get("lastModifiedBy", CP),
            XName::get("revision", CP),
            XName::get("lastPrinted", CP),
            XName::get("created", DCTERMS),
            XName::get("modified", DCTERMS),
        ];
        if remove_children(&mut core, &names) {
            core.store(pkg);
        }
    }
    if let Some(mut app) = Part::load(pkg, APP) {
        let names = [
            XName::get("Manager", EXTENDED),
            XName::get("Company", EXTENDED),
        ];
        if remove_children(&mut app, &names) {
            app.store(pkg);
        }
    }
    if pkg.part_bytes(CUSTOM).is_some() {
        pkg.remove_part(CUSTOM);
        pkg.remove_package_relationships_by_type(CUSTOM_REL);
        pkg.remove_content_type_override(&format!("/{CUSTOM}"));
    }
```

```rust
pub fn scrub(docx: &[u8], options: &ScrubOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ScrubError> {

        .main_document_part()
```

**Scrub returns package after named operations** — `src/scrub.rs:109-155`

The operation invokes scrub_properties and only checks whether new validation errors were introduced.

```rust
pub fn scrub(docx: &[u8], options: &ScrubOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ScrubError> {
    let mut pkg = PartFs::open(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .is_none_or(|main| pkg.part_bytes(&main).is_none())
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "the package has no main document part".into(),
        ));
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias
        && (alias.trim().is_empty() || alias.chars().any(char::is_control))
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "author_alias must be a nonempty name without control characters".into(),
        ));
    }
    let before = crate::validate::validate(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if options.comments {
        remove_comments(&mut pkg);
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias {
        alias_authors(&mut pkg, alias);
    }
    if options.rsids {
        remove_rsids(&mut pkg);
    }
    if options.docprops {
        scrub_properties(&mut pkg);
    }
    let out = pkg
        .to_zip()
        .map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    let after = crate::validate::validate(&out).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    let new = introduced(&before, &after);
    if !new.is_empty() {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(format!(
            "scrubbing would introduce {}",
            new.join(", ")
        )));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// The findings `after` has more of than `before`, as `CODE in part`,
/// counted by code and part: removing elements shifts the paths of
/// findings that were already there.
```

A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue. Parent verified default docprops=true, fixed core/app/custom handling, unchanged-part serialization and Ok(out) after only introduced-finding checks. Python Document.scrub promises the same defaults. Recipient byte inspection establishes disclosure without requiring Word UI behavior. Additional validated trace gives a bounded well-formed metadata/core.xml selected by a root relationship and appropriate content type; absent conventional docProps/core.xml skips removal. Default public/CLI docprops scrub returns unchanged private bytes because general validation only rejects newly introduced findings, not failed privacy postconditions. For docprops-only scrub with an absent conventional CUSTOM file, no custom relationship/content removal occurs; unchanged retained metadata introduces no new validation finding and therefore returns successfully. This is a supported package-loader path, not a claim about an observed Word deployment. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified scrub contract (5-24), default docprops (68-75), public pipeline (109-150), fixed constants (39-47), complete scrub_properties (357-385) and relationship-aware custom_props_part (document_comparer.rs:6180-6188). Alternate related metadata remains unchanged; before/after validation only rejects newly introduced structural findings. Metadata processing loads only CORE, APP and CUSTOM constants. No alternative-target lookup occurs, and PartFs serializes every remaining raw part and package relationship. Consequently an alternate core/app target keeps its selected fields, while an alternate custom target also keeps its relationship.

```rust
pub fn scrub(docx: &[u8], options: &ScrubOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ScrubError> {
    let mut pkg = PartFs::open(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .is_none_or(|main| pkg.part_bytes(&main).is_none())
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "the package has no main document part".into(),
        ));
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias
        && (alias.trim().is_empty() || alias.chars().any(char::is_control))
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "author_alias must be a nonempty name without control characters".into(),
        ));
    }
    let before = crate::validate::validate(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if options.comments {
        remove_comments(&mut pkg);
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias {
        alias_authors(&mut pkg, alias);
    }
    if options.rsids {
        remove_rsids(&mut pkg);
    }
    if options.docprops {
        scrub_properties(&mut pkg);
    }
    let out = pkg
        .to_zip()
        .map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    let after = crate::validate::validate(&out).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
```

#### Reachability

Default ScrubOptions enables docprops. The public scrub API opens package relationships without constraining property filenames; no operator configuration is required. The recipient needs access to the shared scrubbed output, not the original source or victim machine. The owner must enable docprops, which the default scrub settings do. Public scrub with default options and Python Document.scrub default options expose the behavior.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document supplier or outgoing document recipient recipient of a scrubbed document

- **Entry point:** scrub with docprops enabled scrub::scrub with docprops enabled

- **Outcome:** Access to identifying property values intended to be removed

Preconditions:
- Metadata uses an alternate package target.
- User scrubs before distributing the resulting document.
- Document stores identifying properties in nonconventional internal part names.
- Owner requests metadata removal and later shares the output.

#### Severity

**Medium** — The user invokes a privacy operation before sharing, yet identifying or confidential property data remains. A supplier controls package names/relationships; no host privilege is needed. The selected scrub deterministically misses alternate targets.

Impact depends on metadata sensitivity and sharing. Resolving selected metadata through relationships/content types and verifying removal closes the gap.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Potential identifying/confidential document properties exposed to an outgoing-document recipient.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Requires alternate part layout, sensitive metadata and sharing after scrub.

#### Remediation

Resolve all core, extended and custom property parts through authoritative package relationships and content types, sanitize every applicable internal target according to docprops selection, and remove corresponding custom-property parts/relationships/content-type records coherently. Verify the selected privacy postcondition; refuse unsupported or ambiguous layouts rather than returning a successfully scrubbed copy. Preserve intentional title/subject/application and revision-date retention. Missing/invalid selected targets require explicit refusal or documented safe handling; default public and CLI callers must enforce the same postcondition. Include supported Strict property relationship variants and regression cases containing both conventional and relocated targets; every active property target must satisfy the requested postcondition.

Tests:
- Use alternate core/app/custom filenames and case variants with valid relationships/content types.
- Confirm selected fields/parts are absent and references coherent afterward.
- Keep intentional title/subject/application retention.
- Integration tests relocate each metadata part and update its relationship/content type, then verify the same fields are removed from outgoing package bytes.
- Cover multiple metadata relationships and conventional paths without losing unrelated intentional content.
- Relocate core/extended/custom parts with corresponding relationships and assert default scrub removes identifying values.
- Scrub core, extended and custom properties at relocated relationship-selected targets and assert requested identities are absent.
- Cover conventional paths, multiple metadata relationships and missing/invalid targets with explicit refusals or documented handling.
- Relocate each supported document-property part and relationship and assert docprops removes the selected metadata.
- Verify no stale custom-properties relationship or content-type override remains.
- Scrub core/app/custom metadata at alternate relationship targets and require equivalent removal.
- Cover multiple metadata targets and conventional-path decoys.
- Relocate each property class independently with matching relationship/content type and verify requested fields or entire custom part are absent.
- Cover packages with both conventional and relocated targets and verify no active property target survives unexpectedly.

Preventive controls:
- Drive semantic metadata removal from OPC relationships/content types rather than conventional filenames.

#### Summary

A drawing: image destination in ordinary Markdown is base64-decoded and deserialized into a dependency graph without validation. Package materialization recursively follows each dep.rels.part before writing the dependent part and has no active-node or completed-node map. A one-node self-reference causes indefinite recursion and stack exhaustion, even with default Markdown conversion options and no image loader. Header/footer drawing payloads also reach this same materializer through view_stories::story_part. Capture memoizes a part before descending, so even capture-produced envelopes can encode a cycle; capture count/byte limits do not establish an acyclic imported graph. The supplied discovery-0030 trace additionally records that an empty boxes collection bypasses text-box-specific Writer finish checks; these checks do not validate the dependency graph.

#### Root Cause

Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it. The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The deserialization boundary accepts arbitrary graph edges, while materialization assumes acyclic capture output and tracks names rather than graph traversal state. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `picture` recognizes a caller-authored `drawing:` destination and `decode` base64-decodes it into serde graph structs. Package assembly invokes `materialize`, which follows a root `part` index into `deps`. `dep_part` reserves a fresh name and clones XML, then follows every dependent `part` index by calling itself before writing or memoizing the current part. A root pointing to dependency 0 whose own relationship points to 0 repeats indefinitely. Capture's 64-part limits are not validated by decode and would not rule out a one-node cycle anyway.

```rust
pub(crate) fn decode(dest: &str) -> Result<Drawing, String> {
    let encoded = dest
        .strip_prefix("drawing:")
        .ok_or_else(|| "not a drawing: destination".to_string())?;
    use base64::Engine;
    let bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
        .decode(encoded)
        .or_else(|_| {
            base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE.decode(encoded.trim_end_matches('='))
```

```rust
/// Write dependent part `index` and its own dependency closure; its new
/// part name.
fn dep_part(
    drawing: &Drawing,
    index: usize,
    package: &mut PartFs,
    existing: &HashSet<String>,
    used: &mut HashSet<String>,
    next_doc_pr: &mut u32,
) -> Option<String> {
    let dep = drawing.deps.get(index)?;
    let name = name_for(&dep.name, existing, used);
    used.insert(name.clone());
    // The part's own relationships name the parts the recursion is writing;
    // their ids land in a rewrite of its `d{index}.{n}` symbols.
    let mut xml = dep.xml.clone();
    for (n, rel) in dep.rels.iter().enumerate() {
        let (kind, target, external) = match (&rel.u, rel.part, &rel.raw) {
            (Some(url), _, _) => (rel.kind.clone(), url.clone(), true),
            (_, Some(inner), _) if inner < drawing.deps.len() => {
                let inner_name = dep_part(drawing, inner, package, existing, used, next_doc_pr)?;
                (
                    rel.kind.clone(),
                    relative_rel_target(&name, &inner_name),
                    false,
                )
            }
            (_, _, Some(raw)) => (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(&name, raw), false),
            _ => return None,
        };
```

```rust
pub(crate) fn materialize(
    drawing: &Drawing,
    package: &mut PartFs,
    part: &str,
    existing: &HashSet<String>,
    used: &mut HashSet<String>,
    next_doc_pr: &mut u32,
) -> Option<String> {
    let mut xml = drawing.xml.clone();
    for rel in &drawing.rels {
        let (kind, target, external) = match (&rel.u, rel.part, &rel.raw) {
            (Some(url), _, _) => (rel.kind.clone(), url.clone(), true),
            (_, Some(index), _) if index < drawing.deps.len() => {
                let name = dep_part(drawing, index, package, existing, used, next_doc_pr)?;
                (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(part, &name), false)
            }
            (_, _, Some(raw)) => (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(part, raw), false),
            _ => return None,
        };
        let rid = relate(package, part, &kind, &target, external);
        xml = xml.replace(&format!("\"{}\"", rel.sym), &format!("\"{rid}\""));
    }
    renumber_doc_pr(&mut xml, next_doc_pr);
    Some(xml)
```

```rust
    /// first use; `None` when the part is absent.
    fn dep_for(&mut self, package: &mut Package<'_>, target: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        if let Some(&index) = self.index.get(target) {
            return Some(index);
        }
        if self.parts.len() >= MAX_DEPS {
            self.failed = Some(format!("more than {MAX_DEPS} dependent parts"));
            return None;
        }
        let bytes = match package.read(target) {
            Ok(Some(bytes)) if bytes.len() as u64 <= MAX_DEP_BYTES => bytes,
            Ok(Some(_)) => {
                self.failed = Some(format!("{target} exceeds {MAX_DEP_BYTES} bytes"));
                return None;
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
        let index = self.parts.len();
        self.parts.push(Dep::default());
        self.index.insert(target.to_string(), index);
        let rels = package.rels(target).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut pay_rels = Vec::new();
```

```rust
    /// first use; `None` when the part is absent.
    fn dep_for(&mut self, package: &mut Package<'_>, target: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        if let Some(&index) = self.index.get(target) {
            return Some(index);
        }
        if self.parts.len() >= MAX_DEPS {
            self.failed = Some(format!("more than {MAX_DEPS} dependent parts"));
            return None;
        }
        let bytes = match package.read(target) {
            Ok(Some(bytes)) if bytes.len() as u64 <= MAX_DEP_BYTES => bytes,
            Ok(Some(_)) => {
                self.failed = Some(format!("{target} exceeds {MAX_DEP_BYTES} bytes"));
                return None;
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
        let index = self.parts.len();
        self.parts.push(Dep::default());
        self.index.insert(target.to_string(), index);
        let rels = package.rels(target).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut pay_rels = Vec::new();
```

```rust
/// Write dependent part `index` and its own dependency closure; its new
/// part name.
fn dep_part(
    drawing: &Drawing,
    index: usize,
    package: &mut PartFs,
    existing: &HashSet<String>,
    used: &mut HashSet<String>,
    next_doc_pr: &mut u32,
) -> Option<String> {
    let dep = drawing.deps.get(index)?;
    let name = name_for(&dep.name, existing, used);
    used.insert(name.clone());
    // The part's own relationships name the parts the recursion is writing;
    // their ids land in a rewrite of its `d{index}.{n}` symbols.
    let mut xml = dep.xml.clone();
    for (n, rel) in dep.rels.iter().enumerate() {
        let (kind, target, external) = match (&rel.u, rel.part, &rel.raw) {
            (Some(url), _, _) => (rel.kind.clone(), url.clone(), true),
            (_, Some(inner), _) if inner < drawing.deps.len() => {
                let inner_name = dep_part(drawing, inner, package, existing, used, next_doc_pr)?;
                (
                    rel.kind.clone(),
                    relative_rel_target(&name, &inner_name),
                    false,
                )
            }
            (_, _, Some(raw)) => (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(&name, raw), false),
            _ => return None,
        };
```

**Top-level relationship starts dependency traversal** — `src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs:1881-1904`

Top-level relationship starts dependency traversal

```rust
pub(crate) fn materialize(
    drawing: &Drawing,
    package: &mut PartFs,
    part: &str,
    existing: &HashSet<String>,
    used: &mut HashSet<String>,
    next_doc_pr: &mut u32,
) -> Option<String> {
    let mut xml = drawing.xml.clone();
    for rel in &drawing.rels {
        let (kind, target, external) = match (&rel.u, rel.part, &rel.raw) {
            (Some(url), _, _) => (rel.kind.clone(), url.clone(), true),
            (_, Some(index), _) if index < drawing.deps.len() => {
                let name = dep_part(drawing, index, package, existing, used, next_doc_pr)?;
                (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(part, &name), false)
            }
            (_, _, Some(raw)) => (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(part, raw), false),
            _ => return None,
        };
        let rid = relate(package, part, &kind, &target, external);
        xml = xml.replace(&format!("\"{}\"", rel.sym), &format!("\"{rid}\""));
    }
    renumber_doc_pr(&mut xml, next_doc_pr);
    Some(xml)
```

```rust
pub(crate) fn decode(dest: &str) -> Result<Drawing, String> {
    let encoded = dest
        .strip_prefix("drawing:")
        .ok_or_else(|| "not a drawing: destination".to_string())?;
    use base64::Engine;
    let bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
        .decode(encoded)
        .or_else(|_| {
            base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE.decode(encoded.trim_end_matches('='))
        })
        .map_err(|e| format!("drawing payload is not base64: {e}"))?;
    serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|e| format!("drawing payload is not its JSON: {e}"))
```
```rust
}
```

```rust
pub(crate) fn materialize(
    drawing: &Drawing,
    package: &mut PartFs,
    part: &str,
    existing: &HashSet<String>,
    used: &mut HashSet<String>,
    next_doc_pr: &mut u32,
) -> Option<String> {
    let mut xml = drawing.xml.clone();
    for rel in &drawing.rels {
        let (kind, target, external) = match (&rel.u, rel.part, &rel.raw) {
            (Some(url), _, _) => (rel.kind.clone(), url.clone(), true),
            (_, Some(index), _) if index < drawing.deps.len() => {
                let name = dep_part(drawing, index, package, existing, used, next_doc_pr)?;
                (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(part, &name), false)
            }
            (_, _, Some(raw)) => (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(part, raw), false),
            _ => return None,
        };
        let rid = relate(package, part, &kind, &target, external);
        xml = xml.replace(&format!("\"{}\"", rel.sym), &format!("\"{rid}\""));
    }
    renumber_doc_pr(&mut xml, next_doc_pr);
    Some(xml)
```

```rust
    /// first use; `None` when the part is absent.
    fn dep_for(&mut self, package: &mut Package<'_>, target: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        if let Some(&index) = self.index.get(target) {
            return Some(index);
        }
        if self.parts.len() >= MAX_DEPS {
            self.failed = Some(format!("more than {MAX_DEPS} dependent parts"));
            return None;
        }
        let bytes = match package.read(target) {
            Ok(Some(bytes)) if bytes.len() as u64 <= MAX_DEP_BYTES => bytes,
            Ok(Some(_)) => {
                self.failed = Some(format!("{target} exceeds {MAX_DEP_BYTES} bytes"));
                return None;
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
        let index = self.parts.len();
        self.parts.push(Dep::default());
        self.index.insert(target.to_string(), index);
        let rels = package.rels(target).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut pay_rels = Vec::new();
```

#### Reachability

Public markdown_to_docx with default DocxOptions accepts drawing: destinations independently of image-loader callbacks; Rust/Python/WASM consumers processing that Markdown reach the same importer. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Public markdown::markdown_to_docx accepts the Markdown directly; CLI and bindings wrap this library boundary. No image-loader callback or filesystem authority is needed.

- **Attacker:** Supplier of untrusted input processed by a library consumer Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: untrusted Markdown document producer

- **Entry point:** markdown::markdown_to_docx

- **Outcome:** converter availability loss

Preconditions:
- Victim invokes the affected public API with attacker-controlled document input.
- A victim converts the supplied Markdown.

Existing controls:
- Valid serde types and in-range dependency indices are checked, but a self-reference satisfies them.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Medium process-availability impact with high likelihood when an application processes attacker-controlled document bytes. No remote service or host-wide compromise is assumed.

Shared in-process deployments may suffer broader availability loss; external process resource limits contain host impact but still permit worker termination.

**Impact assessment:** Stack overflow or equivalent runtime resource failure terminates conversion and can abort a native in-process host.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** A small shallow JSON envelope can express the required integer cycle.

#### Remediation

Validate dependency indices, count/byte/depth limits and graph shape at import. Materialize with an active/completed traversal state and index-to-output map, rejecting cycles or reserving identities to support cycles without recursive expansion. Memoize shared subgraphs. Enforce explicit dependency-edge and traversal-work budgets before assembly; when rejecting active-node revisits return a typed conversion refusal. Apply the same graph validation and traversal state to header/footer drawing materialization, not only body drawings.

Tests:
- Use one-node and two-node cyclic dependency graphs and assert refusal or bounded supported materialization.
- Test repeated acyclic shared dependencies and import count/depth limits.
- Convert a self-cycle and a two-node cycle and assert a typed refusal without recursion.

### [5] Public Strict-format probe inflates unbounded document headers

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Independent parent source tracing confirms the entrypoint, failing control and sensitive operation. No exploit or application code executed. |
| Category | Unbounded decompression |
| CWE | CWE-409, CWE-400 |
| Affected lines | src/strict_translation.rs:670-675, src/strict_translation.rs:682-703, src/strict_translation.rs:670-703, src/strict_translation.rs:721-728, src/strict_translation.rs:670-700, src/strict_translation.rs:719-727, src/strict_translation.rs:670-676, src/strict_translation.rs:682-703, src/lib.rs:144, src/lib.rs:138-146, src/strict_translation.rs:719-728 |

#### Summary

The public main_part_is_strict helper reads word/document.xml without admission or an inflation/preamble cap. A compressible oversized/unfinished root opening tag or long XML comment keeps the last '\<' at offset zero; the full growing head remains retained and is repeatedly scanned until the root tag completes or EOF, allowing memory/CPU exhaustion for direct library consumers. The assigned audit establishes direct public-library exposure and found no in-repository production caller; ordinary rendering is not claimed to call this detector.

#### Root Cause

Public ZIP-reading sibling bypasses admission and assumes bytes since the last '\<' remain small, without bounding an individual opening tag. The same accumulating buffer is unbounded during comments as well as a root opening tag: rposition('\<') remains zero, drain(..0) drops nothing, and root_open scans the entire retained preamble after every 16 KiB read. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A boolean format probe bypasses package resource admission and assumes retaining bytes since the last \< bounds state; a long comment invalidates that assumption. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `main_part_is_strict()` opens word/document.xml directly. It appends decompressed chunks to `head` until finding `>`, then retains from the last `<`. With an unfinished root tag followed by a long whitespace run, that position remains zero and no bytes are discarded. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `main_part_is_strict` opens the ZIP and `word/document.xml` directly, then reads the part in chunks into `head`. While an opening tag contains only its initial '\<' and no '\>', draining before the last '\<' removes nothing. Each read therefore increases retained decompressed bytes and repeats delimiter scans across the accumulated tag. A highly compressible long run of spaces within the root tag reaches both unbounded memory growth and superlinear scanning before a boolean is returned.

**Public probe has no admission and an accumulating chunk loop** — `src/strict_translation.rs:670-703`

A small compressed comment causes unbounded inflation and repeated full-buffer scanning.

```rust
pub fn main_part_is_strict(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let Ok(mut archive) = crate::opc::open_archive(Cursor::new(bytes)) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Ok(mut part) = archive.by_name("word/document.xml") else {
        return false;
    };
    // The root element's opening tag follows whatever preamble the part
    // carries — a comment, a DOCTYPE — however long: read until it
    // appears, bounded by the part's own size, not by a window a long
    // preamble can push the root past (#561). Only the tail since the
    // last `<` can still hold the tag, so the head stays small.
    let mut head: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    let mut chunk = vec![0u8; 16 * 1024];
    loop {
        let Ok(read) = part.read(&mut chunk) else {
            return false;
        };
        if read == 0 {
            break;
        }
        head.extend(chunk.iter().copied().take(read));
        let window = String::from_utf8_lossy(&head);
        if let Some((start, _)) = root_open(&window)
            && window.split_at(start).1.contains('>')
        {
            break;
        }
        match head.iter().rposition(|&b| b == b'<') {
            Some(lt) => {
                head.drain(..lt);
            }
            None => head.clear(),
        }
```

```
pub fn main_part_is_strict(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let Ok(mut archive) = crate::opc::open_archive(Cursor::new(bytes)) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Ok(mut part) = archive.by_name("word/document.xml") else {
        return false;
    };
    // The root element's opening tag follows whatever preamble the part
    // carries — a comment, a DOCTYPE — however long: read until it
    // appears, bounded by the part's own size, not by a window a long
    // preamble can push the root past (#561). Only the tail since the
    // last `<` can still hold the tag, so the head stays small.
    let mut head: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    let mut chunk = vec![0u8; 16 * 1024];
    loop {
        let Ok(read) = part.read(&mut chunk) else {
            return false;
        };
        if read == 0 {
            break;
        }
        head.extend(chunk.iter().copied().take(read));
        let window = String::from_utf8_lossy(&head);
        if let Some((start, _)) = root_open(&window)
            && window.split_at(start).1.contains('>')
        {
            break;
        }
        match head.iter().rposition(|&b| b == b'<') {
            Some(lt) => {
                head.drain(..lt);
```
```rust
            }
            None => head.clear(),
        }
```

A long comment body causes this scan over all accumulated text each time.

```rust
/// Where `head` opens its root element: the first `<` an element name
/// follows (a comment, PI or DOCTYPE `<!`/`<?` opens none).
fn root_open(head: &str) -> Option<(usize, char)> {
    head.char_indices().find(|&(i, c)| {
        c == '<'
            && head
                .get(i.saturating_add(1)..)
                .is_some_and(|rest| rest.starts_with(char::is_alphabetic))
    })
}
```

**Detector is externally reachable** — `src/lib.rs:141-144`

The module is public, so callers can use this detector independently of the normal admitted conversion entrypoints.

```rust
pub mod scrub;
pub mod settings;
/// ISO Strict → Transitional package normalization.
pub mod strict_translation;
```

#### Reachability

Public strict_translation function accepts raw document bytes and documents no prerequisite gate. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `strict_translation` is a public module and the detector accepts arbitrary bytes without a required admitted-input type or an enforced admission precondition.

- **Attacker:** document supplier to a consumer using this API

- **Entry point:** strict_translation::main_part_is_strict

- **Outcome:** availability loss in that consumer

Preconditions:
- Consumer probes untrusted bytes directly without separately bounded admission.
- Victim calls the public detector on untrusted bytes; normal rendering does not call this function.

Existing controls:
- The normal strict_to_transitional reader limits input/inflation; this separate function does not call it.
- ZIP structural validation checks headers and extents, not the inflated XML preamble.
- Source policy excludes raw infallible XML parser guarantees, but this is an independently exposed archive probe rather than a direct raw parse call.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Medium process-availability impact with high likelihood when the public probe processes untrusted archives. No remote deployment assumed.

A separate caller-owned admission step constrains the path; direct public callers need explicit limits.

**Impact assessment:** Process memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Long compressible tag deterministically drives the unbounded public parser when invoked.

#### Remediation

Apply bounded admission before indexing/inflation and explicit cumulative inflated-byte/preamble/work limits to this public helper. Use a streaming lexical probe with bounded retained state for comments, declarations and chunk-spanning root tags; refuse excessive probes with a checked/limited API and safe default limits.

Tests:
- Test oversized compressed opening tags under a small budget and retain valid within-budget preambles.
- Long compressed comments must hit a deterministic input/work bound.
- A chunk-spanning legal prolog should be recognized with constant retained state.
- An unfinished oversized opening tag terminates classification within a bounded budget.
- Long legitimate preambles retain supported behavior without unbounded head growth.
- Feed an over-budget compressed opening tag and assert a bounded refusal/false result before large retention.
- Test long preambles and quote-aware delimiter parsing with explicit limits.
- Use a small deterministic document with extreme semantic values or alternate valid OPC paths and assert controlled refusal or complete selected sanitization before expensive processing.

Preventive controls:
- Require every public compressed-input probe to share admission and incremental work budgets.

### [6] Rendering an HTML chunk can allocate gigabytes from a single colspan value

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Both independent baseline and focused investigator identified the mechanism; parent verified input parsing, post-admission expansion and allocation loop statically. No runtime reproduction was executed. |
| Category | Uncontrolled resource allocation Unbounded allocation from HTML numeric input Unbounded generated markup expansion |
| CWE | CWE-789, CWE-400, CWE-770, CWE-834 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/mod.rs:772-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:33-39, src/convert/altchunk.rs:557-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-491, src/convert/mod.rs:789-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:34-39, src/convert/altchunk.rs:558-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-490, src/convert/altchunk.rs:558-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-490, src/convert/mod.rs:789-800, src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:34-39, src/convert/mod.rs:773-798, src/convert/mod.rs:422-460, src/convert/mod.rs:762-799, src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-493, src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-566, src/convert/mod.rs:769-798 |

#### Summary

A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory.

#### Root Cause

with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later. The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output.

```rust
/// Render a DOCX package to PDF and return the font-resolution report for

/// # Errors

pub fn docx_to_pdf_report(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<ConvertedPdf, ConvertError> {
```

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

```rust
pub(crate) fn expand(xml: &str, load: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(xml.len());
    let mut rest = xml;
    while let Some(at) = rest.find("<w:altChunk") {
        out.push_str(&rest[..at]);
        let tail = &rest[at..];
        let Some(open_end) = tail.find('>') else {
            // The prefix has already been copied; retain only the unfinished
            // chunk suffix when this diagnostic input cannot be expanded.
            out.push_str(tail);
            return out;
        };
        let open = &tail[..=open_end];
        let end = if open.ends_with("/>") {
            open_end + 1
        } else {
            tail.find("</w:altChunk>")
                .map_or(open_end + 1, |i| i + "</w:altChunk>".len())
        };
        let wml = attr(open, "id")
            .and_then(|rid| load(&rid))
            .and_then(|bytes| chunk_html(&bytes))
            .map(|html| html_to_wml(&html))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        out.push_str(&wml);
        rest = &tail[end..];
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
```

```rust
    fn end_table(&mut self) {
        self.close_open_cell();
        self.flush();
        let Some(table) = self.tables.pop() else {
            return;

            .rows
```

```rust
                    "<w:{edge} w:val=\"single\" w:sz=\"4\" w:space=\"0\" w:color=\"auto\"/>"

            s.push_str("</w:tblBorders>");
        }
        s.push_str("<w:tblLayout w:type=\"fixed\"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid>");
```

Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML. The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing. Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow. Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize. Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): `with_layout` resolves a related package part and invokes `expand`; `expand` routes HTML/MHT to `html_to_wml`. The tokenizer dispatches a `td` to `Builder::start`, whose positive usize span has no upper bound. Closing `table` invokes `end_table`, which writes one record per span before parsing the resulting XML. `1000000000` fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and avoids relying on integer overflow.

```rust
pub fn docx_to_pdf_report(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<ConvertedPdf, ConvertError> {

fn docx_to_pdf_body(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
```

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

**chunk repeat** — `src/convert/altchunk.rs:15-43`

```rust
pub(crate) fn expand(xml: &str, load: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(xml.len());
    let mut rest = xml;
    while let Some(at) = rest.find("<w:altChunk") {
        out.push_str(&rest[..at]);
        let tail = &rest[at..];
        let Some(open_end) = tail.find('>') else {
            // The prefix has already been copied; retain only the unfinished
            // chunk suffix when this diagnostic input cannot be expanded.
            out.push_str(tail);
            return out;
        };
        let open = &tail[..=open_end];
        let end = if open.ends_with("/>") {
            open_end + 1
        } else {
            tail.find("</w:altChunk>")
                .map_or(open_end + 1, |i| i + "</w:altChunk>".len())
        };
        let wml = attr(open, "id")
            .and_then(|rid| load(&rid))
            .and_then(|bytes| chunk_html(&bytes))
            .map(|html| html_to_wml(&html))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        out.push_str(&wml);
        rest = &tail[end..];
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
```

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Original archive size, entry and inflation limits apply before expansion, preventing ZIP bombs but not semantic numeric amplification.
- Native process resource limits can terminate/contain a worker, not make the conversion return a bounded refusal.
- Chunk bytes are package-local, without a filesystem or network fetch.
- Input budgets bound original archive/XML bytes rather than generated markup.
- Page pixel limits and caller process limits do not bound this earlier work.
- Separate from native WML grid-vector allocation: this path must be stopped in HTML expansion itself.
- A downstream OOXML table-column limit cannot contain this earlier generator; no network/filesystem fetch is needed for the package-local chunk.
- ZIP and XML budgets limit original package entries; they do not limit the numeric colspan or derived WML.
- Page raster MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is reached later and does not constrain this importer.
- Archive compressed/inflated-byte, entry, XML depth and tag limits exist; the input with one short HTML attribute fits those limits.
- The chunk loader only looks up pkg.part_bytes using the resolved relationship path (src/convert/mod.rs:790-793,21301-21304); it performs no network request. The finding uses an internal HTML part.
- SECURITY.md recommends CPU/memory-constrained processes and disclaims universal denial-of-service protection; these contain consequences but do not bound the expansion.
- Archive inflation and XML input limits apply to original package bytes, which can remain tiny.
- The parser defaults invalid/zero spans to one but valid huge positive spans remain unrestricted.
- Process resource limits recommended by SECURITY.md constrain host impact without rejecting the expansion.
- Package admission bounds archive and inflated part bytes, but the HTML remains small and the expansion occurs afterward.
- External relationship resolution is not required; an ordinary internal HTML part is sufficient.
- Process memory/CPU limits are documented caller controls and do not prevent the small-input amplification inside a worker.
- Input admission bounds archive bytes/entries/depth and callers are advised to impose CPU/memory limits; neither limits HTML colspan or generated grid size.
- The effect requires rendering an attacker-supplied document; no remote service deployment was assumed.
- Archive admission runs before expansion and limits actual input bytes, not the numeric span or generated XML (src/admission.rs:531-551).
- Existing tests handle invalid, negative and zero spans and ordinary span 2, but show no maximum-span rejection (src/convert/altchunk.rs:1026-1054).
- SECURITY.md requires hosts to apply process CPU/memory limits; these mitigate host scope but do not bound this loop.

#### Reachability

Default public PDF/PNG converter expands internal altChunk parts after admission. Attacker needs only control over a document processed by the victim. Untrusted document suppliers reach this importer whenever the public renderer processes their DOCX. The input need not be large, and no release/OS authority is needed. Public Rust PDF/render APIs and Python/WASM wrappers accept document bytes. A normal table in an internal HTML altChunk reaches this path after admission; no special host setting or raised input limits are required.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted DOCX author untrusted document supplier Provider of an untrusted document rendered by a victim/library consumer

- **Entry point:** convert::docx_to_pdf / render convert::docx_to_pdf and shared layout/render APIs convert::docx_to_pdf / convert::render and bindings

- **Outcome:** Memory/CPU exhaustion and process termination or WASM failure

Preconditions:
- Victim invokes document rendering on the supplied file.
- Victim renders a document containing the supplied chunk.
- Victim renders attacker-supplied DOCX containing an internal HTML/MHT altChunk.

Existing controls:
- Original archive and XML limits apply before conversion.
- External process resource limits can contain impact.

Limitations:
- No file disclosure or code execution established.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. Loss of embedding process/instance availability.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** No special feature option or external resource is needed; a small valid HTML chunk suffices. A small numeric HTML field directly determines work.

#### Remediation

Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/aggregate column counts before generating any table XML. Charge all HTML/MHT-generated WML, including repeated/nested tables, to a cumulative byte/work budget inside altChunk expansion and return a typed input-limit refusal before allocation or DOM construction.

Tests:
- A tiny HTML chunk with colspan=1000000000 must refuse before allocation.
- Check multi-cell aggregate span overflow and repeated/nested table expansion budgets.
- Excessive individual/cumulative colspan in HTML and MHT must fail with bounded output/work.
- Cover malformed spans, overflow and nested tables.
- Preserve valid small HTML tables.
- Unit tests with a small configured column cap cover the inclusive limit, one above it, oversized numeric values, and sums of several otherwise valid spans.
- Integration test through a DOCX altChunk confirms refusal occurs before grid generation.
- Use a tiny in-memory altChunk HTML with excessive td/th colspan and assert a prompt typed refusal without output growth.
- Exercise cumulative spans across multiple cells, numeric overflow and valid inclusive limits.
- A tiny altChunk with colspan 1000000000 must fail before large output allocation.
- Cover inclusive limits, cumulative spans across cells, integer overflow, nested tables, and both HTML and MHT import.
- Reject an oversized colspan in a small admitted DOCX without allocating proportional output.
- Cover aggregate spans across multiple cells and arithmetic overflow while preserving normal merged tables.
- A one-cell HTML table with an excessive numeric colspan returns a typed refusal without allocating proportional output.
- Multiple spans cannot overflow the cumulative count or bypass the generated-grid limit.
- Ordinary bounded colspan tables retain rendering behavior.
- Reject huge representable positive colspan through public rendering while retaining ordinary span behavior.
- Verify many bounded spans cannot exceed the cumulative table/output budget.
- Verify row-span sum overflow returns a refusal on native and wasm32.

Preventive controls:
- Charge representation expansion to explicit output/work budgets rather than relying only on compressed/inflated input limits.
- Budget derived representations before materialization, including post-admission HTML/MHT expansion.

<a id="finding-7"></a>

### [7] Redacting text can leave recoverable copies in UTF-16 XML

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent verified UTF-16 admission, untouched-part preservation, UTF-8-only XML leak scanning and success on an empty result. No end-to-end application execution was performed. |
| Category | Incomplete sensitive-data redaction |
| CWE | CWE-200 |
| Affected lines | src/admission.rs:764-781, src/edit.rs:5381-5386, src/edit.rs:5420-5427, src/edit/prepared.rs:798-808, src/edit.rs:4724-4747, src/scrub.rs:467-472, src/scrub.rs:527-533 |

#### Summary

A successful redact edit can retain the same secret in a UTF-16 `customXml` part. Admission accepts that encoding, but the final leak check treats XML as UTF-8 and misses the duplicate before returning the clean DOCX.

#### Root Cause

Admission and redaction disagree about XML encoding. The package accepts UTF-16 XML and preserves untouched part bytes, but leaks_within routes XML suffixes exclusively through from_utf8_lossy. The resulting BOM replacement/NUL-interleaved text cannot be parsed or match a normal multi-character needle. xml_holds returns a negative raw string search, so check_redactions treats an incomplete scan as clean.

**Admission supports UTF-16 XML** — `src/admission.rs:764-781`

A valid UTF-16LE/BE customXml part containing the secret passes the same semantic XML admission as UTF-8.

```rust
/// A part's text for scanning. Word writes UTF-8, but a part may be UTF-16
/// with a byte-order mark (SharePoint's `customXml` items often are) and
/// Word opens it, so it is transcoded; other bytes decode lossily, as the
/// rest of the engine reads them.
fn part_text(xml: &[u8]) -> Cow<'_, str> {
    let utf16 = |rest: &[u8], unit: fn([u8; 2]) -> u16| {
        let units = rest.as_chunks::<2>().0.iter().map(|&pair| unit(pair));
        Cow::Owned(
            char::decode_utf16(units)
                .map(|c| c.unwrap_or(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER))
                .collect(),
        )
    };
    match xml {
        [0xFF, 0xFE, rest @ ..] => utf16(rest, u16::from_le_bytes),
        [0xFE, 0xFF, rest @ ..] => utf16(rest, u16::from_be_bytes),
        _ => String::from_utf8_lossy(xml),
    }
```

```rust
    /// Refuse the plan when the text of a redaction still occurs in one of

    /// document properties). The message names the parts, never the text.
    fn check_redactions(&self, outputs: &[&[u8]]) -> Result<(), EditError> {
        for (op, operation) in self.plan.operations.iter().enumerate() {
            let OperationKind::Redact { find, .. } = &operation.kind else {
                continue;
            };
            let parts: std::collections::BTreeSet<String> = outputs
                .iter()
                .flat_map(|doc| crate::scrub::leaks(doc, find))
                .collect();
            if parts.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let message = format!(
                "the redacted text still occurs in {}; redact every copy in the same plan, or remove the comment or part that holds it",
                parts.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
            );
            let mut error = self.conflict(op, &message);
            error.code = "REDACTION_LEAK".into();
            error.outcomes[op].code = Some(error.code.clone());
            return Err(error);
        }
```

#### Reachability

A document producer can supply duplicate content in standard custom XML, or an output recipient can exploit an existing duplicate. The victim invokes redact and shares the result under its fail-closed guarantee.

- **Attacker:** A document producer who embeds a duplicate of text that a recipient will redact, or a recipient of an exported document containing such a duplicate.

- **Entry point:** Public edit redaction and scrub::leaks

- **Outcome:** Recover the text the user intended to remove.

Existing controls:
- The leak scanner checks both output packages, bounds archive inflation and fails closed on archive/read errors.
- It detects UTF-8 XML entities, split Word text runs, and raw UTF-16LE in non-XML parts; existing tests at src/scrub.rs:667-735 establish those controls but omit UTF-16 XML.
- This does not require an invalid XML part: admission intentionally transcodes UTF-16 customXml inputs.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A recipient can recover sensitive text from an artifact the user believed was checked for complete redaction. Exploitation requires a duplicate encoded XML part and subsequent sharing of the successful output; the sensitivity and deployment are unknown.

Evidence that the workflow routinely publishes highly sensitive redacted documents would raise impact; rejecting or correctly decoding every supported XML encoding would prevent disclosure.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Potential disclosure of the redacted secret.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Requires a UTF-16 duplicate and later distribution of the output.

#### Remediation

Share the XML decoder used by admission with the leak scanner, decode UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE before xml_holds, and refuse unrecognized/invalid encodings rather than silently classifying them as clean. Preserve raw-byte checks as defense in depth. Add redaction tests proving a UTF-16 customXml duplicate causes REDACTION_LEAK and no artifact is returned.

Tests:
- Redact a UTF-8 paragraph with UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE customXml duplicates and require REDACTION_LEAK.
- Exercise unsupported or invalid XML encodings and ensure the checker fails closed.

### [8] Listing many comments over one large range multiplies retained anchor text

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Source-backed input-to-operation trace and explicit controls/counterevidence; no application execution or deployment assumption. |
| Category | Allocation without resource limits |
| CWE | CWE-770 |
| Affected lines | src/comments.rs:132-156, src/comments.rs:380-398 |

#### Summary

A document with many comments covering the same large text range is small relative to the comment listing it produces. list_comments copies the full range into every CommentRecord without an expanded-output budget, allowing a compact document to demand gigabytes of retained memory.

#### Root Cause

comments_in materializes all comment records into a Vec and calls Anchors::fill for each one. fill clones the entire anchored paragraph or joined range into each record independently. Shared source text is therefore retained once per comment, with no aggregate anchor/output limit.

**Public comment listing materializes records** — `src/comments.rs:132-156`

Caller-controlled comments are collected into a single Vec and filled one by one.

```rust
pub fn list_comments(docx: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<CommentRecord>, CommentError> {
    comments_in(&mut Opened::open(docx)?)
}

/// [`list_comments`] of a package already open. The scan marks up the
/// body's DOM, so read what else `opened` holds first.
pub(crate) fn comments_in(opened: &mut Opened) -> Result<Vec<CommentRecord>, CommentError> {
    let family = CommentFamily::load(&opened.pkg, &opened.main).map_err(CommentError::Package)?;
    if family.is_empty() {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }
    let mut anchors = Anchors::default();
    anchors.scan("body", &mut opened.dom, opened.body, true);
    for (id, _, part) in opened.story_parts() {
        let (mut dom, _, root) = crate::inspect::parse_part(&opened.pkg, &part)?;
        anchors.scan(&id, &mut dom, root, false);
    }
    Ok(family
        .order()
        .into_iter()
        .map(|id| {
            let mut record = family.record(id);
            anchors.fill(&mut record);
            record
        })
```

#### Dataflow

Many distinct comment anchors covering one shared long text range -\> Public comments::list_comments and consumers -\> Per-record anchor_text cloning into collected Vec\<CommentRecord\>

- **Outcome:** Host availability loss through disproportionate memory allocation.

- Victim lists comments or invokes a consumer that materializes full anchor text.

**Medium** — High availability impact with medium likelihood because document content alone controls comment count and overlapping range size; a victim must request comment listing or a consumer that lists them.

Effective host isolation and narrower exposure lower impact/likelihood; automatic untrusted workflows increase exposure.
