Enforce a cumulative comment-anchor/output byte budget before cloning, return a typed refusal or bounded/truncated representation, and consider shared ranges or streaming records instead of duplicating every full anchor in memory.

### [9] PDF font subsetting can enumerate billions of codepoints

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | The repository callback is unbounded and matching installed ttf-parser range iteration was inspected; no runtime workload was executed. |
| Category | Excessive iteration Excessive iteration over attacker-defined font ranges |
| CWE | CWE-834 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/font_table.rs:220-230, src/convert/pdf.rs:455-471, src/convert/pdf.rs:1285-1288, src/convert/pdf.rs:1434-1451, src/convert/font_table.rs:212-242, src/convert/font.rs:1480-1501, src/convert/pdf.rs:462-469, src/convert/pdf.rs:1286-1288, src/convert/pdf.rs:1434-1449 |

#### Summary

An embedded TrueType font with a compact format12 or format13 cmap range ending at u32::MAX can make PDF conversion perform about 4.29 billion callbacks. The converter only keeps BMP entries, but filters them after the unbounded enumeration. Assigned discovery-0032 preserves Windows platform 3/encoding 10 format13 acceptance and the inclusive full-u32 group: 4294967296 callbacks. Tuple evaluation also performs glyph lookup when u16 conversion fails.

#### Root Cause

subset_cmap calls a dependency's codepoints iterator on each Unicode subtable without bounding its authored ranges. The later u16 conversion only discards results; it cannot prevent iteration. Format12/13 store a range in a small record and the matching dependency enumerates every u32 value in that range. Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): A valid selected embedded face reaches `subset_keep_gids()` and `subset_cmap()`. `subset_cmap()` calls `sub.codepoints()` on every Unicode subtable, then checks `u16::try_from(cp)` inside the callback. The locally selected dependency's format-12/13 implementations enumerate each integer in encoded ranges, with no Unicode-domain or aggregate-work cap. Thus the BMP output restriction occurs after expensive enumeration; the tuple also evaluates `sub.glyph_index(cp)` even when u16 conversion fails.

#### Validation

Used embedded glyf faces reach subset_keep_gids and subset_cmap. ttf-parser0.25.1 format12/13 parse group records without a Unicode upper bound and codepoints loops start_char_code..=end_char_code. A valid format13 range can map visible text to an existing glyph while covering 0..u32::MAX. The parent callback still runs for non-BMP values, and its tuple evaluates glyph lookup even when u16 conversion fails. Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Verified ttf-parser 0.25.1 is selected by Cargo.lock. Its format13 parser reads group storage without bounding start/end to Unicode scalars, codepoints loops start_char_code..=end_char_code, and is_unicode accepts Windows platform 3 encoding 10 for format13. A single 0..0xffffffff group mapped to a valid glyph therefore yields 4,294,967,296 callbacks. Repository BMP and used-glyph checks are inside the callback and do not bound the enumeration.

Validation method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

- **Status:** validated

#### Reachability

A sender provides a used embedded font with a large Unicode cmap range and a caller renders PDF.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document/font provider

- **Outcome:** Billions of callback/glyph lookup operations

#### Severity

**Medium** — A document/font provider can monopolize the converting process through a compact font table with high likelihood. Impact is availability loss; no remote service or code execution is inferred.

Clamping or replacing codepoint enumeration with bounded BMP lookup removes the path; a shared-service deployment would increase impact.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Conversion availability loss.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** A compact unbounded range directly controls iteration.

#### Remediation

Generate the BMP subset by bounded codepoint lookup or explicitly intersect and budget ranges before enumeration. Bound cumulative iteration across subtables, including overlapping ranges. Additional retained remediation detail: Enumerate the bounded output codepoint domain directly, or intersect encoded ranges with it before enumeration. Bound aggregate mappings/work across subtables and reject invalid or excessive ranges before callbacks.

Tests:
- Cover format12 and format13 ranges extending beyond Unicode and u16 bounds without enumerating them.
- Verify many overlapping subtables also respect a cumulative work budget.
- Subset a minimal format13 full-u32 range under a deterministic small work budget and assert bounded handling.
- Cover format12, overlapping groups, non-BMP ranges and multiple subtables while preserving normal BMP mappings.

### [10] Repeated relationship IDs trigger quadratic repair work

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent independently inspected the cited source and actual caller/control path. Exploit inputs and resource exhaustion were not executed. |
| Category | Algorithmic complexity denial of service |
| CWE | CWE-407 |
| Affected lines | src/opc/mod.rs:99-124, src/opc/mod.rs:222-250, src/opc/mod.rs:520-542, src/opc/mod.rs:99-126, src/opc/mod.rs:520-546, src/opc/mod.rs:99-120, src/opc/mod.rs:524-539, src/opc/mod.rs:222-234, src/opc/mod.rs:520-541, src/opc/mod.rs:99-125, src/opc/mod.rs:222-250, src/opc/mod.rs:524-542, src/opc/mod.rs:1064-1093 |

#### Summary

Opening a package repairs identical duplicate relationship IDs. For n distinct IDs each repeated identically, each repair linearly searches an increasingly long Vec, producing quadratic CPU work on shallow metadata that fits existing byte and attribute limits.

#### Root Cause

Duplicate reporting uses repaired.contains on a growing Vec even though first-occurrence lookup already uses a HashMap. Root and every part relationship set invoke this repair. N distinct IDs each duplicated identically require N(N-1)/2 prior-ID string comparisons despite first-occurrence hashing; byte/depth/attribute checks do not limit this product. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): An ordered report vector is also used as a membership set, so the first duplicate of each new ID scans all preceding repaired IDs. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read_relationships` preserves the record list and `PartFs::open_within` invokes `drop_repeated_relationships`. Its `seen` map finds duplicates efficiently, but each duplicate then uses `repaired.contains` over all previously repaired IDs. Repeating each of N distinct IDs twice requires roughly N(N-1)/2 string comparisons.

**Linear search for every distinct duplicate** — `src/opc/mod.rs:99-124`

Linear search for every distinct duplicate supports the validated source-to-sink trace.

```rust
fn drop_repeated_relationships(rels: &mut Relationships) -> Result<Vec<String>, OpcError> {
    let mut seen: HashMap<&str, &Relationship> = HashMap::new();
    let mut repaired: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut keep = Vec::with_capacity(rels.items.len());
    for item in &rels.items {
        match seen.get(item.id.as_str()) {
            None => {
                seen.insert(&item.id, item);
                keep.push(true);
            }
            Some(first) => {
                if first.rel_type != item.rel_type
                    || first.target != item.target
                    || first.target_mode != item.target_mode
                {
                    return Err(OpcError::InvalidRelationship);
                }
                if !repaired.contains(&item.id) {
                    repaired.push(item.id.clone());
                }
                keep.push(false);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut keep = keep.into_iter();
    rels.items.retain(|_| keep.next().unwrap_or(true));
```

```rust
    pub(crate) fn open_within(
        bytes: &[u8],
        limits: crate::admission::InputLimits,
    ) -> Result<Self, OpcError> {
        let mut fs = read_package(bytes, limits)?;
        let mut repaired_duplicate_ids: Vec<(String, String)> =
            drop_repeated_relationships(&mut fs.package_rels)?
                .into_iter()
                .map(|id| (String::new(), id))
                .collect();
        let mut owners: Vec<&String> = fs.part_rels.keys().collect();
        owners.sort();
        let owners: Vec<String> = owners.into_iter().cloned().collect();
        for owner in owners {
            if let Some(rels) = fs.part_rels.get_mut(&owner) {
                let part = owner.trim_start_matches('/').to_string();
                repaired_duplicate_ids.extend(
                    drop_repeated_relationships(rels)?
                        .into_iter()
                        .map(|id| (part.clone(), id)),
                );
            }
        }
        fs.repaired_duplicate_ids = repaired_duplicate_ids;
        Ok(fs)
    }
```

**Retain all relationship records** — `src/opc/mod.rs:222-250`

The parser retains each independently decoded relationship, including identical duplicate IDs.

```rust
fn read_relationships(xml: &[u8]) -> Result<Relationships, OpcError> {
    let mut rels = Relationships::new();
    let mut items = Vec::new();
    for record in metadata_records(
        xml,
        "Relationships",
        "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships",
        &["Relationship"],
    )? {
        for item in oxml_opc::Relationships::from_xml(&record)?.items {
            items.push(item);
        }
    }
    // Seed the private counter once: add_with_id removes existing IDs, so
    // calling it for every record would turn a linear read into a quadratic one.
    // A fresh collection also has no retained source XML: to_xml stays canonical.
    if let Some((_, item)) = items
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|item| {
            item.id
                .strip_prefix("rId")
                .and_then(|id| id.parse::<u32>().ok())
                .map(|id| (id, item))
        })
        .max_by_key(|(id, _)| *id)
    {
        rels.add_with_id(&item.id, &item.rel_type, &item.target);
    }
    rels.items = items;
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn a_repeated_relationship_id_is_repaired_when_identical_and_refused_otherwise() {
        let font = |id: &str, target: &str| {
            format!(
                r#"<Relationship Id="{id}" Type="{HYPERLINK}" Target="{target}" TargetMode="External"/>"#
            )
        };
        let same = package_with_document_rels(&format!(
            "{}{}{}",
            font("rId1", "https://a.example/"),
            font("rId2", "https://b.example/"),
            font("rId1", "https://a.example/")
        ));
        let fs = PartFs::open(&same).unwrap();
        let rels = fs.read_rels_for("word/document.xml").unwrap();
        let ids: Vec<&str> = rels.items.iter().map(|r| r.id.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(ids, ["rId1", "rId2"]);
        assert_eq!(
            fs.repaired_duplicate_ids(),
            [("word/document.xml".to_string(), "rId1".to_string())]
        );
        let conflict = package_with_document_rels(&format!(
            "{}{}",
            font("rId1", "https://a.example/"),
            font("rId1", "https://other.example/")
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            PartFs::open(&conflict),
            Err(OpcError::InvalidRelationship)
        ));
```

#### Validation

Independently verified Attacker package/part .rels -\> read_relationships preserves records -\> PartFs::open_within -\> drop_repeated_relationships -\> repeated repaired.contains string scans. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently traced metadata reader222-246, open_within520-546 and repair99-126. Identical duplicates are explicitly accepted/repaired, while conflicting targets are refused. Attribute/depth and ZIP entry-count budgets do not bound relationship-element count within an admitted part. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read complete drop_repeated_relationships (opc/mod.rs:99-125), open_within repair calls (524-540), and metadata record parsing.100000 distinct IDs each duplicated identically cause~5billion String comparisons; records fit a64MiB part and do not consume additional ZIP entries. Conflicting duplicate rejection does not apply to identical pairs. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Metadata parsing preserves duplicate IDs (`rels.items = items`), and identical duplicates are intentionally repaired rather than rejected. A large shallow .rels fits XML depth/tag/byte caps and uses only one ZIP entry; max_entries limits ZIP members, not relationship records. No record-count bound precedes the vector scan. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): `read_relationships` parses records individually and retains duplicates. `open_within` repairs package and part relationships. Conflicting duplicates refuse, but identical copies enter the linear repaired.contains check. N=100000 distinct repeated IDs imply N(N-1)/2 comparisons. Per-tag attribute and ZIP entry limits do not bound records inside one .rels part.

Validation method: Preserved already-validated Standard evidence and attack paths; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only, without code inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis

- **Status:** validated

```rust
            font("rId1", "https://a.example/"),
            font("rId2", "https://b.example/"),
            font("rId1", "https://a.example/")
        ));
        let fs = PartFs::open(&same).unwrap();
        let rels = fs.read_rels_for("word/document.xml").unwrap();
        let ids: Vec<&str> = rels.items.iter().map(|r| r.id.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(ids, ["rId1", "rId2"]);
        assert_eq!(
            fs.repaired_duplicate_ids(),
            [("word/document.xml".to_string(), "rId1".to_string())]
        );
        let conflict = package_with_document_rels(&format!(
            "{}{}",
            font("rId1", "https://a.example/"),
            font("rId1", "https://other.example/")
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            PartFs::open(&conflict),
            Err(OpcError::InvalidRelationship)
        ));
```

### [11] Redacting a numeric identifier can leave its custom XML attribute intact

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent review confirms local-name-only filtering, numeric/hex classifier and byte-preserving auxiliary output before the final leak check. |
| Category | Overbroad sensitive-data scan exemption |
| CWE | CWE-201, CWE-200 |
| Affected lines | src/scrub.rs:543-552, src/scrub.rs:484-490, src/scrub.rs:522-525, src/edit.rs:4727-4745, src/edit/prepared.rs:873, src/scrub.rs:543-550, src/edit.rs:4727-4745, src/edit/prepared.rs:873, src/opc/mod.rs:368-376 |

#### Summary

The final redaction leak scan exempts numeric-looking attributes by local name alone. A sensitive value such as a customer or account identifier in custom XML `id` is ignored, allowing visible redaction to succeed while the value remains recoverable in the returned DOCX.

#### Root Cause

`check_redactions()` refuses outputs only when `scrub::leaks()` finds the target. For XML attributes, `xml_holds()` ignores a matching value if its local name appears in `NUMERIC_ATTRIBUTES` and its value is hexadecimal-looking. The exemption checks neither namespace nor owning element/part. Thus business XML `<customer id="123456789"/>`, including a business-namespaced `id`, is treated like an OOXML layout identifier. Ordinary body redaction leaves that auxiliary part unchanged and the final scan reports no residual target.


#### Reachability

Public redaction preparation invokes this scan without extra flags; an arbitrary custom XML duplicate whose local name matches the exemption is sufficient.

- **Attacker:** Recipient of redacted output; document supplier can arrange the duplicate

- **Entry point:** Public Redact operation

- **Outcome:** Sensitive identifier disclosure

Preconditions:
- Target identifier is duplicated in a numeric-looking custom XML attribute with exempt local name.
- Output is shared.

#### Severity

**Medium** — The confidentiality operation can certify an output still containing the exact sensitive identifier. A business-data duplicate and subsequent sharing are required; there is no asserted automatic network transmission or arbitrary file access.

Routine exposure of highly sensitive identifiers in shared redacted documents would increase impact; independent complete sanitization or withholding output prevents disclosure.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** A confidentiality check certifies a file containing sensitive business data.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Requires a specified duplicate representation and sharing workflow.

#### Remediation

Remove numeric exemptions from strict redaction verification, or restrict them to verified OOXML namespace/element/attribute combinations representing exclusively generated layout state. Always scan arbitrary custom XML business attributes.

Tests:
- Redact visible numeric targets duplicated in unqualified and business-namespaced custom XML id attributes; assert REDACTION_LEAK.
- Retain explicit tests for legitimate OOXML layout exemptions only if their exact namespace and element contexts are enforced.
- Redact an account identifier also held by customXml metadata/@id and assert refusal.
- Keep regression coverage for legitimate qualified OOXML numeric layout attributes and scan the same local names in unrelated namespaces.

#### Summary

An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission.

#### Root Cause

cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene. The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic. Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span. Assigned discovery-0017 additionally traces leading/trailing grid_skip_cell placeholders and stretch_stale_spans, which leaves oversized rows unchanged; gridSpan=2147483647 requests about 8 GiB for f32 columns. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: The renderer parses attacker-authored table span attributes into `usize` and preserves them in raw cells, including synthetic cells for omitted columns. `table_block` sums the spans and allocates a column vector of that size; `resolve_table_merges` then allocates merge tracking to the same extent. XML byte, depth and attribute budgets do not restrict these numeric values. For example, a one-cell span of 1000000000 requests roughly 4 GB for columns alone despite requiring only ten digits in XML.

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
```

**Stale span repair does not reduce oversized spans** — `src/convert/mod.rs:14168-14201`

Oversized authored spans skip this repair when `used >= cols.len()`; it does not clamp them.

```rust
/// brings its width closer to the tcW: Word reads the row by its cell
/// widths and the saved grid as a cache (25f1d311bd). A row whose cells
/// fit their columns (within `STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT`) is a short row and
/// stays one.
fn stretch_stale_spans(rows: &mut [Vec<RawCell>], cols: &[f32]) {
    const STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT: f32 = 20.0;
    for row in rows.iter_mut() {
        let used: usize = row.iter().map(|c| c.colspan.max(1)).sum();
        if used >= cols.len() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut spare = cols.len() - used;
        let mut col = 0usize;
        for cell in row.iter_mut() {
            let span = cell.colspan.max(1);
            if let PrefWidth::Dxa(want) = cell.pref {
                let mut covered: f32 = cols.iter().skip(col).take(span).sum();
                let mut extra = 0usize;
                while extra < spare
                    && want - covered > STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT
                    && let Some(&next) = cols.get(col + span + extra)
                    && (covered + next - want).abs() < (want - covered).abs()
                {
                    covered += next;
                    extra += 1;
                }
                if extra > 0 {
                    cell.colspan = span + extra;
                    spare -= extra;
                }
            }
            col += cell.colspan.max(1);
        }
    }
```

```
fn cell_span(dom: &Dom, cell: NodeId) -> (usize, VMerge) {
    let Some(pr) = first_named(dom, cell, "tcPr") else {
        return (1, VMerge::None);
    };
    // Direct child only. first_named walks into tcPrChange (addition_removal
    // remnant: live colspan=1, change gridSpan=2) and pads three 80pt
    // columns so the live last cell wraps at ~50pt.
    let colspan = direct_named(dom, pr, "gridSpan")
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "val"))
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .max(1);
```
```rust
    let vmerge = match direct_named(dom, pr, "vMerge") {
        None => VMerge::None,
        Some(n) => match dom.attribute(n, &W::val()) {
            Some("restart") | Some("Restart") => VMerge::Restart,
            _ => VMerge::Continue,
        },
    };
    (colspan, vmerge)
}
```

Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value. The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path. Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -\> with_layout -\> body table_block -\> cell_span/row_grid_skip -\> RawCell.colspan -\> occupancy -\> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): The public rendering path admits and opens the document before table parsing. A positive 2147483647 fits usize on supported 32/64-bit targets. It is retained as `colspan`; the stale-span repair skips oversized rows. Occupancy reaches `vec![each; occupancy]` or `resize` without a maximum. Both row-skip fields independently feed the same sum via grid_skip_cell. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Validated public conversion -\> admitted layout -\> `cell_span`/`row_grid_skip` -\> raw cell occupancy -\> `Vec` expansion. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows whose used count exceeds existing columns and does not clamp hostile spans. Admission does not inspect grid span semantics. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 passes the shown integer parse on supported 32/64-bit sizes. stretch_stale_spans leaves already-large spans unchanged. occupancy selects that value and a Vec\<f32\> requests about 16 GiB (or refuses/aborts on platform capacity); rendering fails before any useful output.

```rust
    docx: &[u8],

    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;

        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
```
```rust
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
```

```rust
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

**Render imports a related HTML chunk after admission** — `src/convert/mod.rs:769-798`

Untrusted DOCX bytes are admitted, then the related chunk bytes are passed to `altchunk::expand` before DOM construction.

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
```

```rust
        Some(n) => match dom.attribute(n, &W::val()) {
            Some("restart") | Some("Restart") => VMerge::Restart,
```

**Stale span repair does not reduce oversized spans** — `src/convert/mod.rs:14168-14201`

Oversized authored spans skip this repair when `used >= cols.len()`; it does not clamp them.

```rust
/// brings its width closer to the tcW: Word reads the row by its cell
/// widths and the saved grid as a cache (25f1d311bd). A row whose cells
/// fit their columns (within `STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT`) is a short row and
/// stays one.
fn stretch_stale_spans(rows: &mut [Vec<RawCell>], cols: &[f32]) {
    const STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT: f32 = 20.0;
    for row in rows.iter_mut() {
        let used: usize = row.iter().map(|c| c.colspan.max(1)).sum();
        if used >= cols.len() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut spare = cols.len() - used;
        let mut col = 0usize;
        for cell in row.iter_mut() {
            let span = cell.colspan.max(1);
            if let PrefWidth::Dxa(want) = cell.pref {
                let mut covered: f32 = cols.iter().skip(col).take(span).sum();
                let mut extra = 0usize;
                while extra < spare
                    && want - covered > STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT
                    && let Some(&next) = cols.get(col + span + extra)
                    && (covered + next - want).abs() < (want - covered).abs()
                {
                    covered += next;
                    extra += 1;
                }
                if extra > 0 {
                    cell.colspan = span + extra;
                    spare -= extra;
                }
            }
            col += cell.colspan.max(1);
        }
    }
```

```rust
fn cell_span(dom: &Dom, cell: NodeId) -> (usize, VMerge) {
    let Some(pr) = first_named(dom, cell, "tcPr") else {
        return (1, VMerge::None);

    // Direct child only. first_named walks into tcPrChange (addition_removal
    // remnant: live colspan=1, change gridSpan=2) and pads three 80pt
    // columns so the live last cell wraps at ~50pt.
    let colspan = direct_named(dom, pr, "gridSpan")
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "val"))
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .max(1);
    let vmerge = match direct_named(dom, pr, "vMerge") {
        None => VMerge::None,
        Some(n) => match dom.attribute(n, &W::val()) {
            Some("restart") | Some("Restart") => VMerge::Restart,
            _ => VMerge::Continue,
        },
    };
    (colspan, vmerge)
}
```

#### Reachability

Attacker controls only DOCX table XML; a victim processes it with the public renderer. No special option, filesystem privilege, local account or privileged configuration is required. Public convert::docx_to_pdf/render/docx_to_png/docx_render_report accept DOCX bytes and reach with_layout/table_block; no nondefault option or external relationship is needed. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: The public in-process renderer accepts document bytes and uses this table parser after admission, which checks structure rather than numeric table semantics. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Public rendering calls with_layout, which admits then parses table input and enters table_block.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author Untrusted document supplier Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: untrusted document producer Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): DOCX supplier

- **Entry point:** convert::docx_to_pdf / render / docx_to_png and shared PDF/PNG/render-report binding/CLI callers Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: convert::docx_to_pdf, docx_to_png, docx_render_report Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): convert rendering APIs and their CLI/Python/WASM/MCP adapters

- **Outcome:** loss of availability of the rendering process Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Process memory exhaustion or WASM allocation trap

Preconditions:
- Victim renders the supplied DOCX.
- Victim renders a document containing the attacker-controlled table.
- Victim processes the supplied DOCX through layout; attacker needs no host filesystem/configuration access.
- Victim renders the supplied DOCX; ordinary package structure and table XML required.

Existing controls:
- Original archive and XML admission apply; caller may impose process memory/CPU limits.

Limitations:
- No data disclosure or code execution established; remote service exposure is deployment-dependent.

#### Severity

**Medium** — An untrusted document can deterministically drive huge allocations through a public parser boundary. This compromises availability of the rendering process; shared-service exposure is conditional and process memory limits constrain the blast radius.

Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): high
- **Rationale:** Memory exhaustion or process termination; no code execution or data access is established.
- **Why:** An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Availability of the CLI or embedding process; no confidentiality/integrity compromise established. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Process memory exhaustion or WASM allocation trap

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): medium
- **Rationale:** Direct integer-to-allocation path reachable with a tiny document.
- **Why:** The numeric input is document-controlled and reaches the sink with default conversion. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: A short decimal attribute directly controls allocation on an ordinary supported conversion path. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Victim must process attacker input through the cited public interface.

#### Remediation

Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess. Propagate a caller-adjustable semantic column limit through all public rendering surfaces and charge later column/merge vectors to that same budget.

Tests:
- Check that a tiny table with an enormous gridSpan is refused before allocation.
- Cover gridBefore/gridAfter, accumulated spans, and overflow boundaries.
- Reject huge positive gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before allocation.
- Reject checked aggregate row overflow and total table-grid budget overflow; valid small tables must preserve layout.
- Excessive individual and cumulative spans/skips must refuse with bounded work.
- Cover count overflow and 32-bit WASM.
- Keep valid merged/skipped-column rendering.
- Test excessive individual spans, row offsets and cumulative spans using tiny in-memory documents; assert typed refusal before allocation.
- Test numeric overflow and valid boundary tables.
- Integration-test huge cell spans and row skips through public rendering APIs and assert bounded typed refusal, including aggregate overflow.
- Keep representative valid merged tables rendering correctly within the budget.
- Tiny tables with very large gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter must fail with a resource-limit error before vector allocation.
- Test cumulative spans exceeding the limit and arithmetic overflow; retain supported ordinary merged tables.
- Reject huge gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter in otherwise small admitted DOCX files.
- Cover aggregate span overflow and normal merged cells without large allocation.
- Reject oversized gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter through public rendering APIs.
- Verify cumulative occupancy and integer-overflow refusal on native and wasm32.
- Preserve valid merged-cell and row-skip layouts.
- Use a tiny admitted table with a very large positive gridSpan; assert a typed refusal before column or merge-state allocation.
- Small table with huge gridSpan is refused before dense allocation.
- Equivalent gridBefore and gridAfter inputs are refused.
- Cumulative spans near overflow are refused using checked addition.
- Normal merged tables remain supported at the documented inclusive limit.
- Convert a minimal admitted DOCX with a huge gridSpan and assert a typed resource refusal before allocating.
- Cover huge gridBefore/gridAfter and multiple individually valid spans whose sum exceeds the grid budget.
- Refuse excessive cell spans and skipped-grid columns through each rendering binding.
- Check cumulative spans and integer-overflow boundaries before allocation.

Preventive controls:
- Bound derived dimensions and generated output independently from archive/XML input byte limits.
- Use one semantic table-column policy for authored and synthesized cells.
- Use shared semantic allocation budgets for document-controlled counts in every layout path.

#### Summary

Package admission ignores opaque DTD and top-level CDATA events, while the permissive DOM handles top-level \<! constructs by skipping only to the first '\>'. A delimiter within a quoted entity or CDATA body exposes deeply nested literal markup as recursive elements, bypassing admission depth and potentially exhausting the host stack. Rendering and lazy WmlDocument main-part access are preserved affected entrypoints. An internal-subset comment with a literal \> supplies an additional hidden-tag framing at the same declaration boundary. The assigned corroboration additionally identifies get_revisions main-document parsing after ordinary admission.

#### Root Cause

`check_xml_depth()` counts Start/Empty events and ignores DocType. The streaming reader correctly consumes the complete internal subset, including quoted element-like text. `parse_document()` instead skips any declaration only to the first closing angle bracket, even inside that literal, then treats the remaining literal markup as actual elements. Its recursive element parser has no independent depth guard. The checked XML API's explicit DTD rejection is absent from package admission. WmlDocument::from_bytes admits/stores parts and main_document later parses the same main bytes unchecked. A single quoted internal entity value with nested literal tags is sufficient; the earlier two-entity illustration is not a prerequisite. The package gate and permissive DOM disagree on lexical boundaries of DTD/top-level CDATA. Admission ignores opaque tokens while the DOM's first-\> skip reinterprets their remaining bytes as recursively nested markup. The additional legal internal-subset-comment framing uses a literal \> before nested-looking tags, exposing comment content through the same first-delimiter skip; it needs no entity expansion. The rendering corroboration also retains quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST internal-subset handling in quick-xml 0.42 (parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205; reader/state.rs:163-173). A Transitional main part without altChunk or strict namespace rewriting remains unchanged before unchecked with_layout parsing; main-part existence/content-type checks are not declaration safety checks. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration: get_revisions (src/document_comparer.rs:6299-6308) shares the admitted-main unchecked DOM route. Checked inspect/edit parse_part_within rejects DTDs and is excluded from this specific declaration path.

```rust
fn check_xml_depth(name: &str, xml: &[u8], limits: InputLimits) -> Result<(), AdmissionError> {
    let invalid =
        |why: String| AdmissionError::new(AdmissionErrorKind::InvalidXml, format!("{name}: {why}"));
    let text = part_text(xml);
    let mut reader = Reader::from_str(&text);
    reader.config_mut().check_end_names = true;
    let max_depth = limits.max_xml_depth;
    let mut policy = crate::xmllinq::parse::TagPolicy::tolerant(limits);
    let mut depth = 0usize;
    loop {
        match reader.read_event() {
            Ok(Event::Start(tag)) => {
                policy.open(&tag).map_err(invalid)?;
                depth = depth.saturating_add(1);
                if depth > max_depth {
                    return Err(invalid(format!("XML nests deeper than {max_depth}")));
                }
            }
            Ok(Event::Empty(tag)) => {
                policy.empty(&tag).map_err(invalid)?;
            }
            Ok(Event::End(_)) => {
                depth = depth
                    .checked_sub(1)
                    .ok_or_else(|| invalid("end tag with no open element".to_string()))?;
                policy.close();
            }
            Ok(Event::Eof) if depth > 0 => {
                return Err(invalid(format!("{depth} element(s) left unclosed")));
            }
            Ok(Event::Eof) => return Ok(()),
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(e) => return Err(invalid(e.to_string())),
        }
```

A valid internal entity declaration can contain a long literal with nested tag text without using the entity. quick-xml0.42 consumes the entire declaration as DocType (cached src/parser/dtd.rs:28-59,194-200,262-265), so package depth remains shallow. The DOM skip ends at the literal's first tag terminator and immediately enters recursion over the remaining literal. Normal rendering parses before it can reject the phantom root. This is independent of non-XML filenames. Verified current quick-xml 0.42.0 parser/dtd.rs:28-30,124-135,194-199 preserves quoted entity values while scanning the internal subset, and reader/state.rs:163-173 emits the entire declaration as DocType. Admission ignores that event. The raw parser uses its first-'\>' search regardless of quotation and resumes element parsing, so sufficiently deep literal tags can exceed the admitted depth. Parent verified admission event match, DOM top-level skip and recursion plus WmlDocument admission/lazy parse. Current direct dependency quick-xml0.42.0 (Cargo.toml) treats quoted ENTITY content as one DTD and emits one DocType; local parser/dtd.rs:194-202,262-265 and reader/state.rs:163-174 confirm it. A quoted literal containing many opening/closing tags can remain below physical byte budgets but exceed DOM stack depth. Top-level CDATA is a sibling opaque-token path. Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified DOCX main part with internal-subset comment -\> admission quick-xml DocType ignored -\> WmlDocument::main_document -\> parse_document first-\> skip -\> hidden \<a\> strings -\> recursive parse_element. Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Verified admission.rs:798-821 has no DocType refusal, parse.rs:539-547 stops at the first delimiter, and parse.rs:660-663 recurses. Installed quick-xml 0.42 source parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205 and reader/state.rs:163-173 show that quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST content is returned within one DocType event. Main-part metadata checks inspect existence/content type rather than XML declaration safety. with_layout then parses the unchanged Transitional main XML. Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read admission's event match, installed quick-xml0.42 quote-sensitive DTD state, WmlDocument constructor/main parse, and DOM declaration/recursive branches. A quoted replacement beginning with \> then nested markup is not counted as elements by admission but is consumed by DOM recursion. Checked raw-XML validation rejects DTDs and is not the affected entry. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified unreferenced quoted DTD content is excluded from admission's depth events but can be treated as recursive markup by the DOM. The package path invokes admission yet never calls the checked DTD-rejecting validator before these consumers. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Pinned quick-xml 0.42 DtdParser uses quote-sensitive parsing for ENTITY declarations. Thus nested markup inside a quoted replacement value remains one DocType event during admission. The local skipper stops inside that value, then calls recursive parse_element on its contents before semantic root rejection. Source trace verifies WmlDocument and get_revisions reach this path. Supplied discovery-0030 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Verified check_xml_depth's event match, parse_document's declaration skip and recursive parse_element. WmlDocument::from_bytes admits the package at lines50-58, then main_document lines85-96 parses the same XML unchecked. An unused internal entity can legally contain literal nested markup; no entity expansion or external resolution is required.

Validation method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

```rust
fn check_xml_depth(name: &str, xml: &[u8], limits: InputLimits) -> Result<(), AdmissionError> {
    let invalid =
        |why: String| AdmissionError::new(AdmissionErrorKind::InvalidXml, format!("{name}: {why}"));
    let text = part_text(xml);
    let mut reader = Reader::from_str(&text);
    reader.config_mut().check_end_names = true;
    let max_depth = limits.max_xml_depth;
    let mut policy = crate::xmllinq::parse::TagPolicy::tolerant(limits);
    let mut depth = 0usize;
    loop {
        match reader.read_event() {
            Ok(Event::Start(tag)) => {
                policy.open(&tag).map_err(invalid)?;
                depth = depth.saturating_add(1);
                if depth > max_depth {
                    return Err(invalid(format!("XML nests deeper than {max_depth}")));
                }
            }
            Ok(Event::Empty(tag)) => {
                policy.empty(&tag).map_err(invalid)?;
            }
            Ok(Event::End(_)) => {
                depth = depth
                    .checked_sub(1)
                    .ok_or_else(|| invalid("end tag with no open element".to_string()))?;
                policy.close();
            }
            Ok(Event::Eof) if depth > 0 => {
                return Err(invalid(format!("{depth} element(s) left unclosed")));
            }
            Ok(Event::Eof) => return Ok(()),
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(e) => return Err(invalid(e.to_string())),
```

#### Reachability

Public rendering admits caller bytes with check_xml_depth and later calls permissive parse_xdocument on the same main XML. A `.bin` alias or operator setting is unnecessary. WmlDocument::from_bytes also admits the main XML and main_document later uses the permissive parser. The public byte-oriented WmlDocument API is a sufficient boundary; the document supplier requires no environment control or raised input budgets. Public WmlDocument::from_bytes followed by main_document/main_document_root suffices. It admits the package then directly parses its main XML; no elevated limits or external service deployment needed. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): The public constructor and revision API admit the archive but then use the permissive parser without checked DTD rejection.

- **Outcome:** Native stack exhaustion or WASM trap Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Stack exhaustion and process termination

Preconditions:

- Victim invokes the affected public API with attacker-controlled document input.

Existing controls:

- Process isolation contains broader application consequences.

#### Severity

Rejecting DTD declarations at package admission and enforcing parser depth makes the representations agree. Isolated workers reduce shared-host impact.

#### Remediation

Align admission and DOM lexical/structural semantics for every opaque \<! construct. Reject unsupported DTD and CDATA/text outside the root consistently with checked XML validation, and enforce active depth during DOM construction or use the checked API before every untrusted consumer. If opaque constructs are supported, consume their complete grammar rather than the first '\>'. A DTD-only refusal does not fix the top-level CDATA subcase; retain valid in-root CDATA. Include get_revisions main-document parsing in the mandatory lexical/depth boundary while preserving existing checked-consumer distinctions.

#### Summary

The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its XML leak branch uses lossy UTF-8 and misses the retained copy, which a recipient can recover after sharing. Even the scanner's no-root fallback searches the already lossily decoded string, so it cannot recover a multi-character value split by UTF-16 NUL bytes.

#### Root Cause

Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes. The standalone leaks API and both prepared artifacts use this same branch; ordinary Transitional input does not require Strict normalization to rewrite the untouched auxiliary part. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `check_redactions()` relies on `scrub::leaks()` to detect retained text in both output packages. The scanner chooses its XML branch by suffix and lossy-decodes as UTF-8; its UTF-16LE raw-byte search runs only for non-XML. BOM-prefixed UTF-16 XML is accepted by admission but its NUL-separated characters evade the scan. The no-root fallback returns xml.contains(needle) after incompatible decoding rather than searching the original bytes; non-XML UTF-16LE test coverage exercises a different branch.

```rust
fn part_text(xml: &[u8]) -> Cow<'_, str> {
    let utf16 = |rest: &[u8], unit: fn([u8; 2]) -> u16| {
        let units = rest.as_chunks::<2>().0.iter().map(|&pair| unit(pair));

    };

        _ => String::from_utf8_lossy(xml),
```
```rust
    }
```

An ordinary multi-character secret in BOM UTF16LE/BE customXml survives raw package storage and serialization. UTF8-lossy decoding produces replacement/NUL-interleaved text; xml_holds either has no root and uses a UTF8 substring check or cannot match decoded ordinary text. Both final artifacts are checked with that same routine. Existing malformed-XML validation findings are baseline, not automatically introduced failures. Additional validated trace follows public edit preparation into both serialized artifacts, unchanged auxiliary bytes and xml_holds fallback. Ordinary Transitional main XML avoids normalization rewriting the auxiliary UTF-16 copy. Both LE/BE supported encodings and the standalone leaks API share the missing XML decoding control. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected admission.rs764-792 BOM decoding, strict_translation.rs769-837 zero-change/raw preservation, PartFs raw insertion, edit.rs5381-5424 untouched-part serialization and final scanner. An ASCII secret duplicated inside a valid BOM UTF16LE/BE customXml XML text node remains extractable in clean output while UTF8-lossy XML scanning cannot match it. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified admission's UTF-16LE/BE decoding and existing customXml admission test, output serialization preserving untouched parts, and both check_redactions call sites in prepared::produce. A body redaction can succeed while a same-text UTF-16 customXml/item1.xml remains recoverable. Source baseline validation reports do not automatically block unchanged source findings. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): BOM UTF16LE/BE XML is supported by admission. In a normal .xml entry, ASCII needle characters are separated by NUL bytes and cannot match in lossy UTF8. xml_holds cannot recover the XML and its fallback still misses the contiguous needle. strict translation's zero-churn path preserves such data, and PartFs::to_zip writes untouched parts unchanged. Custom XML is outside the edited story, so a copied secret can remain while visible text is redacted and check_redactions returns success.

Validation method: Preserved already-validated Standard source evidence and assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

```rust
/// A part's text for scanning. Word writes UTF-8, but a part may be UTF-16
/// with a byte-order mark (SharePoint's `customXml` items often are) and
/// Word opens it, so it is transcoded; other bytes decode lossily, as the
/// rest of the engine reads them.
fn part_text(xml: &[u8]) -> Cow<'_, str> {
    let utf16 = |rest: &[u8], unit: fn([u8; 2]) -> u16| {
        let units = rest.as_chunks::<2>().0.iter().map(|&pair| unit(pair));
        Cow::Owned(
            char::decode_utf16(units)
                .map(|c| c.unwrap_or(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER))
                .collect(),
        )
    };
    match xml {
        [0xFF, 0xFE, rest @ ..] => utf16(rest, u16::from_le_bytes),
        [0xFE, 0xFF, rest @ ..] => utf16(rest, u16::from_be_bytes),
        _ => String::from_utf8_lossy(xml),
```
```rust
    }
```

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Unreadable archives/entries and inflation-budget failures correctly refuse redaction.
- UTF8 XML entities and Word text split across runs are handled.
- UTF16 raw matching exists for non-XML parts only.
- Normal redaction outcome diagnostics avoid repeating the secret.
- Archive read/inflation failures fail closed and UTF-8 XML comments, processing instructions/entities and joined Word runs are scanned.
- Neither those controls nor the non-XML UTF-16LE fallback covers UTF-16 XML.
- A simple transitional package does not need strict translation that could rewrite auxiliary XML.
- Scanner iterates every ZIP entry and fails closed on archive/read/name/budget errors.
- UTF8 XML text/comments/PI/ordinary textual attributes and split Word runs are scanned.
- Numeric OOXML layout attributes have intentional false-positive exemptions; arbitrary custom data has no such structural guarantee.
- UTF-8 XML and UTF-16LE binary parts are searched; neither path handles supported UTF-16 XML. Untouched custom XML remains serialized.
- Actual inflated streams remain bounded and read failures fail closed.
- The checker handles raw UTF16LE in non-XML files, but that branch is not used for .xml.
- No plaintext copy is required outside the encoded XML.
- UTF8 XML entities/comments/split runs are searched.
- Non-XML UTF16LE bytes are searched; existing utf16.bin tests exercise that different branch.
- A redaction with any detected residual value fails REDACTION_LEAK; this encoding produces a false negative.

Limitations:
- No product-generated trigger or runtime redaction test executed.
- Disclosure requires the resulting package to be shared or inspected by another party.
- Static source validation only; disclosure additionally requires sharing the returned document with a recipient.
- No application/test execution or constructed package.
- Finding establishes clean-output preservation; it does not require every comparer path to preserve all auxiliary data identically.
- No application execution or vulnerability-triggering runtime tests were performed.
- No document generated or redaction executed; validation is source-only.
- No crafted input or edit runtime test executed.
- This finding establishes encoded auxiliary-copy leakage,not every possible redaction mechanism.

#### Dataflow

Supported UTF16 auxiliary XML -\> unchanged PartFs bytes -\> UTF8-lossy leak scan misses copy -\> redaction success -\> raw secret-bearing part serialized

- **Source:** Document-supplied duplicate confidential text

- **Sink:** Redaction leak certification and outgoing ZIP parts

- **Outcome:** Recipient can recover the supposedly removed text.

```rust
                parts.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
            );
            let mut error = self.conflict(op, &message);
```

#### Reachability

Public redact plan checks both clean/redline artifacts with scrub::leaks. No control of victim environment or edit plan is needed beyond the victim choosing which visible secret to redact.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document supplier or outgoing document recipient

- **Entry point:** Redact plan operation and scrub::leaks

Preconditions:
- Input contains duplicate text in BOM UTF16 auxiliary XML.
- User redacts visible text and distributes the output.

#### Severity

**Medium** — An outgoing document can disclose text the user explicitly asked to remove. A supplier can place a duplicate in supported customXml and the user performs ordinary redaction; successful checking makes the confidentiality failure likely when that document is shared.

Impact depends on sensitivity and subsequent sharing. Consistent BOM-aware decoding and fail-closed scanning remove the bypass.

#### Remediation

Decode every XML part with the same BOM-aware policy as admission before semantic leak scanning. Fail closed on unsupported/undecodable/unparseable representations and retain raw UTF8 and both UTF16 byte-order checks as defense in depth. Use the same decoding across leak checks and package validation.

Tests:
- Redact visible body text while UTF16LE and UTF16BE customXml retains the same text; require REDACTION_LEAK.
- Cover XML entities, split runs and encoding errors.
- A document with no remaining copy must still redact successfully.
- Redact a visible target while matching UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE custom XML remains; assert REDACTION_LEAK.
- Verify the standalone leaks API reports encoded auxiliary copies and unsupported encodings fail closed.
- Keep UTF-8 comments, processing instructions, entities and split-run matching; malformed/unsupported XML encodings must refuse rather than certify a partial scan.
- Redact body text duplicated in UTF16LE and UTF16BE customXml XML and assert REDACTION_LEAK.
- Assert successful outputs have no decoded copy across all supported XML encodings.
- End-to-end redact refuses retained same-text UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE custom XML copies in both clean/redline.
- Retain coverage for UTF-8 entities, split runs, attributes, comments and binary UTF-16.
- Redact visible text while UTF16LE/BE custom XML copies remain; require REDACTION_LEAK.
- Verify direct leaks reports both encoded XML variants.
- Preserve ordinary split-run and decoded-entity detection.
- Verify leaks finds multi-character text in BOM UTF16LE/BE .xml and .rels members.
- Verify redact refuses when an untouched UTF16 XML part retains the removed value and succeeds only after every copy is removed.
- Check that UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE XML text, attributes and comments are reported as leaks.
- Assert a redaction plan refuses when a UTF-16 customXml part retains the redacted value.
- Redact a visible value duplicated in UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE XML text/attributes; require REDACTION_LEAK.
- Verify both clean and redline output checks preserve the fail-closed invariant.

Preventive controls:
- Use the same accepted encoding rules at admission and security postcondition checks.

### [15] Rendering nested HTML tables bypasses the XML depth limit

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Independent static inspection connects input controls, transformations and unchecked allocation/iteration/recursion. Exact runtime failure thresholds were not measured. |
| Category | Uncontrolled resource consumption |
| CWE | CWE-674 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/altchunk.rs:543-550, src/convert/altchunk.rs:495-509, src/convert/mod.rs:789-799, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:660-663, src/convert/mod.rs:789-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:558-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:495-517 |

#### Summary

HTML table expansion runs after package admission and can generate arbitrarily deep WordprocessingML, which is passed to the unchecked recursive DOM parser. The supplied corroboration preserves the innermost-paragraph prerequisite for retaining nested cell WML and confirms that huge colspan is unnecessary; exact abort depth is platform-dependent.

#### Root Cause

Opaque HTML part bytes pass admission. The importer permits nested tables/cells and emits their nested WML after original XML checks. `with_layout()` invokes infallible `parse_xdocument()` on expanded output without rechecking active depth limits. An innermost paragraph makes the contains('\<w:p\>') guard retain inner table markup through each containing cell; generated nesting therefore survives to recursive parsing independently of numeric-span amplification.

### [16] Unbounded tab-leader positions create attacker-sized repeated strings

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Independent investigator and parent source traces establish attacker input, propagation, missing numeric bound and allocation sink. Exact runtime failure threshold is unmeasured. |
| Category | Memory allocation with excessive size value |
| CWE | CWE-789 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/mod.rs:772-791, src/convert/mod.rs:3243-3264, src/convert/mod.rs:3152-3170, src/convert/mod.rs:24141-24153, src/convert/mod.rs:26524-26539, src/convert/mod.rs:26442-26470, src/convert/mod.rs:26394-26402, src/convert/mod.rs:3243-3265, src/convert/mod.rs:24141-24152, src/convert/mod.rs:26464-26469, src/convert/mod.rs:26394-26401 |

#### Summary

A very large left tab stop with a dot, hyphen or underscore leader makes document rendering allocate and shape a huge repeated string, even when the stop lies far outside the page.

#### Root Cause

parse_tab_stops accepts arbitrary f32 pos values. The compatibility landing correction clamps only Right-aligned stops in mode\>=15, leaving Left stops unchanged. advance_tab computes the authored destination, and paint_tab_leader casts its geometric mark count to usize and calls repeat before painting can clip output. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `parse_tab_stops()` retains an arbitrarily large floating position. Layout preserves left stops, and a lone explicit tab survives wrapping. `advance_tab()` passes its distant endpoint to `paint_tab_leader()`, which casts the calculated count to usize and repeats a marker.

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Package admission does not bound numeric layout values. Right-stop compatibility clamping does not protect Left leaders. The eventual text clipping occurs after the allocation.
- Host process resource limits can contain failure but do not bound the allocation request.
- Admission bounds source ZIP/XML size, nesting and entries, and the policy recommends host process limits. These do not bound this generated work.
- Modern right-aligned tab clamping does not cover the left-aligned trigger; raster pixel limits are downstream.

Limitations:
- No application code, generated input or runtime reproduction was executed.
- No application execution or vulnerability-triggering runtime test was performed.

```rust
fn next_tab_stop(x: f32, origin: f32, stops: &[TabStop], default_tab: f32) -> TabStop {
    for &stop in stops {
        // `bar` is a drawn rule, not a destination (ECMA-376 17.3.1.38).
        if stop.align == TabAlign::Bar {
            continue;
        }
        let abs = origin + stop.pos;
        if abs > x + 0.01 {
            return TabStop {
                pos: abs,
                align: stop.align,
                leader: stop.leader,
                numbering: stop.numbering,
            };
```

#### Reachability

A caller supplying untrusted DOCX paragraph tab stops and a tab character. Victim must process the supplied file; no special option or privileged account is required.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author

- **Entry point:** Public document render/PDF/PNG APIs and shared callers

Limitations:
- No data disclosure or code execution established; remote service exposure is deployment-dependent.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A small untrusted document can reliably cause disproportionate processing memory use. Impact is availability of the worker or embedding process; no deployed public service is assumed.

Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** A tiny paragraph with a large left tab position and dot/hyphen/underscore leader causes a huge repeated string and subsequent shaping allocations. Sufficiently large finite values also produce capacity-overflow panics.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** The numeric input is document-controlled and reaches the sink with default conversion.

#### Remediation

Reject nonfinite coordinates and cap tab destinations or generated leader glyphs to the visible line/page extent before constructing strings.

Tests:
- Bound huge finite and nonfinite Left/Center/Decimal/Right tab positions before repeated string construction.
- Exercise dot, hyphen and underscore leaders across compatibility modes and small font widths.
- Huge finite, nonfinite and negative tab positions return a typed refusal or bounded rendering.
- Exercise left/center/decimal and legacy right tabs; downstream raster limits must not be the first guard.

Preventive controls:
- Bound derived dimensions and generated output independently from archive/XML input byte limits.

<a id="finding-17"></a>

### [17] Comparing large tables can allocate a quadratic matrix

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Independent static source trace establishes the missing control and input-to-sink path. No runtime exploit or deployment observation is claimed. |
| Category | Uncontrolled resource consumption |
| CWE | CWE-789 |
| Affected lines | src/comparer/lcs.rs:4080-4087, src/comparer/lcs_table.rs:638-642, src/comparer/lcs_table.rs:51-65, src/comparer/lcs_table.rs:147-159 |

#### Summary

Table alignment allocates an unchecked (old_rows+1) by (new_rows+1) usize matrix. A few-megabyte pair of 20,000-row tables can request about 3.2 GB before output.

#### Root Cause

`do_lcs_algorithm_for_table()` sends eligible unmerged table pairs to shared-word alignment. That path and content-based row LCS allocate full nested usize matrices from row counts without checking their product against a memory/work budget.

**Single-table pairs enter table alignment** — `src/comparer/lcs.rs:4080-4087`

A sole-table residual pair reaches the table-specific algorithm.

```rust
    // H3 — single table vs single table → DoLcsAlgorithmForTable (M4.D).
    if left_tables == 1
        && left_len == 1
        && right_tables == 1
        && right_len == 1
        && let Some(r) = super::lcs_table::do_lcs_algorithm_for_table(dom, cul1, cul2, settings)
    {
        return r;
```

**Word mode selects shared-word alignment** — `src/comparer/lcs_table.rs:638-642`

Default Word behavior tries this route before other table fallbacks.

```rust
    if settings.merge_replaced_paragraphs
        && let Some(rows) = shared_word_row_sequences(dom, rows1, rows2)
    {
        return Some(rows);
    }
```

**Content row LCS has the same unchecked product** — `src/comparer/lcs_table.rs:51-65`

The other row LCS independently materializes all cells without a product budget.

```rust
pub fn apply_lcs_to_table_rows(
    rows1: &[ComparisonUnit],
    rows2: &[ComparisonUnit],
) -> Vec<CorrelatedSequence> {
    let m = rows1.len();
    let n = rows2.len();
    let mut lcs = vec![vec![0usize; n + 1]; m + 1];
    for i in 1..=m {
        for j in 1..=n {
            lcs[i][j] = if rows1[i - 1].sha1() == rows2[j - 1].sha1() {
                lcs[i - 1][j - 1] + 1
            } else {
                lcs[i - 1][j].max(lcs[i][j - 1])
            };
        }
```

**Row counts directly allocate all DP cells** — `src/comparer/lcs_table.rs:147-159`

Both dimensions derive from supplied document rows, with no work/memory cap.

```rust
pub(crate) fn align_rows_by_shared_words(
    old: &[std::collections::HashSet<String>],
    new: &[std::collections::HashSet<String>],
) -> Vec<WordRowOp> {
    let (m, n) = (old.len(), new.len());
    let score = |i: usize, j: usize| old[i].intersection(&new[j]).count();
    let mut best = vec![vec![0usize; n + 1]; m + 1];
    for i in 1..=m {
        for j in 1..=n {
            best[i][j] = best[i - 1][j]
                .max(best[i][j - 1])
                .max(best[i - 1][j - 1] + score(i - 1, j - 1));
        }
```

Verified single-table dispatch, Word-mode gate and eligibility: nonempty unmerged tables, no identical row hashes and nonempty tokens. Repeated 'alpha old' vs 'alpha new' rows satisfy them. A 20001² matrix contains 400,040,001 cells (~3.2 GB on 64-bit) in addition to document state. Earlier identical-row eligibility checks also scan the row product.

Validation method: independent static source trace

```rust
            best[i][j] = best[i - 1][j]
                .max(best[i][j - 1])
                .max(best[i - 1][j - 1] + score(i - 1, j - 1));
```


#### Reachability

Public Rust/Python/WASM document comparison, with default Word-mode shared-word alignment.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document supplier

- **Entry point:** Public Rust/Python/WASM document comparison, with default Word-mode shared-word alignment.

- **Outcome:** Processing host loses availability

Preconditions:
- Victim invokes the affected public API on the supplied input.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Source-supported attacker input crosses a resource or confidentiality boundary with concrete process-availability or retained-sensitive-content impact. Exploitation does not need raised limits or privileged configuration.

Per-job resource isolation limits availability impact; for disclosure, risk depends on the sensitivity of retained text and distribution of output documents.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Availability of the processing host.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Direct source path lacks the relevant resource/encoding gate.

#### Remediation

Check row products against a comparison work/memory budget before all nested scans/allocations and use bounded-memory alignment or a typed refusal for excessive work.

Tests:
- Large unmerged changed tables refuse or use bounded-memory alignment before matrix allocation.
- Apply the same budget to shared-word and content row LCS.

### [18] Ragged legacy DOC tables expand into an unbounded padded rectangle

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Independent static trace establishes attacker-controlled legacy text/table structure and disproportionate conversion work. No runtime benchmark was performed. |
| Category | Allocation without resource limits |
| CWE | CWE-770, CWE-409 |
| Affected lines | src/legacy_doc.rs:511-525, src/legacy_doc.rs:225-236, src/legacy_doc.rs:512-525, src/legacy_doc.rs:1436-1443, src/legacy_doc.rs:1625-1645, src/legacy_doc.rs:1625-1643, src/legacy_doc.rs:1707-1719, src/legacy_doc.rs:511-526, src/legacy_doc.rs:225-236, src/legacy_doc.rs:225-249, src/legacy_doc.rs:1623-1648, src/legacy_doc.rs:430-460, src/legacy_doc.rs:511-527, src/legacy_doc.rs:511-528, src/legacy_doc.rs:1625-1643, src/legacy_doc.rs:180-194 |

#### Summary

A table with one wide row and many narrow rows contains relatively few cells, but legacy Markdown serialization emits the widest row's cell count for every row. Compact input can therefore generate gigabytes of output and exhaust importer memory. The same unbounded serialization is independently exposed through public to_markdown(LegacyDocument), in addition to DOC byte conversions. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a static 100000-cell row plus 100000 short/empty rows framing: about ten billion serialized cells before DOCX admission. No numeric colspan forgery or logical-piece alias is required.

#### Root Cause

Story::blocks and flush_table preserve per-row cell counts from DOC table marks/properties. push_block then chooses maximum row length and pads every row to it without checking width times row count or generated bytes. A table with O(N) physical cells becomes O(N squared) serialized cells before DOCX admission. Assigned discovery-0016 explicitly traces PAPX row_end operands and cell markers into arbitrary-width rows. Both doc_to_markdown and doc_to_docx use the same unbudgeted Markdown rectangle; O(W+R) source markers/properties emit O(W\*R) cells. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a static 100000-cell row plus 100000 short/empty rows framing: about ten billion serialized cells before DOCX admission. No numeric colspan forgery or logical-piece alias is required.

```
fn flush_table(out: &mut Vec<Block>, rows: &mut Vec<(Vec<String>, bool)>, row: &mut Vec<String>) {
    if !row.is_empty() {
        rows.push((std::mem::take(row), false));
    }
    if !rows.is_empty() {
        let rows = std::mem::take(rows);
        // Only leading rows repeat: a header mark after a data row is
        // ignored ([MS-DOC] 2.6.3 sprmTTableHeader).
        let header_rows = rows.iter().take_while(|(_, header)| *header).count();
        out.push(Block::Table(Table {
            rows: rows.into_iter().map(|(cells, _)| cells).collect(),
            header_rows,
        }));
```

```rust
pub fn to_markdown(document: &LegacyDocument) -> String {
    blocks_to_markdown(document, None)

/// The blocks as Markdown; an empty paragraph is left out, or with
/// `empty`, written as that text (for the `.docx` writer to take out).
fn blocks_to_markdown(document: &LegacyDocument, empty: Option<&str>) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    for block in &document.blocks {
        if let Block::Paragraph(paragraph) = block
            && paragraph.text().trim().is_empty()
        {
            let Some(placeholder) = empty else {
                continue;
            };
            // One placeholder a line, so the paragraph's line breaks
            // survive as `w:br` runs between them.
            let lines = vec![placeholder; placeholder_lines(paragraph)];
            let placeholder = Paragraph {
                spans: vec![Span {
                    text: lines.join("\n"),
                    ..Span::default()
                }],
                ..paragraph.clone()
            };
            push_block(&mut out, &Block::Paragraph(placeholder));
            continue;
        }
        push_block(&mut out, block);
    }
    out
```

- Physical CFB streams and numeric offsets remain bounded; they do not bound this generated work.
- Ordinary short inputs are unaffected.
- CLI timeout is opt-in and public APIs have no built-in deadline.
- Physical text/property reads are bounded.

- Downstream Markdown behavior and runtime resource threshold were not exercised.

- Logical-piece expansion, giant DOCX gridSpan and field nesting are unnecessary and have different controls.
- Padding shorter rows is intentional and tested.
- Physical parser and per-cell bounds do not constrain the product of row count and maximum width.
- No numeric colspan forgery or piece alias is required; this is an independent legacy table sink.
