Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB. Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text. Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.

Evidence:
- Local public legacy parser, FIB/PCD decode and logical-story consumer inspected.

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Checked arithmetic and word.get/u16_at refuse physical offsets outside WordDocument. Increasing CP validation prevents backwards logical pieces. Neither control bounds repeated physical-range references or total logical expansion. Public legacy APIs have no InputLimits parameter, and CLI parsing happens before resulting DOCX admission.
- Compound-file parsing and character addressing use bounds/overflow checks.
- main_text rejects decreasing logical CPs, gaps and physical out-of-bounds reads; the repeated in-range aliases satisfy these checks.
- No malformed auxiliary table is needed because expansion runs first.
- Sector chains are bounded and repeated FAT locations rejected; integer arithmetic and physical byte reads are checked.
- Decreasing CPs and gaps are refused, so the rejected repeated 0..N logical-range proposal is not needed. This construction uses increasing contiguous CPs.
- The repository recommends host process limits, which constrain damage but do not provide a bounded parser refusal.
- Compound-file sector walks and numeric offsets use checked/bounded arithmetic; these bound physical reads, not logical reuse.
- Main-story CP coverage must be continuous and increasing; the described pieces satisfy that condition.
- Process memory/CPU limits are recommended by SECURITY.md and can contain the host impact.
- CFB sector-chain iteration is bounded by file size and invalid CP coverage is rejected.
- No deployment exposure or measured allocation size is assumed; the exact StoryChar layout is platform dependent.
- CFB sectors/chains, table slicing and physical offsets have checked bounds.
- Decreasing or noncovering CP intervals are refused; the attack uses contiguous increasing ranges.
- An invalid FC fails on physical read; repeated valid FC spans remain accepted.
- No current Python/WASM legacy export is asserted by this finding.
- Physical-input/bounds checks and host process limits do not bound this derived output or per-character work.

Limitations:
- No input constructed, code executed, network contacted or exact runtime threshold measured.
- No dynamic reproduction or deployment-specific impact was measured.
- No application execution, exploit fixture or memory threshold measurement; no deployment exposure assumed.
- No generated DOC or application execution; exact peak allocation and abort behavior were not measured.
- Static-only validation; no runtime measurement or deployed embedding assessment.
- No legacy file was generated or imported; exact host memory failure was not measured.
- No application execution, crafted-input execution, stress test or deployment observation.

#### Reachability

A caller supplying an untrusted legacy DOC piece table. Victim must process the supplied file; no privileged configuration is needed. legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown and doc_to_docx are public byte APIs. CLI convert also dispatches legacy input; no privileged configuration is required.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author Supplier of untrusted input processed by a library consumer

- **Entry point:** legacy_doc::read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI conversion

Preconditions:
- Victim invokes the affected public API with attacker-controlled document input.

Existing controls:
- Physical stream bounds remain enforced; they do not bound logical expansion.

Limitations:
- Memory-safe reads remain bounded; no arbitrary code execution or confidentiality impact is established.

#### Severity

**Medium** — An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** The triggering structure and values are document-controlled and not rejected by existing guards.

#### Remediation

Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget.

Tests:
- Aliased physical text pieces exceeding a small logical-character budget must refuse before StoryChar allocation.
- Preserve legitimate shared/fast-save pieces within the configured budget; cover maximum ccp_text and cumulative metadata budgets.
- Use small repeated physical aliases with a deliberately small decoded budget; assert typed refusal before expanding beyond it.
- Retain valid aliases, split UTF-16 surrogate handling and continuity/error cases.
- Use a small physical text stream with many increasing CP ranges sharing FC backing; assert a budget error before materialization.
- Retain tests accepting legitimate short FC aliases and refusing decreasing CPs, gaps and out-of-range physical references.
- A compact valid compound file with repeated FC pieces and excessive logical CP coverage must be refused before expansion.
- Boundary-sized permitted stories and legitimate reused text pieces should import successfully.
- CLI conversion must apply the same logical expansion budget as direct library calls.
- A valid piece table with increasing CPs but many references to one short physical range must return a resource-limit error before allocating proportional to its claimed story.
- Preserve legitimate repeated/fast-save pieces within the configured decoded-text limit.
- Reject compact piece tables whose repeated physical spans exceed the logical-character/work budget.
- Preserve legitimate fast-saved pieces and reject excessive logical stories before allocation.
- Repeated physical ranges cannot exceed the logical-character/decoded-output budget.
- Valid fast-save piece reuse remains supported within bounds.

Preventive controls:
- Budget logical processing work and representation expansion, and bind preflight validation to the actual consumer's selected input.

### [31] Document font names trigger quadratic persistent index rewrites

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent traced all-family resolution, missing-family recording and whole-index rewrite; practical runtime threshold was not measured. |
| Category | Algorithmic Complexity |
| CWE | CWE-407 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/font.rs:3427-3432, src/convert/font.rs:3236-3248, src/convert/font.rs:3205-3229, src/convert/font.rs:3098-3107 |

#### Summary

Many distinct unknown font names in a DOCX cause the native renderer to record each miss and rewrite the entire growing font index separately. A document supplier can force quadratic CPU/disk work and grow persistent state across conversions without controlling host configuration.

#### Root Cause

Document-controlled font-family misses are persisted one at a time with an unbounded whole-index read/merge/sort/write, without batching, eviction or aggregate work/state limits.

**Every font-table family triggers resolution** — `src/convert/font.rs:3427-3432`

Every font-table family triggers resolution; misses remain distinct and each save reads/merges/formats all prior entries.

fn indexed_faces(
    index: &Mutex<FontIndex>,
    key: &str,
    scan: impl FnOnce() -> (SourcedFaces, Vec<PathBuf>),
) -> Vec<((bool, bool), Vec<u8>)> {
    let entry = index.lock().ok().and_then(|i| i.entries.get(key).cloned());
    if let Some(faces) = entry.and_then(|e| e.load()) {
        return faces;
    }
    let (faces, dirs) = scan();
    if let Ok(mut index) = index.lock() {
        index.record(key, &dirs, &faces);
    }
```

/// `$JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX` (empty or `off` disables it), else
/// `font-index.tsv` beside jubarte's font folder.
fn font_index_path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    match std::env::var_os("JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX") {
        Some(path) if path.is_empty() || path == "off" => None,
        Some(path) => Some(PathBuf::from(path)),
        None => user_font_dir()?
            .parent()
            .map(|dir| dir.join("font-index.tsv")),
    }
```

#### Validation

Parent independently verified font_table rows are eagerly visited (3427-3432), cached_faces stores distinct misses (3042-3055), installed_family_faces uses a family-specific key (2258-2275), indexed_faces records even empty results (3236-3247), and record/save rewrites all accumulated entries (3192-3227). Format sorts the whole index at 3264-3311.

Validation method: offline static source review

- **Status:** validated

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Exact repeated names hit cache; attack requires fresh distinct noncatalogue names.
- Empty/off JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX disables persistence, and an unwritable location prevents successful disk growth.
- Input XML byte limits bound one document but not quadratic work over its distinct names or persistent cross-document cache size.
- No arbitrary host path control or filesystem disclosure is asserted.

Limitations:
- No timing, disk-volume or memory measurements, and actual deployment/index permissions unknown.

#### Dataflow

DOCX font table -\> each unknown family -\> cached_faces/installed_family_faces -\> indexed_faces miss -\> FontIndex::record -\> save parses/merges/sorts/rewrites whole growing index -\> quadratic aggregate I/O/CPU and persistent growth.

#### Reachability

Default native render setup calls add_installed_faces for every font-table entry, including unused families. The font index defaults beside the platform user font directory and is created when possible.

- **Attacker:** Supplier of documents rendered by a native process

- **Entry point:** src/convert/mod.rs:857

- **Sink:** src/convert/font.rs:3213-3227

Preconditions:
- Victim renders supplied DOCX via native font resolution.
- Enabled writable native index for persistent disk effects; distinct missing names avoid cache hits.

#### Severity

**Medium** — High worker availability impact from repeated growing-index work, with medium deployment-dependent likelihood; writable default native persistence is required for disk growth.

Disable persistence with JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX=off or isolate per-document quotas to reduce impact; exposed long-lived native renderers with writable shared index face higher risk.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Worker availability degradation from aggregate quadratic CPU/I/O; persistent state makes later loads larger.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Default native path is proven, but service exposure and disk permissions are unspecified.

#### Remediation

Batch font-index persistence once per conversion, bound/evict recorded unknown names and total index size, limit family-resolution work, and avoid rescanning/reformatting the entire index for each miss.

Tests:
- With an in-memory fake index backend, verify many unique misses cause bounded writes per conversion and enforce family/index-size limits; retain intentional miss caching semantics.

#### Summary

An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates the existing one-billion-column, 4,000,000,000-byte f32-vector framing through both span and row-skip inputs; these are static counts. Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates the live span and both synthetic row-skip paths, including merge-slot expansion; separate Markdown span clamping does not protect rendering.

#### Root Cause

cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene. The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic. Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span. Assigned discovery-0017 additionally traces leading/trailing grid_skip_cell placeholders and stretch_stale_spans, which leaves oversized rows unchanged; gridSpan=2147483647 requests about 8 GiB for f32 columns. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: The renderer parses attacker-authored table span attributes into `usize` and preserves them in raw cells, including synthetic cells for omitted columns. `table_block` sums the spans and allocates a column vector of that size; `resolve_table_merges` then allocates merge tracking to the same extent. XML byte, depth and attribute budgets do not restrict these numeric values. For example, a one-cell span of 1000000000 requests roughly 4 GB for columns alone despite requiring only ten digits in XML. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates the existing one-billion-column, 4,000,000,000-byte f32-vector framing through both span and row-skip inputs; these are static counts. Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): `cell_span()` accepts a live positive `usize` span, and `row_grid_skip()` independently creates synthetic cells from positive skipped-column values. `table_block()` retains those values, computes maximum row occupancy with an unchecked sum, then constructs or resizes a column vector to that size. `resolve_table_merges()` independently expands a tracking vector to `col + span`. No maximum table-column or layout allocation budget gates these operations.

    let pr = direct_named(dom, row, "trPr")?;
    let span = direct_named(dom, pr, &format!("grid{side}"))
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "val"))
        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<usize>().ok())

        .and_then(parse_len)
        .filter(|w| *w > 0.0)

    Some((span, pref))
}

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);

**Stale span repair does not reduce oversized spans** — `src/convert/mod.rs:14168-14201`

Oversized authored spans skip this repair when `used >= cols.len()`; it does not clamp them.

```rust
/// brings its width closer to the tcW: Word reads the row by its cell
/// widths and the saved grid as a cache (25f1d311bd). A row whose cells
/// fit their columns (within `STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT`) is a short row and
/// stays one.
fn stretch_stale_spans(rows: &mut [Vec<RawCell>], cols: &[f32]) {
    const STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT: f32 = 20.0;
    for row in rows.iter_mut() {
        let used: usize = row.iter().map(|c| c.colspan.max(1)).sum();
        if used >= cols.len() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut spare = cols.len() - used;
        let mut col = 0usize;
        for cell in row.iter_mut() {
            let span = cell.colspan.max(1);
            if let PrefWidth::Dxa(want) = cell.pref {
                let mut covered: f32 = cols.iter().skip(col).take(span).sum();
                let mut extra = 0usize;
                while extra < spare
                    && want - covered > STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT
                    && let Some(&next) = cols.get(col + span + extra)
                    && (covered + next - want).abs() < (want - covered).abs()
                {
                    covered += next;
                    extra += 1;
                }
                if extra > 0 {
                    cell.colspan = span + extra;
                    spare -= extra;
                }
            }
            col += cell.colspan.max(1);
        }
    }
```

fn cell_span(dom: &Dom, cell: NodeId) -> (usize, VMerge) {
    let Some(pr) = first_named(dom, cell, "tcPr") else {
        return (1, VMerge::None);
    };
    // Direct child only. first_named walks into tcPrChange (addition_removal
    // remnant: live colspan=1, change gridSpan=2) and pads three 80pt
    // columns so the live last cell wraps at ~50pt.
    let colspan = direct_named(dom, pr, "gridSpan")
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "val"))
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .max(1);
    let vmerge = match direct_named(dom, pr, "vMerge") {
        None => VMerge::None,
        Some(n) => match dom.attribute(n, &W::val()) {
            Some("restart") | Some("Restart") => VMerge::Restart,
            _ => VMerge::Continue,
        },
    };
    (colspan, vmerge)
}

/// A row's `w:gridBefore`/`w:gridAfter` (`side` "Before"/"After"): the

fn row_grid_skip(dom: &Dom, row: NodeId, side: &str) -> Option<(usize, PrefWidth)> {
    let pr = direct_named(dom, row, "trPr")?;
    let span = direct_named(dom, pr, &format!("grid{side}"))
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "val"))
        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<usize>().ok())
        .filter(|n| *n > 0)?;

        .filter(|n| attr_any(dom, *n, "type").is_none_or(|t| t == "dxa"))
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "w"))
        .and_then(parse_len)
        .filter(|w| *w > 0.0)
        .map_or(PrefWidth::Auto, PrefWidth::Dxa);
    Some((span, pref))
}

#### Validation

Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value. The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path. Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -\> with_layout -\> body table_block -\> cell_span/row_grid_skip -\> RawCell.colspan -\> occupancy -\> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): The public rendering path admits and opens the document before table parsing. A positive 2147483647 fits usize on supported 32/64-bit targets. It is retained as `colspan`; the stale-span repair skips oversized rows. Occupancy reaches `vec![each; occupancy]` or `resize` without a maximum. Both row-skip fields independently feed the same sum via grid_skip_cell. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Validated public conversion -\> admitted layout -\> `cell_span`/`row_grid_skip` -\> raw cell occupancy -\> `Vec` expansion. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows whose used count exceeds existing columns and does not clamp hostile spans. Admission does not inspect grid span semantics. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 passes the shown integer parse on supported 32/64-bit sizes. stretch_stale_spans leaves already-large spans unchanged. occupancy selects that value and a Vec\<f32\> requests about 16 GiB (or refuses/aborts on platform capacity); rendering fails before any useful output. Supplied discovery-0030 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Verified with_layout admission followed by table_block, cell_span, RawCell storage at 13530-13536, occupancy and vector growth. A one-cell table with one grid column avoids arithmetic overflow and reaches the giant allocation directly. Also verified row-skip siblings and merge-state sink. **Shared renderer admits and then lays out the document** — `src/convert/mod.rs:769-799`

Admission enforces package/XML budgets; no layout semantic bound is introduced before DOM use.

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

**Stale span repair does not reduce oversized spans** — `src/convert/mod.rs:14168-14201`

Oversized authored spans skip this repair when `used >= cols.len()`; it does not clamp them.

```rust
/// brings its width closer to the tcW: Word reads the row by its cell
/// widths and the saved grid as a cache (25f1d311bd). A row whose cells
/// fit their columns (within `STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT`) is a short row and
/// stays one.
fn stretch_stale_spans(rows: &mut [Vec<RawCell>], cols: &[f32]) {
    const STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT: f32 = 20.0;
    for row in rows.iter_mut() {
        let used: usize = row.iter().map(|c| c.colspan.max(1)).sum();
        if used >= cols.len() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut spare = cols.len() - used;
        let mut col = 0usize;
        for cell in row.iter_mut() {
            let span = cell.colspan.max(1);
            if let PrefWidth::Dxa(want) = cell.pref {
                let mut covered: f32 = cols.iter().skip(col).take(span).sum();
                let mut extra = 0usize;
                while extra < spare
                    && want - covered > STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT
                    && let Some(&next) = cols.get(col + span + extra)
                    && (covered + next - want).abs() < (want - covered).abs()
                {
                    covered += next;
                    extra += 1;
                }
                if extra > 0 {
                    cell.colspan = span + extra;
                    spare -= extra;
                }
            }
            col += cell.colspan.max(1);
        }
    }
```

Assertions:
- A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits a tiny shallow XML part yet requests a 4,000,000,000-byte f32 column vector.
- gridBefore and gridAfter synthesize RawCells with the same unchecked span, and merge tracking adds another span-sized allocation.

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- ZIP, inflated bytes and XML nesting are bounded before layout.
- The security policy recommends process CPU/memory limits; these limit damage to a worker but do not reject the document.
- with_layout performs package admission at lines 773-774. Its compressed, inflated-byte, entry, XML-depth, and attribute budgets do not constrain the numeric value or derived grid occupancy. This path requires no altChunk. gridBefore/gridAfter share the same broken table-allocation control.
- Host process resource limits can contain failure but do not bound the allocation request.
- ZIP/XML syntax and byte budgets remain effective.
- PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS applies after layout; PDF and render reports also lay out tables.
- Caller process limits contain the worker but do not bound this tiny-input allocation.
- with_layout admits original packages using comparison InputLimits, which bound bytes, entries, depth and tag policy.
- Checked arithmetic on other parser offsets does not constrain table occupancy.

fn row_grid_skip(dom: &Dom, row: NodeId, side: &str) -> Option<(usize, PrefWidth)> {
    let pr = direct_named(dom, row, "trPr")?;
    let span = direct_named(dom, pr, &format!("grid{side}"))
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "val"))
        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<usize>().ok())
        .filter(|n| *n > 0)?;
    let pref = direct_named(dom, pr, &format!("w{side}"))
        .filter(|n| attr_any(dom, *n, "type").is_none_or(|t| t == "dxa"))
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "w"))
        .and_then(parse_len)
        .filter(|w| *w > 0.0)
        .map_or(PrefWidth::Auto, PrefWidth::Dxa);
    Some((span, pref))
}
```

**Unbounded cell span** — `src/convert/mod.rs:14204-14224`

`w:gridSpan/@w:val` is parsed as `usize` with only a lower bound; the untrusted value becomes `RawCell.colspan`.

```rust
fn cell_span(dom: &Dom, cell: NodeId) -> (usize, VMerge) {
    let Some(pr) = first_named(dom, cell, "tcPr") else {
        return (1, VMerge::None);
    };
    // Direct child only. first_named walks into tcPrChange (addition_removal
    // remnant: live colspan=1, change gridSpan=2) and pads three 80pt
    // columns so the live last cell wraps at ~50pt.
    let colspan = direct_named(dom, pr, "gridSpan")
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "val"))
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .max(1);
    let vmerge = match direct_named(dom, pr, "vMerge") {
        None => VMerge::None,
        Some(n) => match dom.attribute(n, &W::val()) {
            Some("restart") | Some("Restart") => VMerge::Restart,
            _ => VMerge::Continue,
        },
    };
    (colspan, vmerge)
}
```

fn row_grid_skip(dom: &Dom, row: NodeId, side: &str) -> Option<(usize, PrefWidth)> {
    let pr = direct_named(dom, row, "trPr")?;
    let span = direct_named(dom, pr, &format!("grid{side}"))
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "val"))
        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<usize>().ok())
        .filter(|n| *n > 0)?;
    let pref = direct_named(dom, pr, &format!("w{side}"))
        .filter(|n| attr_any(dom, *n, "type").is_none_or(|t| t == "dxa"))
        .and_then(|n| attr_any(dom, n, "w"))
        .and_then(parse_len)
        .filter(|w| *w > 0.0)
        .map_or(PrefWidth::Auto, PrefWidth::Dxa);
    Some((span, pref))
}

#### Reachability

Attacker controls only DOCX table XML; a victim processes it with the public renderer. No special option, filesystem privilege, local account or privileged configuration is required. Public convert::docx_to_pdf/render/docx_to_png/docx_render_report accept DOCX bytes and reach with_layout/table_block; no nondefault option or external relationship is needed. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: The public in-process renderer accepts document bytes and uses this table parser after admission, which checks structure rather than numeric table semantics. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Public rendering calls with_layout, which admits then parses table input and enters table_block.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author Untrusted document supplier Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: untrusted document producer Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): DOCX supplier

- **Entry point:** convert::docx_to_pdf / render / docx_to_png and shared PDF/PNG/render-report binding/CLI callers Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: convert::docx_to_pdf, docx_to_png, docx_render_report Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): convert rendering APIs and their CLI/Python/WASM/MCP adapters

- **Outcome:** loss of availability of the rendering process Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Process memory exhaustion or WASM allocation trap

Preconditions:
- Victim renders the supplied DOCX.
- Victim renders a document containing the attacker-controlled table.
- Victim processes the supplied DOCX through layout; attacker needs no host filesystem/configuration access.
- Victim renders the supplied DOCX; ordinary package structure and table XML required.

Existing controls:
- Original archive and XML admission apply; caller may impose process memory/CPU limits.

Limitations:
- No data disclosure or code execution established; remote service exposure is deployment-dependent.

#### Severity

**Medium** — An untrusted document can deterministically drive huge allocations through a public parser boundary. This compromises availability of the rendering process; shared-service exposure is conditional and process memory limits constrain the blast radius.

Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): high
- **Rationale:** Memory exhaustion or process termination; no code execution or data access is established.
- **Why:** An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Availability of the CLI or embedding process; no confidentiality/integrity compromise established. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Process memory exhaustion or WASM allocation trap

Likelihood assessment:

#### Remediation

Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess. Propagate a caller-adjustable semantic column limit through all public rendering surfaces and charge later column/merge vectors to that same budget. Additional retained remediation detail: Enforce explicit maximum live cell spans, row skips, aggregate table columns and merge slots before any allocation. Use checked sums and a cumulative layout resource budget, returning a typed refusal when exceeded.

- Test cumulative spans exceeding the limit and arithmetic overflow; retain supported ordinary merged tables.

- Cover aggregate span overflow and normal merged cells without large allocation.
- Reject oversized gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter through public rendering APIs.
- Verify cumulative occupancy and integer-overflow refusal on native and wasm32.
- Preserve valid merged-cell and row-skip layouts.
- Use a tiny admitted table with a very large positive gridSpan; assert a typed refusal before column or merge-state allocation.
- Small table with huge gridSpan is refused before dense allocation.
- Equivalent gridBefore and gridAfter inputs are refused.

- Convert a minimal admitted DOCX with a huge gridSpan and assert a typed resource refusal before allocating.

- Refuse excessive cell spans and skipped-grid columns through each rendering binding.

Preventive controls:

#### Summary

An untrusted DOCX can select Chicago numbering with a huge list start/startOverride or section page start. The shared chicago_label formatter repeats a UTF-8 symbol roughly n/4 times without a length bound, allowing gigabyte allocations during list rendering, ordinary section-page processing and Markdown numbered-list views. Authored endnote starts also reach this shared formatter. The supplied u32::MAX framing selects 1073741824 double-daggers, about 3 GiB of UTF-8 label bytes; this is static arithmetic. Additional supplied static framing: start=2147483647 selects 536870912 UTF-8 double-daggers (‡), requesting 1.5 GiB of marker bytes before downstream copies. Assigned discovery-0032 additionally supplies start=4294967294: 1073741824 daggers (†), about 3 GiB of UTF-8 before copies. Level-zero reader/agent labels reach the shared formatter without a large ilvl.

#### Root Cause

List starts/startOverrides and section pgNumType starts retain full u32 values. Numbering::next_marker uses the authored first counter and substitutes format_num output; section_page_label independently dispatches its page counter through format_num. Chicago calls chicago_label, which computes i=n.saturating_sub(1) and MARKS\[i%4\].repeat(i/4+1) without a bound. Markdown list-label generation uses the same shared formatter. Counter saturation prevents overflow but retains enormous values; ordinary paragraph processing evaluates chapter/page labels even before an empty bookmarks loop. A level-zero list suffices independently of excessive ilvl iteration; bounding level indices alone does not bound Chicago label length. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): Numbering levels accept an uncapped u32 start and the counter renderer passes it to format_num. The Chicago formatter repeats its selected symbol n/4 times without a label-length budget. Page numbering and the DOCX-to-Markdown list view call the same formatter, so the same missing control affects distinct consumers. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Numbering start/startOverride values enter u32 counters with only max(1). `Numbering::render()` calls `format_num()`, whose Chicago branch repeats one marker `(n-1)/4+1` times without an output budget. Endnote numStart/format also reaches the same shared formatter through number_endnote_refs; its generated-label budget must cover that route as well as list, page and agent/MCP read-view consumers. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: A shared formatter converts a bounded-width but numerically huge input into output proportional to its magnitude, without checking the resulting label length before String::repeat. Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Both numbering parsers accept a u32 start without a label-output budget. The renderer's counter/startOverride path calls `format_num()` during token replacement, and Markdown/agent `list_marker()` calls the same formatter through `list_number()`. `chicago_label()` computes `(n - 1) / 4 + 1` repetitions and allocates them with `String::repeat()`. Section page-number starts reuse that helper. Limiting ilvl to nine levels in the reader does not limit the chosen counter or label length.

/// The last letter label Word writes, thirty z's.
pub(crate) const ALPHA_LABEL_MAX: u32 = 26 * 30;
/// The last Roman numeral Word writes.
pub(crate) const ROMAN_LABEL_MAX: u32 = 32767;

/// `lowerLetter` / `upperLetter` and `\* alphabetic`: past z Word repeats
/// the letter, 27 "aa", 28 "bb", 53 "aaa" (Word 16 probes la1006 and
/// nf1006, 2026-10-06). Past thirty z's (780) a list label starts again
/// at "a" (probe bn1006b). Zero counts as 1.
pub(crate) fn alpha_label(n: u32, upper: bool) -> String {
    let n = (n.max(1) - 1) % ALPHA_LABEL_MAX;
    let ch = char::from(b'a' + (n % 26) as u8);
    let ch = if upper { ch.to_ascii_uppercase() } else { ch };
    std::iter::repeat_n(ch, (n / 26) as usize + 1).collect()
}

**MCP read tool exposes agent view** — `jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-144`

An MCP docx_text request reads a root-confined document and calls native read_view, whose output formatting reaches the reader.

```python
    @mcp.tool(annotations=_READ)
    def docx_text(path: str) -> str:
        """The agent view `jubarte read` prints: a header (sha256, counts, page
        setup), then Markdown with a <!-- pN --> id line before each paragraph
        and every revision (r12) and comment (c5) with its id.

        Those ids are the coordinates an edit plan uses (`p12` as written).
        Read before you edit. Warnings follow the view, one per line.
        """
        from . import _native

        doc = load(path)
        markdown, warnings = engine(lambda: _native.read_view(doc.to_bytes(), source=Path(path).name))
        return markdown + "".join(f"warning: {w}\n" for w in warnings)
```

fn number_endnote_refs(blocks: &mut [Block], (fmt, start): (NumFmt, u32)) {
    let mut labels: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
    visit_runs_mut(blocks, |run| {
        let Some(id) = run.endnote_id.as_deref().filter(|id| !id.is_empty()) else {
            return;
        };
        let next = start + labels.len() as u32;
        let label = labels
            .entry(id.to_string())
            .or_insert_with(|| format_num(fmt, next));
        run.text.clone_from(label);
```

```rust

/// The last letter label Word writes, thirty z's.
pub(crate) const ALPHA_LABEL_MAX: u32 = 26 * 30;
/// The last Roman numeral Word writes.
pub(crate) const ROMAN_LABEL_MAX: u32 = 32767;

/// `lowerLetter` / `upperLetter` and `\* alphabetic`: past z Word repeats
/// the letter, 27 "aa", 28 "bb", 53 "aaa" (Word 16 probes la1006 and
/// nf1006, 2026-10-06). Past thirty z's (780) a list label starts again
/// at "a" (probe bn1006b). Zero counts as 1.
pub(crate) fn alpha_label(n: u32, upper: bool) -> String {
    let n = (n.max(1) - 1) % ALPHA_LABEL_MAX;
    let ch = char::from(b'a' + (n % 26) as u8);
    let ch = if upper { ch.to_ascii_uppercase() } else { ch };
    std::iter::repeat_n(ch, (n / 26) as usize + 1).collect()
}

/// again at "I", 100000 "MDCXCIX" (Word 16 probe bn1006b, 2026-10-06).
pub(crate) fn roman_label(n: u32, upper: bool) -> String {
    if n == 0 {
        return "0".into();
    }
    let mut n = (n - 1) % ROMAN_LABEL_MAX + 1;
    const MAP: &[(u32, &str)] = &[

**MCP read tool exposes agent view** — `jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-144`

An MCP docx_text request reads a root-confined document and calls native read_view, whose output formatting reaches the reader.

```python
    @mcp.tool(annotations=_READ)
    def docx_text(path: str) -> str:
        """The agent view `jubarte read` prints: a header (sha256, counts, page
        setup), then Markdown with a <!-- pN --> id line before each paragraph
        and every revision (r12) and comment (c5) with its id.

        Those ids are the coordinates an edit plan uses (`p12` as written).
        Read before you edit. Warnings follow the view, one per line.
        """
        from . import _native

        doc = load(path)
        markdown, warnings = engine(lambda: _native.read_view(doc.to_bytes(), source=Path(path).name))
        return markdown + "".join(f"warning: {w}\n" for w in warnings)
```

fn number_endnote_refs(blocks: &mut [Block], (fmt, start): (NumFmt, u32)) {
    let mut labels: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
    visit_runs_mut(blocks, |run| {
        let Some(id) = run.endnote_id.as_deref().filter(|id| !id.is_empty()) else {
            return;
        };
        let next = start + labels.len() as u32;
        let label = labels
            .entry(id.to_string())
            .or_insert_with(|| format_num(fmt, next));
        run.text.clone_from(label);
```

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Other alphabetic and Roman formats have explicit wrapping maxima, but Chicago has no corresponding bound (convert/mod.rs:6492-6520).
- Admission constrains input bytes and depth; it does not constrain generated label length.
- Counter saturation prevents integer overflow but preserves enormous values.
- Admission restricts input bytes and XML structure, not the expanded label. Sibling alphabetic and Roman formatters explicitly cycle at ALPHA_LABEL_MAX and ROMAN_LABEL_MAX (lines 6491-6514); Chicago lacks an equivalent bound.
- Host process resource limits can contain failure but do not bound the allocation request.
- Alphabetic labels wrap at ALPHA_LABEL_MAX=780 and Roman labels at 32767; those related claims are rejected.
- The attack uses level zero, so it does not require the separate high-ilvl issue.
- Archive/input bounds do not bound generated marker length.
- Other numbering formats use bounded representations or wrapping; that does not constrain Chicago's String::repeat.
- A process/WASM memory ceiling may terminate or reject the allocation but does not produce the expected typed input refusal.
- Saturating counter increments prevent arithmetic wrap but do not cap marker size.
- The attack works at normal level zero, so enforcing the supported level range does not fix it.
- Input byte/depth/attribute limits do not cap the magnitude of the small numeric start.
- An agent-view counter uses the shared formatter and likewise needs the output-length bound.
- Admission bounds source ZIP/XML size, nesting and entries, and the policy recommends host process limits. These do not bound this generated work.
- The Markdown reader clamps nesting to eight but does not cap the counter's start magnitude.
- Other formats have bounded Roman/alphabetic policies; Chicago's constructor lacks them.
- Archive and XML budgets constrain the tiny source representation, not its label expansion.
- Host CPU/memory limits can contain worker failure.
- Input ZIP/XML budgets apply but do not bound numeric label size.
- Markdown clamps ilvl to eight, which prevents its level-index issue but does not cap list starts or Chicago output.
- Other numbering formats use bounded/logarithmic output; this claim is specific to Chicago.
- Requires document-controlled Chicago format and a token naming the current level; both are accepted source fields.
- Other formats can remain bounded; correctly small starts produce short labels.
- Package byte/depth/tag budgets limit source data rather than semantic output size; caller process limits contain blast radius.
- Other alphabetic/Roman formatters reduce counter ranges; Chicago does not.
- Markdown clamps depth but forwards the large counter into list_number.
- Input size and XML depth budgets allow the ten-digit start value.
- Alphabetic/Roman formatters have bounded cycling but Chicago does not.
- The reader clamps ilvl to eight, which does not cap numeric start.
- The document must select Chicago and a displayed label or page-number consumer; ordinary decimal formatting remains bounded.
- Host memory limits can contain termination but cannot make the operation succeed safely.

/// The last letter label Word writes, thirty z's.
pub(crate) const ALPHA_LABEL_MAX: u32 = 26 * 30;
/// The last Roman numeral Word writes.
pub(crate) const ROMAN_LABEL_MAX: u32 = 32767;

/// `lowerLetter` / `upperLetter` and `\* alphabetic`: past z Word repeats
/// the letter, 27 "aa", 28 "bb", 53 "aaa" (Word 16 probes la1006 and
/// nf1006, 2026-10-06). Past thirty z's (780) a list label starts again
/// at "a" (probe bn1006b). Zero counts as 1.
pub(crate) fn alpha_label(n: u32, upper: bool) -> String {
    let n = (n.max(1) - 1) % ALPHA_LABEL_MAX;
    let ch = char::from(b'a' + (n % 26) as u8);
    let ch = if upper { ch.to_ascii_uppercase() } else { ch };
    std::iter::repeat_n(ch, (n / 26) as usize + 1).collect()
}

#### Reachability

An untrusted DOCX author controls numbering format and counters. A victim needs only to render or generate a Markdown numbered-list label view; the section-page route needs no bookmarks, special option or privileged setting. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Reachable through public DOCX read/Markdown conversion and render/PDF/PNG when the relevant Chicago-formatted list/page/endnote label is generated.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Document author controlling numbering metadata.

- **Entry point:** Public PDF/PNG/render APIs, Markdown numbered-list label views and shared list_number callers

Preconditions:
- Victim reads/renders document with Chicago-formatted numbering and a large start value.

Existing controls:
- Other alphabetic/Roman formatters reduce counter ranges; Chicago does not.
- Markdown clamps depth but forwards the large counter into list_number.
- Input size and XML depth budgets allow the ten-digit start value.

Limitations:
- No data disclosure or code execution established; remote service exposure is deployment-dependent.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Attacker-selected document numbers directly cause excessive allocations in public document-processing paths. Impact is host-process availability; no remote service is assumed and memory isolation limits wider damage.

Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Memory exhaustion and host-process availability loss. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Memory exhaustion/process termination.
- **Why:** An admitted start value of 4294967295 causes chicago_label to repeat a three-byte symbol 1073741824 times, requesting roughly 3 GiB for one label before downstream shaping/copying. The section-page route evaluates the label for ordinary paragraph blocks even without bookmarks.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Tiny decimal values amplify directly into very large allocations without configuration changes. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Compact metadata reaches normal read/render paths.
- **Why:** The numeric input is document-controlled and reaches the sink with default conversion.

#### Remediation

Bound generated byte/glyph length inside the shared Chicago formatter before repetition, with a documented safe cycle/fallback or typed refusal. Apply that bound to all list, startOverride, section-page and Markdown/direct list_number callers; do not rely on input bytes, counter saturation or later clipping. Include authored endnote numStart/format and MCP agent-view callers in the shared formatter budget. Additional retained remediation detail: Apply a central maximum output length to Chicago labels before repetition and enforce a cumulative numbering-output budget. Use a documented bounded fallback or typed refusal consistently for list, read/agent, page and future formatter consumers.

Tests:
- Cover maximum u32 Chicago start and startOverride values without large allocations.
- Exercise section page labels and Markdown list-label views as well as ordinary list rendering.
- Reject or safely cycle a Chicago list start/startOverride at u32::MAX.
- Exercise Chicago section pgNumType start=u32::MAX on an ordinary paragraph and direct list_number callers.
- Chicago starts near u32::MAX must avoid proportional allocation in render and Markdown output.
- Verify inclusive label budgets and preserve existing alphabetic/Roman wrapping.
- Chicago values near u32::MAX must return a bounded result or typed resource-limit error without large allocation.
- Exercise ordinary list labels, section page labels and DOCX-to-Markdown list markers through the same fixed helper.
- Refuse oversized Chicago starts and overrides at level zero before allocating a large label.
- Exercise the same malformed counter through rendering and agent-view reading, and retain ordinary Chicago cycles.
- Maximum u32 start and startOverride never allocate proportional marker text.
- Normal Chicago cycles preserve their expected markers.
- Reject huge Chicago list starts and overrides through reading and rendering APIs.
- Cover page and endnote Chicago starts as sibling routes.
- Keep ordinary Chicago symbol cycles and existing Roman/alphabetic behavior.
- Use small test label budgets to verify exact-boundary and over-limit refusal from list starts, startOverride, page starts, endnote starts and Markdown reads.
- Verify large starts in bounded numeric formats remain supported without proportional allocation.
- Use small deterministic boundary cases for Chicago label byte limits, huge start/startOverride values and normal Chicago sequences; assert refusal occurs before repetition.
- Use a small deterministic document with extreme semantic values or alternate valid OPC paths and assert controlled refusal or complete selected sanitization before expensive processing.
- Read and render level-zero Chicago lists using large start and startOverride values; assert bounded refusal/fallback.
- Exercise Chicago page numbering with a large section start, and preserve small intended labels in reading and rendering.

Preventive controls:
- Bound derived dimensions and generated output independently from archive/XML input byte limits.
- Every numeric-to-text formatter should have an explicit output-size bound.

#### Summary

HTML altChunk text with bare ampersands and the public XML entity decoder repeatedly search the remaining suffix for ';', yielding quadratic CPU work. A valid admitted .rels Target containing repeated &amp; is normalized upstream and redundantly decoded by PartFs, reaching the same XML sink during rendering, inspection, revision processing or comparison even when the target part does not exist.

#### Root Cause

Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix. oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated &amp; in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans.

pub fn unescape_xml_text(s: &str) -> String {
    if !s.contains('&') {
        return s.to_string();

    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;

        if chars[i] == '&' {

                if let Some(decoded) = decode_entity(&body) {
                    out.push_str(&decoded);
                    i = i + 1 + semi_rel + 1;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            out.push('&');
            i += 1;

            out.push(chars[i]);
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out

pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {

pub fn unescape_xml_text(s: &str) -> String {
    if !s.contains('&') {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < chars.len() {
        if chars[i] == '&' {
            // find ';'
            if let Some(semi_rel) = chars[i + 1..].iter().position(|&c| c == ';') {
                let body: String = chars[i + 1..i + 1 + semi_rel].iter().collect();
                if let Some(decoded) = decode_entity(&body) {
                    out.push_str(&decoded);
                    i = i + 1 + semi_rel + 1;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            out.push('&');
            i += 1;
        } else {

            i += 1;

/// A main-document part found the OPC way, by relationship type
/// (`…/relationships/<kind>`, transitional or strict), falling back to
/// Word's conventional name. Other producers may name these parts freely.
pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
    let suffix = format!("/{kind}");
    pkg.main_document_part()
        .and_then(|main| {
            let rel = pkg.read_rels_for(&main)?.items.iter().find(|r| {
                r.rel_type.ends_with(&suffix) && r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
            })?;
            Some(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &rel.target))
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback.to_string())

#### Summary

HTML altChunk text with bare ampersands and the public XML entity decoder repeatedly search the remaining suffix for ';', yielding quadratic CPU work. A valid admitted .rels Target containing repeated &amp; is normalized upstream and redundantly decoded by PartFs, reaching the same XML sink during rendering, inspection, revision processing or comparison even when the target part does not exist. An additional admitted-main-XML route uses an unquoted value whose first character never reappears: the DOM consumes through EOF and decodes a bare-ampersand comment as an attribute, reaching the same quadratic XML decoder. Ordinary bare-ampersand text is rejected upstream and is not this proof. The same HTML decoder is also reached by Markdown-to-DOCX raw HTML blocks and attribute values; its ten-byte accepted-entity bound is applied after the unbounded search. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates both established decoders independently: ordinary HTML/MHT paragraph text reaches the HTML helper even when script/style content is skipped, while an internal fontTable target reaches redundant XML decoding before any absent-part lookup. Its supplied offline dependency evidence identifies oxml-opc 0.14.2 and quick-xml 0.41.0 attribute normalization, independently supported by the repository target round-trip test. No reducer dependency inspection occurred.

#### Root Cause

Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix. oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated &amp; in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans. The assigned current-tree relationship round-trip assertion corroborates normalized targets independently of dependency-version assumptions, and the established internal story renderer resolves the target before checking whether the selected part exists. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read_relationships` loads each record through oxml-opc, whose `parse_relationship` applies `decoded_and_normalized_value` before storing Target. Internal consumers pass that decoded string to `PartFs::resolve_rel_target`, which invokes `unescape_xml_text` again. For N escaped ampersands in source, the second pass sees N literal ampersands and no semicolons. Each failed semicolon search revisits the suffix, then advances by one, yielding N(N-1)/2 comparisons. Attribute count, XML depth and package byte limits do not bound this quadratic work adequately. Assigned discovery-0022 adds tolerant HTML-style attribute boundaries versus DOM first-character-as-quote parsing: comment ampersands can become one large decoded attribute. This is an additional source path to the retained XML suffix-search root; no relationship resolution is required. Assigned discovery-0026 corroboration: Markdown html_attribute (src/markdown/write.rs:1350-1357) and html_block_text (1415-1425), including Event::Html, reuse altchunk::decode_entities. Both therefore share the HTML helper's full-suffix search before its length filter; these consumers do not require an XML relationship or ordinary malformed XML text. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates both established decoders independently: ordinary HTML/MHT paragraph text reaches the HTML helper even when script/style content is skipped, while an internal fontTable target reaches redundant XML decoding before any absent-part lookup. Its supplied offline dependency evidence identifies oxml-opc 0.14.2 and quick-xml 0.41.0 attribute normalization, independently supported by the repository target round-trip test. No reducer dependency inspection occurred.

```
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;

    let table = font_table::load_font_table(&pkg);
    let mut embedded = font_table::load_embedded_fonts(&pkg, &table);
```

```
fn read_relationships(xml: &[u8]) -> Result<Relationships, OpcError> {
    let mut rels = Relationships::new();
    let mut items = Vec::new();
    for record in metadata_records(
        xml,
        "Relationships",
        "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships",
        &["Relationship"],
    )? {
        for item in oxml_opc::Relationships::from_xml(&record)?.items {
            items.push(item);
        }
    }
    // Seed the private counter once: add_with_id removes existing IDs, so
    // calling it for every record would turn a linear read into a quadratic one.
    // A fresh collection also has no retained source XML: to_xml stays canonical.
    if let Some((_, item)) = items
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|item| {
            item.id
                .strip_prefix("rId")
                .and_then(|id| id.parse::<u32>().ok())
                .map(|id| (id, item))
        })
        .max_by_key(|(id, _)| *id)
    {
        rels.add_with_id(&item.id, &item.rel_type, &item.target);
    }
    rels.items = items;
    Ok(rels)
```

        // escapes again when writing: every open/write added one `&amp;`, and

                .clone()

        let once = PartFs::open(&fs.to_zip().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let twice = PartFs::open(&once.to_zip().unwrap()).unwrap();

/// The main document's other story parts (headers, footers, footnotes,
/// endnotes, comments), found by relationship type.
fn story_parts_xml(pkg: &PartFs, main: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(main) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    rels.items
        .iter()
        .filter(|r| {
            r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
                && ["/header", "/footer", "/footnotes", "/endnotes", "/comments"]
                    .iter()
                    .any(|k| r.rel_type.ends_with(k))
        })
        .filter_map(|r| pkg.part_string(&pkg.resolve_rel_target(main, &r.target)))
        .collect()
}

**Every unsupported ampersand rescans the remaining suffix** — `src/xmllinq/parse.rs:764-796`

For each literal ampersand the decoder searches all remaining characters for a semicolon. If there is no supported entity it advances by only one; N literal ampersands therefore require roughly N(N-1)/2 character checks.

```rust
pub fn unescape_xml_text(s: &str) -> String {
    if !s.contains('&') {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < chars.len() {
        if chars[i] == '&' {
            // find ';'
            if let Some(semi_rel) = chars[i + 1..].iter().position(|&c| c == ';') {
                let body: String = chars[i + 1..i + 1 + semi_rel].iter().collect();
                if let Some(decoded) = decode_entity(&body) {
                    out.push_str(&decoded);
                    i = i + 1 + semi_rel + 1;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            out.push('&');
            i += 1;
        } else {
            out.push(chars[i]);
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

fn decode_entity(body: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let b: Vec<char> = body.chars().collect();
    if b.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
```

**Entity decoder rescans suffix** — `src/convert/altchunk.rs:724-762`

For each untrusted ampersand the decoder searches the full remaining suffix for a semicolon before applying its ten-byte check; failure advances only one ampersand and repeats the scan.

```rust
pub(crate) fn decode_entities(s: &str) -> String {
    if !s.contains('&') {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut rest = s;
    while let Some(a) = rest.find('&') {
        out.push_str(&rest[..a]);
        let tail = &rest[a..];
        let semi = tail.find(';').filter(|&e| e <= 10);
        let decoded = semi.and_then(|e| {
            let ent = &tail[1..e];
            let ch = match ent {
                "amp" => Some('&'),
                "lt" => Some('<'),
                "gt" => Some('>'),
                "quot" => Some('"'),
                "apos" => Some('\''),
                "nbsp" => Some('\u{a0}'),
                _ if ent.starts_with("#x") || ent.starts_with("#X") => {
                    u32::from_str_radix(&ent[2..], 16)
                        .ok()
                        .and_then(char::from_u32)
                }
                _ if ent.starts_with('#') => ent[1..].parse().ok().and_then(char::from_u32),
                _ => None,
            };
            ch.map(|c| (c, e))
        });
        if let Some((c, e)) = decoded {
            out.push(c);
            rest = &tail[e + 1..];
        } else {
            out.push('&');
            rest = &tail[1..];
        }
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
```

    #[test]
    fn rel_attributes_survive_round_trips_unescaped() {

        // escapes again when writing: every open/write added one `&amp;`, and

        let mut fs = package_with_header_rels();
        fs.set_part(
            "word/_rels/document.xml.rels",
            format!(r#"<Relationships xmlns="{RELS_NS}"><Relationship Id="rId1" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/image" Target="media/p.jpg&amp;ehk=Q"/></Relationships>"#).into_bytes(),
        );
        let target = |fs: &PartFs| {
            fs.read_rels_for("word/document.xml").unwrap().items[0]
                .target
                .clone()
        };
        assert_eq!(target(&fs), "media/p.jpg&ehk=Q");
        let once = PartFs::open(&fs.to_zip().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let twice = PartFs::open(&once.to_zip().unwrap()).unwrap();

/// (`…/relationships/<kind>`, transitional or strict), falling back to
/// Word's conventional name. Other producers may name these parts freely.
pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
    let suffix = format!("/{kind}");
    pkg.main_document_part()
        .and_then(|main| {
            let rel = pkg.read_rels_for(&main)?.items.iter().find(|r| {
                r.rel_type.ends_with(&suffix) && r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
            })?;
            Some(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &rel.target))
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback.to_string())
}

Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed valid escaped Target syntax reaches a once-decoded raw ampersand string, then the second decoder's quadratic scan. Notes/story consumers resolve before checking part existence. Exact oxml-opc 0.14.2 parse_relationship at cached relationship.rs:924-938 decodes Target with quick-xml 0.41 normalized attribute values. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Reviewed the decoder loop through failed entity handling, which advances by one ampersand then searches the next suffix. HTML part byte limits permit large repeated runs; there is no entity-count/work cap. No runtime timing claim is made. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): with_layout imports the related HTML chunk and Builder::text calls this decoder. For N ampersands without ';', suffix lengths N,N-1,...,1 are searched. The decoder preserves invalid references instead of refusing them. Archive admission scans XML/.rels policy but treats an HTML part as bounded opaque bytes, so the checked-XML malformed-reference countercontrol does not apply. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Confirmed oxml-opc0.14.2 src/relationship.rs:925-938 normalizes Target; local opc/mod.rs then unescapes again. Reviewed inspect::related and comparison note resolution, which resolve internal targets before loading parts. Correctly escaped input passes strict XML validation, and the missing target does not short-circuit the expensive resolver. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Inspected pinned oxml-opc 0.14.2 parse_relationship confirms decoded_and_normalized_value before target storage. Valid raw &amp; repetitions become bare ampersands. inspect::related passes that string unchanged to the second decoder, which searches the suffix before advancing only one character when no semicolon exists. Missing target lookup happens afterward.

An unsuccessful search advances one character, scanning the remainder again. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration: Each raw ampersand scans the remaining character vector for a semicolon, then advances just one character if none is decoded.

```rust
pub fn unescape_xml_text(s: &str) -> String {
    if !s.contains('&') {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < chars.len() {
        if chars[i] == '&' {
            // find ';'
            if let Some(semi_rel) = chars[i + 1..].iter().position(|&c| c == ';') {
                let body: String = chars[i + 1..i + 1 + semi_rel].iter().collect();
                if let Some(decoded) = decode_entity(&body) {
                    out.push_str(&decoded);
                    i = i + 1 + semi_rel + 1;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            out.push('&');
            i += 1;
        } else {
            out.push(chars[i]);
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out

pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {

}

**Current-tree regression asserts decoded targets** — `src/opc/mod.rs:1258-1276`

This source test documents the current model contract: an encoded ampersand in Target becomes a literal ampersand and survives subsequent package round trips.

```rust
    fn rel_attributes_survive_round_trips_unescaped() {
        // rdocx-opc 0.1.0 keeps `Target="a&amp;b"` escaped when parsing and
        // escapes again when writing: every open/write added one `&amp;`, and
        // `image11.jpg&ehk=…` ended up pointing at `image11.jpg&amp;amp;amp;…`,
        // a part that does not exist (a2412654, 2026-09-26 English redlines).
        let mut fs = package_with_header_rels();
        fs.set_part(
            "word/_rels/document.xml.rels",
            format!(r#"<Relationships xmlns="{RELS_NS}"><Relationship Id="rId1" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/image" Target="media/p.jpg&amp;ehk=Q"/></Relationships>"#).into_bytes(),
        );
        let target = |fs: &PartFs| {
            fs.read_rels_for("word/document.xml").unwrap().items[0]
                .target
                .clone()
        };
        assert_eq!(target(&fs), "media/p.jpg&ehk=Q");
        let once = PartFs::open(&fs.to_zip().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let twice = PartFs::open(&once.to_zip().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(target(&twice), "media/p.jpg&ehk=Q");
```

**Decoded internal targets are resolved before lookup** — `src/convert/mod.rs:21283-21299`

```rust
/// The main document's other story parts (headers, footers, footnotes,
/// endnotes, comments), found by relationship type.
fn story_parts_xml(pkg: &PartFs, main: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(main) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    rels.items
        .iter()
        .filter(|r| {
            r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
                && ["/header", "/footer", "/footnotes", "/endnotes", "/comments"]
                    .iter()
                    .any(|k| r.rel_type.ends_with(k))
        })
        .filter_map(|r| pkg.part_string(&pkg.resolve_rel_target(main, &r.target)))
        .collect()
}
```

**Every unsupported ampersand rescans the remaining suffix** — `src/xmllinq/parse.rs:764-796`

For each literal ampersand the decoder searches all remaining characters for a semicolon. If there is no supported entity it advances by only one; N literal ampersands therefore require roughly N(N-1)/2 character checks.

```rust
pub fn unescape_xml_text(s: &str) -> String {
    if !s.contains('&') {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < chars.len() {
        if chars[i] == '&' {
            // find ';'
            if let Some(semi_rel) = chars[i + 1..].iter().position(|&c| c == ';') {
                let body: String = chars[i + 1..i + 1 + semi_rel].iter().collect();
                if let Some(decoded) = decode_entity(&body) {
                    out.push_str(&decoded);
                    i = i + 1 + semi_rel + 1;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            out.push('&');
            i += 1;
        } else {
            out.push(chars[i]);
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

fn decode_entity(body: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let b: Vec<char> = body.chars().collect();
    if b.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
```
