**Entity decoder rescans suffix** — `src/convert/altchunk.rs:724-762`

For each untrusted ampersand the decoder searches the full remaining suffix for a semicolon before applying its ten-byte check; failure advances only one ampersand and repeats the scan.

```rust
pub(crate) fn decode_entities(s: &str) -> String {
    if !s.contains('&') {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut rest = s;
    while let Some(a) = rest.find('&') {
        out.push_str(&rest[..a]);
        let tail = &rest[a..];
        let semi = tail.find(';').filter(|&e| e <= 10);
        let decoded = semi.and_then(|e| {
            let ent = &tail[1..e];
            let ch = match ent {
                "amp" => Some('&'),
                "lt" => Some('<'),
                "gt" => Some('>'),
                "quot" => Some('"'),
                "apos" => Some('\''),
                "nbsp" => Some('\u{a0}'),
                _ if ent.starts_with("#x") || ent.starts_with("#X") => {
                    u32::from_str_radix(&ent[2..], 16)
                        .ok()
                        .and_then(char::from_u32)
                }
                _ if ent.starts_with('#') => ent[1..].parse().ok().and_then(char::from_u32),
                _ => None,
            };
            ch.map(|c| (c, e))
        });
        if let Some((c, e)) = decoded {
            out.push(c);
            rest = &tail[e + 1..];
        } else {
            out.push('&');
            rest = &tail[1..];
        }
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
```
```rust
    out
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn rel_attributes_survive_round_trips_unescaped() {
        // rdocx-opc 0.1.0 keeps `Target="a&amp;b"` escaped when parsing and
        // escapes again when writing: every open/write added one `&amp;`, and
        // `image11.jpg&ehk=…` ended up pointing at `image11.jpg&amp;amp;amp;…`,
        // a part that does not exist (a2412654, 2026-09-26 English redlines).
        let mut fs = package_with_header_rels();
        fs.set_part(
            "word/_rels/document.xml.rels",
            format!(r#"<Relationships xmlns="{RELS_NS}"><Relationship Id="rId1" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/image" Target="media/p.jpg&amp;ehk=Q"/></Relationships>"#).into_bytes(),
        );
        let target = |fs: &PartFs| {
            fs.read_rels_for("word/document.xml").unwrap().items[0]
                .target
                .clone()
        };
        assert_eq!(target(&fs), "media/p.jpg&ehk=Q");
        let once = PartFs::open(&fs.to_zip().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let twice = PartFs::open(&once.to_zip().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(target(&twice), "media/p.jpg&ehk=Q");
    }
```

**Auxiliary targets may use arbitrary part names** — `src/convert/mod.rs:21308-21320`

```rust
/// (`…/relationships/<kind>`, transitional or strict), falling back to
/// Word's conventional name. Other producers may name these parts freely.
pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
    let suffix = format!("/{kind}");
    pkg.main_document_part()
        .and_then(|main| {
            let rel = pkg.read_rels_for(&main)?.items.iter().find(|r| {
                r.rel_type.ends_with(&suffix) && r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
            })?;
            Some(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &rel.target))
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback.to_string())
```
```
}
```

**Suffix rescanned for every unresolved ampersand** — `src/xmllinq/parse.rs:764-787`

Each ampersand without a following semicolon triggers another scan over the remaining string.

```
pub fn unescape_xml_text(s: &str) -> String {
    if !s.contains('&') {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < chars.len() {
        if chars[i] == '&' {
            // find ';'
            if let Some(semi_rel) = chars[i + 1..].iter().position(|&c| c == ';') {
                let body: String = chars[i + 1..i + 1 + semi_rel].iter().collect();
                if let Some(decoded) = decode_entity(&body) {
                    out.push_str(&decoded);
                    i = i + 1 + semi_rel + 1;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            out.push('&');
            i += 1;
        } else {
            out.push(chars[i]);
            i += 1;
        }
```

#### Reachability

Untrusted document supplier or caller-controlled parser input controls input reaching the cited consumers without needing operator environment or filesystem authority. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Public inspection and comparison paths consume internal relationship targets; external filtering does not exclude this internal relationship. Part existence is checked after resolution. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Summary follows internal header/footer/comments/footnotes/endnotes/settings/styles targets; resolve_rel_target runs before part existence validation.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document supplier or caller-controlled parser input Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): DOCX supplier

- **Entry point:** src/convert/altchunk.rs:405; src/convert/mod.rs:789 Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: inspect::inspect and document comparison note/header processing Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): inspect::summary and package consumers following internal relationships

- **Sink:** src/convert/altchunk.rs:728; src/convert/altchunk.rs:753; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:768

- **Outcome:** worker CPU exhaustion Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Quadratic CPU consumption before target refusal

Preconditions:
- A rendering host imports an internal HTML/MHT chunk containing a large run of bare ampersands, which HTML text can contain.
- The XML helper independently accepts arbitrary strings; package acceptance of malformed bare-ampersand XML is not required for the HTML attack.
- Victim inspects or compares the package.
- Victim processes the DOCX using a consumer that follows the relationship kind.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A document supplier can exhaust resources of its processing host through accepted public conversion paths. Remote/shared exposure is conditional; there is no established confidentiality/integrity compromise.

Process CPU/memory quotas and isolated workers constrain impact; shared document-processing deployments increase affected availability.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Availability of the invoking process. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Quadratic CPU consumption before target refusal

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Valid shallow XML and standard internal relationship types reach the sink. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Victim must process attacker input through the cited public interface.

#### Remediation

Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&amp;' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips. Preserve the standalone XML helper's documented permissive output for unsupported or unterminated references while making its work linear. Apply practical relationship-target length/work bounds as defense in depth, preserving exactly one normalization pass and the standalone helper's linear permissive behavior. Align admission/DOM attribute token boundaries or reject unsupported unquoted syntax as defense in depth. Preserve the linear XML decoder fix for this comment-to-attribute route; removing only the redundant relationship decode does not cover it. Apply the bounded HTML helper consistently to Markdown raw-HTML block text and attribute consumers, using UTF-8-safe bounded lookahead and preserving recognized entities, malformed literal retention and multibyte text.

Tests:
- Deterministic operation-count tests for long bare-ampersand runs must scale linearly.
- Preserve predefined/numeric entity decoding and literal retention of unknown/truncated entities in both helpers.
- Add deterministic regression inputs for the source-supported differential and assert a typed bounded refusal.
- Verify ordinary compatible documents still process under unchanged limits.
- Use valid .rels Targets with repeated &amp; through revision processing and comparison, including nonexistent internal targets; verify bounded linear work and one-time entity normalization. Keep malformed-reference literal preservation and ordinary valid target behavior.
- Resolve targets containing many encoded literal ampersands with linear work.
- Preserve literal '&amp;' part names without repeated decoding and round-trip corruption.
- Verify an escaped-ampersand relationship resolves with exactly one decode.
- Use instrumented scan-step assertions for long ampersand-only strings and unknown entities to ensure linear work.
- Keep legitimate encoded targets resolving correctly.
- Resolve a legal relationship containing many escaped ampersands with linear work and correct literal target preservation.
- Retain handling of numeric/predefined entities and nonexistent internal targets without double-decoding them.
- Many raw ampersands require linear scan work.
- Named/numeric entity behavior and malformed suffix handling remain correct.
- Verify repeated malformed ampersands require linear work through the public HTML import path.
- Retain unknown/numeric/predefined entity behavior.
- Count bounded lookahead steps for ampersand-heavy semicolon-free text and assert work proportional to input length.
- Assert relationship target decoding occurs once; use deterministic counted work for a long escaped-ampersand target and malformed public decoder strings.
- Regression-test literal ampersands in parsed targets for exactly-once decoding.
- Count scanner steps for long ampersand targets and assert linear growth without wall-clock unit assertions.
- Integration-test rendering a document whose missing internal story target contains a long encoded-ampersand sequence.
- Inspect and compare valid relationships with long escaped-ampersand targets and verify bounded linear work/refusal.
- Preserve correct resolution of names with a literal ampersand or semicolon after exactly one XML decode.
- Deterministic boundary regression tests should assert typed refusal or bounded work for the identified tokenizer/classification/count discrepancy, with normal supported inputs preserved.
- Malformed ampersand runs require linear bounded search work.
- Recognized entities and multibyte text preserve current output.
- Both altChunk and Markdown HTML callers use the bounded helper.
- Inspect a valid &amp;-heavy target with work proportional to attribute length.
- Ensure literal encoded entity-looking filenames retain exactly one decoding step.
- Use a deterministic comparison/work counter to establish linear bounded scanning for long runs of unterminated ampersands.
- A relationship target containing many encoded ampersands must resolve or fail in linear work without a second entity decode.
- Assert bounded/linear scanning for semicolon-free ampersands and far-away semicolons across HTML and Markdown callers.

Preventive controls:
- Specify encoded-versus-decoded contracts at parser adapters and avoid repeated representation decoding.

#### Summary

An attacker-authored Word 97–2003 DOC can repeatedly begin fields and enter their result sections, leaving an increasingly long all-false field stack. Story::blocks scans the entire stack before every input character, giving quadratic CPU work during reading/conversion and even the native Word-input refusal hint.

#### Root Cause

The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec\<bool\> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.

**Control preservation** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:1115-1129`

cp1252 preserves ASCII-range field markers.

```rust
/// Windows-1252 bytes 0x80-0x9F as the spec's compressed-text table maps
/// them (MS-DOC 2.4.1); every other byte is its own code point.
fn cp1252(byte: u8) -> char {
    const HIGH: [u16; 32] = [
        0x20AC, 0x0081, 0x201A, 0x0192, 0x201E, 0x2026, 0x2020, 0x2021, 0x02C6, 0x2030, 0x0160,
        0x2039, 0x0152, 0x008D, 0x017D, 0x008F, 0x0090, 0x2018, 0x2019, 0x201C, 0x201D, 0x2022,
        0x2013, 0x2014, 0x02DC, 0x2122, 0x0161, 0x203A, 0x0153, 0x009D, 0x017E, 0x0178,
    ];
    match byte {
        0x80..=0x9F => HIGH
            .get(usize::from(byte.wrapping_sub(0x80)))
            .and_then(|&unit| char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)))
            .unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'),
        _ => char::from(byte),
```

#### Validation

Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -\> main_text -\> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection. Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -\> legacy_doc::read -\> main_text -\> Story::blocks -\> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops. Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For \[0x13,0x14\] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.

Validation method: Preserved already-validated Standard evidence and assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only, without repository inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis

```rust
/// Windows-1252 bytes 0x80-0x9F as the spec's compressed-text table maps
/// them (MS-DOC 2.4.1); every other byte is its own code point.
fn cp1252(byte: u8) -> char {
    const HIGH: [u16; 32] = [
        0x20AC, 0x0081, 0x201A, 0x0192, 0x201E, 0x2026, 0x2020, 0x2021, 0x02C6, 0x2030, 0x0160,
        0x2039, 0x0152, 0x008D, 0x017D, 0x008F, 0x0090, 0x2018, 0x2019, 0x201C, 0x201D, 0x2022,
        0x2013, 0x2014, 0x02DC, 0x2122, 0x0161, 0x203A, 0x0153, 0x009D, 0x017E, 0x0178,
    ];
    match byte {
        0x80..=0x9F => HIGH
            .get(usize::from(byte.wrapping_sub(0x80)))
            .and_then(|&unit| char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)))
            .unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'),
        _ => char::from(byte),
    }
```

#### Reachability

A legacy DOC author controls the story passed to legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown, doc_to_docx and native CLI convert. Native Word-input refusal also reads the DOC for its conversion hint. A valid OLE container, Word FIB and covering piece table are required; no privileged configuration is needed.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author

- **Entry point:** legacy_doc::read / doc_to_markdown / doc_to_docx; native CLI convert and read_document refusal hint

Limitations:
- Memory-safe reads remain bounded; no arbitrary code execution or confidentiality impact is established.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Small untrusted document input can cause disproportionate CPU consumption through public legacy conversion APIs. This affects host availability; shared-server exposure is not assumed and process CPU limits constrain impact.

Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Processing-thread CPU exhaustion and conversion service degradation.
- **Why:** Repeated nested field beginnings followed by separators leave an increasingly long all-false field-state stack. Each subsequent character scans that stack. Approximately 300 KiB of balanced field delimiters at depth 100000 requires billions of Boolean examinations, consuming substantial CPU before returning.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** The algorithmic amplification requires only crafted field text, not privileged configuration.
- **Why:** The triggering structure and values are document-controlled and not rejected by existing guards.

#### Remediation

Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work.

Tests:
- Verify linear field-processing work for deeply nested begin/separator/result/end sequences.
- Cover mixed code/result nesting to retain the rule that any code ancestor suppresses text.
- Nested result fields must consume linear work with a maintained active-code count.
- Over-depth balanced and unbalanced fields must refuse within an explicit depth budget.
- Assert work scales linearly for deeply nested balanced result-phase fields.
- Preserve nested-code suppression semantics, repeated separators and unmatched field-marker behavior.
- Extend existing nested-field fixtures with deeply nested balanced result fields.
- Assert linear parser operations with a deterministic counter rather than wall-clock timing.
- Check correctness and configured depth refusal.
- Use deterministic work counters to show linear processing of deeply nested field-result sequences.
- Refuse nesting above the configured bound and preserve ordinary nested-field semantics.
- Use a deterministic parser test with many nested result-phase fields; assert bounded work using an instrumented operation count and correct ordinary field output.
- Bound work for deeply nested result fields and enforce a maximum depth.
- Preserve nested code/result visibility semantics without rescanning the complete stack per character.
- Deep nested result fields process in linear time or return a typed depth refusal.
- Nested code/result semantics retain expected text inclusion.

Preventive controls:
- Budget logical processing work and representation expansion, and bind preflight validation to the actual consumer's selected input.

#### Summary

An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission.

#### Root Cause

cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene. The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic. Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.
```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
```

**Stale span repair does not reduce oversized spans** — `src/convert/mod.rs:14168-14201`

Oversized authored spans skip this repair when `used >= cols.len()`; it does not clamp them.

```rust
/// brings its width closer to the tcW: Word reads the row by its cell
/// widths and the saved grid as a cache (25f1d311bd). A row whose cells
/// fit their columns (within `STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT`) is a short row and
/// stays one.
fn stretch_stale_spans(rows: &mut [Vec<RawCell>], cols: &[f32]) {
    const STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT: f32 = 20.0;
    for row in rows.iter_mut() {
        let used: usize = row.iter().map(|c| c.colspan.max(1)).sum();
        if used >= cols.len() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut spare = cols.len() - used;
        let mut col = 0usize;
        for cell in row.iter_mut() {
            let span = cell.colspan.max(1);
            if let PrefWidth::Dxa(want) = cell.pref {
                let mut covered: f32 = cols.iter().skip(col).take(span).sum();
                let mut extra = 0usize;
                while extra < spare
                    && want - covered > STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT
                    && let Some(&next) = cols.get(col + span + extra)
                    && (covered + next - want).abs() < (want - covered).abs()
                {
                    covered += next;
                    extra += 1;
                }
                if extra > 0 {
                    cell.colspan = span + extra;
                    spare -= extra;
                }
            }
            col += cell.colspan.max(1);
        }
    }
```

Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value. The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path. Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -\> with_layout -\> body table_block -\> cell_span/row_grid_skip -\> RawCell.colspan -\> occupancy -\> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): The public rendering path admits and opens the document before table parsing. A positive 2147483647 fits usize on supported 32/64-bit targets. It is retained as `colspan`; the stale-span repair skips oversized rows. Occupancy reaches `vec![each; occupancy]` or `resize` without a maximum. Both row-skip fields independently feed the same sum via grid_skip_cell.

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

**Stale span repair does not reduce oversized spans** — `src/convert/mod.rs:14168-14201`

Oversized authored spans skip this repair when `used >= cols.len()`; it does not clamp them.

```rust
/// brings its width closer to the tcW: Word reads the row by its cell
/// widths and the saved grid as a cache (25f1d311bd). A row whose cells
/// fit their columns (within `STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT`) is a short row and
/// stays one.
fn stretch_stale_spans(rows: &mut [Vec<RawCell>], cols: &[f32]) {
    const STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT: f32 = 20.0;
    for row in rows.iter_mut() {
        let used: usize = row.iter().map(|c| c.colspan.max(1)).sum();
        if used >= cols.len() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut spare = cols.len() - used;
        let mut col = 0usize;
        for cell in row.iter_mut() {
            let span = cell.colspan.max(1);
            if let PrefWidth::Dxa(want) = cell.pref {
                let mut covered: f32 = cols.iter().skip(col).take(span).sum();
                let mut extra = 0usize;
                while extra < spare
                    && want - covered > STALE_SPAN_SLACK_PT
                    && let Some(&next) = cols.get(col + span + extra)
                    && (covered + next - want).abs() < (want - covered).abs()
                {
                    covered += next;
                    extra += 1;
                }
                if extra > 0 {
                    cell.colspan = span + extra;
                    spare -= extra;
                }
            }
            col += cell.colspan.max(1);
        }
    }
```

#### Reachability

Attacker controls only DOCX table XML; a victim processes it with the public renderer. No special option, filesystem privilege, local account or privileged configuration is required. Public convert::docx_to_pdf/render/docx_to_png/docx_render_report accept DOCX bytes and reach with_layout/table_block; no nondefault option or external relationship is needed.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author Untrusted document supplier

- **Entry point:** convert::docx_to_pdf / render / docx_to_png and shared PDF/PNG/render-report binding/CLI callers

Preconditions:
- Victim renders the supplied DOCX.
- Victim renders a document containing the attacker-controlled table.

Existing controls:
- Original archive and XML admission apply; caller may impose process memory/CPU limits.

Limitations:
- No data disclosure or code execution established; remote service exposure is deployment-dependent.

#### Severity

**Medium** — An untrusted document can deterministically drive huge allocations through a public parser boundary. This compromises availability of the rendering process; shared-service exposure is conditional and process memory limits constrain the blast radius.

Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Memory exhaustion or process termination; no code execution or data access is established.
- **Why:** An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Direct integer-to-allocation path reachable with a tiny document.
- **Why:** The numeric input is document-controlled and reaches the sink with default conversion.

#### Remediation

Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess.

Tests:
- Check that a tiny table with an enormous gridSpan is refused before allocation.
- Cover gridBefore/gridAfter, accumulated spans, and overflow boundaries.
- Reject huge positive gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before allocation.
- Reject checked aggregate row overflow and total table-grid budget overflow; valid small tables must preserve layout.
- Excessive individual and cumulative spans/skips must refuse with bounded work.
- Cover count overflow and 32-bit WASM.
- Keep valid merged/skipped-column rendering.
- Test excessive individual spans, row offsets and cumulative spans using tiny in-memory documents; assert typed refusal before allocation.
- Test numeric overflow and valid boundary tables.
- Integration-test huge cell spans and row skips through public rendering APIs and assert bounded typed refusal, including aggregate overflow.
- Keep representative valid merged tables rendering correctly within the budget.
- Tiny tables with very large gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter must fail with a resource-limit error before vector allocation.
- Test cumulative spans exceeding the limit and arithmetic overflow; retain supported ordinary merged tables.
- Reject huge gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter in otherwise small admitted DOCX files.
- Cover aggregate span overflow and normal merged cells without large allocation.
- Reject oversized gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter through public rendering APIs.
- Verify cumulative occupancy and integer-overflow refusal on native and wasm32.
- Preserve valid merged-cell and row-skip layouts.

Preventive controls:
- Bound derived dimensions and generated output independently from archive/XML input byte limits.
- Use one semantic table-column policy for authored and synthesized cells.

### [39] Explicit Markdown revision IDs trigger quadratic run splitting

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent verified revision_tags accepts an unbounded count of valid IDs, mark_ids retains them for a single change, name_revision stores them, and story invokes the repeated scan/clone/insert loop. Work growth is derived statically; no timing was measured. |
| Category | Algorithmic complexity |
| CWE | CWE-407 |
| Affected lines | src/markdown/write.rs:59-66, src/markdown/view_notes.rs:371-401, src/markdown/write.rs:4540-4554, src/markdown/xml.rs:632-639, src/markdown/xml.rs:1788-1822, src/markdown/xml.rs:1826-1839 |

#### Summary

A long unspaced insertion with proportionally many explicit revision IDs makes split_for_ids repeatedly search existing one-character tails, scan the remaining text, clone the long run and insert another tail. Work and copied bytes grow quadratically even though the Markdown input and resulting XML are linear in the number of IDs.

#### Root Cause

The number of explicit revision IDs determines repeated full-run splitting. Each iteration scans increasingly many unsplittable tails and clones the remaining long content instead of computing all split positions once.

**split loop** — `src/markdown/xml.rs:1788-1822`

Caller Markdown revision IDs are retained on a change; story() calls split_for_ids, which repeatedly scans and clones the remaining long run to create one piece per ID. This excerpt implements split-loop.

```
pub(super) fn revision_tags(text: &str) -> Option<Vec<Tag>> {
    text.trim()
        .split("; ")
        .map(|tag| {
            let mut words = tag.split(' ');
            let id = words.next()?;
            let handle = words.next()?.strip_prefix('@')?;
            let date = words.next();
            if words.next().is_some() || !is_handle(handle) {
                return None;
            }
            // A bare number (`5 @AC`) is a person's comment, not a tag.
            let id_ok = !id.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit())
                && (id == "noid"
                    || id.strip_suffix(".noid").is_some()
                    || crate::ids::parse_change_ids(id).is_ok());
            let date_ok = date.is_none_or(super::write::is_date);
            (id_ok && date_ok && !id.starts_with('#')).then(|| Tag {
                handle: handle.to_string(),
                date: date.map(str::to_string),
                ids: crate::ids::parse_change_ids(id)
                    .map(|ids| {
                        ids.iter()
                            .filter_map(|c| c.wid.parse().ok())
                            .filter(|&id| id <= MOST_ID)
                            .collect()
                    })
                    .unwrap_or_default(),
            })
        })
        .collect()
```

#### Severity

**Medium** — An untrusted Markdown author can consume excessive CPU and allocation work through a supported conversion API with a moderate linear-size input. No remote service is assumed.

A shared conversion process without time/memory limits increases availability impact; bounded isolated workers limit the failure to one task.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Quadratic CPU and copying can monopolize the converter or exhaust memory.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Supported revision-note syntax directly determines the work count.

#### Remediation

Compute all split boundaries in one pass and build the final run vector once, moving/slicing source content rather than repeatedly cloning it. Apply an explicit revision-ID/work budget before conversion.

- A large one-run/many-ID case uses bounded linear work while preserving exact IDs and text.
- Boundary cases with more IDs than splittable text and Unicode characters preserve existing behavior.

### [40] Document numbering values allocate multi-gigabyte Chicago labels

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Static source establishes unchecked u32 parsing, direct counter propagation, and unconditional repeat; no runtime or deployment proof is required for the public parser boundary. |
| Category | Uncontrolled memory allocation |
| CWE | CWE-789 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/mod.rs:6015-6018, src/convert/mod.rs:6750-6753, src/convert/mod.rs:5629-5641, src/convert/mod.rs:5765, src/convert/mod.rs:8645-8685, src/convert/mod.rs:422-448 |

#### Summary

A small admitted DOCX can set a list start or endnote numStart to 4294967295 with Chicago numbering. The renderer converts that numeric value directly into 1,073,741,824 repeated double-daggers, allocating 3 GiB before subsequent layout and copies. Document suppliers can exhaust a consuming process without a large archive or deep XML.

#### Root Cause

Numeric numbering parameters are treated as output sizes; chicago_label applies str::repeat without checking the expanded marker byte length.

**Numeric value controls allocation length** — `src/convert/mod.rs:6015-6018`

At u32::MAX, the selected 3-byte mark is repeated 2^30 times with no output budget.

```rust

    const MARKS: [&str; 4] = ["*", "†", "‡", "§"];
    let i = n.saturating_sub(1) as usize;
    MARKS[i % 4].repeat(i / 4 + 1)
```

**Untrusted list start accepts full u32 range** — `src/convert/mod.rs:6750-6753`

The parsed start feeds NumLevel.start, next_marker and render without a semantic maximum.

```rust

```

#### Validation

Independently validated from public PDF entry through with_layout admission, list start parsing, counter propagation and render/format_num; endnote numStart reaches the same sink. Archive/XML budgets bound input bytes and structure, not numeric expansion.

Validation method: offline static source trace

- **Status:** validated

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- src/convert/mod.rs:773-774 admits the input first; src/admission.rs:63-76 bounds archive sizes and XML depth, but no semantic number/output bound exists on this path.
- SECURITY.md advises CPU/memory-limited workers; no guarantee against all denial of service is claimed.

Limitations:
- No vulnerability-triggering input or runtime reproduction executed.
- No shared-service deployment is established.

#### Dataflow

word/numbering.xml w:start (or endnotePr/numStart) -\> u32 start -\> Numbering counter/endnote counter -\> format_num(Chicago,n) -\> chicago_label -\> str::repeat.

#### Reachability

Public docx_to_pdf\[_with/_report\] accepts caller-provided bytes, admits the package, loads numbering, and formats the first matching numbered paragraph; a normal %1 placeholder is sufficient.

- **Attacker:** Supplier of a DOCX processed by another user's application

Preconditions:
- Victim converts or renders attacker-controlled DOCX containing an active Chicago numbered paragraph or endnote.
- No trusted configuration changes, large payload, or prior host access are needed.

Existing controls:
- Input admission
- Caller-owned process limits

#### Severity

**Medium** — Attacker-supplied document input deterministically amplifies a tiny numeric field into gigabytes, threatening process availability. No shared production service is assumed; policy recommends external CPU/memory isolation.

A network-facing shared conversion deployment raises exposure; strict worker memory/time limits constrain the blast radius to a worker.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Process memory exhaustion, OOM termination or prolonged CPU/memory pressure.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Direct deterministic numeric-to-allocation path under default parsing; exploitation depends on victim processing the document.

#### Remediation

Enforce a finite expanded-marker byte budget before allocation for every numeric-format consumer. Refuse or safely fall back when start/counter values exceed format-specific limits; propagate a typed refusal instead of allocating. Cover list starts, startOverride, and endnote numbering.

Tests:
- Use deterministic formatter tests at the maximum accepted marker size and just beyond it, including u32::MAX, without allocating the oversized string.
- Add integration fixtures with small Chicago list starts/startOverride and endnote numStart that exceed the output budget; assert bounded refusal.

Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap. The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded. Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable. Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed. The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace. The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts. fn notes_part_names(pkg: &PartFs) -> (String, String) {
```rust
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "word/document.xml".to_string());
    let mut fn_p = "word/footnotes.xml".to_string();
    let mut en_p = "word/endnotes.xml".to_string();
    if let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(&main) {
        for r in &rels.items {
            if r.target_mode.as_deref() == Some("External") {
                continue;
            }
            match r.rel_type.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or("") {
                "footnotes" => fn_p = pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &r.target),
                "endnotes" => en_p = pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &r.target),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
```

**Revision transformation parser** — `src/revision_processor.rs:3732-3748`

process_part independently parses selected XML unchecked.

```rust
fn process_part<F>(pkg: &mut crate::opc::PartFs, part: &str, f: F)
where
    F: FnOnce(&mut Dom, NodeId) -> Option<NodeId>,
{
    let Some(xml) = pkg.part_string(part) else {
        return;
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let Some(root) = dom.root(doc) else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(new_root) = f(&mut dom, root) else {
        return;
    };
    dom.replace_with(root, &[new_root]);
    pkg.set_part(part, dom.serialize_document(doc).into_bytes());
```

```
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;

    let table = font_table::load_font_table(&pkg);
    let mut embedded = font_table::load_embedded_fonts(&pkg, &table);
```

```
fn existing_comment_ids(opened: &Opened) -> Option<u32> {

            dom.attribute(c, &W::id())
                .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u32>().ok())
        })
```

```
/// A main-document part found the OPC way, by relationship type
/// (`…/relationships/<kind>`, transitional or strict), falling back to
/// Word's conventional name. Other producers may name these parts freely.
pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
    let suffix = format!("/{kind}");
    pkg.main_document_part()
        .and_then(|main| {
            let rel = pkg.read_rels_for(&main)?.items.iter().find(|r| {
                r.rel_type.ends_with(&suffix) && r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
            })?;
            Some(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &rel.target))
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback.to_string())
}

fn settings_part(pkg: &PartFs) -> String {
    main_rel_part(pkg, "settings", "word/settings.xml")
}
```

**Revision parts selected by relationship type** — `src/revision_processor.rs:3689-3728`

Header/footer/notes/comments/styles relationships select arbitrary safe target names without requiring XML suffixes.

```rust
pub(crate) fn revision_bearing_parts(pkg: &crate::opc::PartFs) -> Vec<(String, bool)> {
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "word/document.xml".to_string());
    let mut headers = Vec::new();
    let mut footers = Vec::new();
    let mut endnotes = Vec::new();
    let mut footnotes = Vec::new();
    let mut comments = Vec::new();
    let mut styles = Vec::new();
    if let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(&main) {
        for r in &rels.items {
            if r.target_mode.as_deref() == Some("External") {
                continue;
            }
            let bucket = match r.rel_type.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or("") {
                "header" => &mut headers,
                "footer" => &mut footers,
                "endnotes" => &mut endnotes,
                "footnotes" => &mut footnotes,
                "comments" => &mut comments,
                "styles" => &mut styles,
                _ => continue,
            };
            bucket.push(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &r.target));
        }
    }
    let mut out = vec![(main, false)];
    for p in headers
        .into_iter()
        .chain(footers)
        .chain(endnotes)
        .chain(footnotes)
        .chain(comments)
    {
        out.push((p, false));
    }
    for p in styles {
        out.push((p, true));
    }
```

```
/// `word/settings.xml` parsed once per reader; `None` when the part is absent.
fn settings_dom(pkg: &PartFs) -> Option<ParsedSettings> {
    let xml = pkg.part_string(&settings_part(pkg))?;
    settings_dom_xml(&xml)
}

/// A parsed settings part and its root element.
type ParsedSettings = Rc<(Dom, NodeId)>;

/// `xml` parsed, memoised per thread on the text: a conversion asks a dozen
/// settings questions of the same part, and parsing it each time was 11% of
/// a one-page conversion (samply, fixtures_500 0081ba58).
fn settings_dom_xml(xml: &str) -> Option<ParsedSettings> {
    thread_local! {
        static LAST: RefCell<Option<(String, ParsedSettings)>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
    }
    if let Some(hit) = LAST.with_borrow(|last| {
        last.as_ref()
            .filter(|(text, _)| text == xml)
            .map(|(_, parsed)| Rc::clone(parsed))
    }) {
        return Some(hit);
    }
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc)?;
    let parsed = Rc::new((dom, root));
    LAST.set(Some((xml.to_string(), Rc::clone(&parsed))));
```

```
fn part_xml_by_rel_kind(pkg: &PartFs, main: &str, kind: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(main) {
        let exact = format!("/{kind}");
        let by_type = rels.items.iter().filter(|i| i.rel_type.ends_with(&exact));
        let loose = rels
            .items
            .iter()
            .filter(|i| i.rel_type.ends_with(kind) || i.target.contains(kind));
        for item in by_type.chain(loose) {
            let path = pkg.resolve_rel_target(main, &item.target);
            if let Some(xml) = pkg.part_string(&path) {
                return Some(xml);
            }
        }
    }
    pkg.part_string(&format!("word/{kind}.xml"))
```

```
fn main_part<R: Read + std::io::Seek>(
    archive: &ZipArchive<R>,
    kept: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
) -> Result<String, AdmissionError> {
    use AdmissionErrorKind as K;
    let types = kept
        .get("[content_types].xml")
        .ok_or_else(|| AdmissionError::new(K::UnsupportedPackage, "no [Content_Types].xml"))?;
    let from_rels = kept.get("_rels/.rels").and_then(|rels| {
        elements(rels, "Relationship")
            .into_iter()
            .find_map(|attrs| {
                let is_main = attrs
                    .get("Type")
                    .is_some_and(|t| OFFICE_DOCUMENT_REL.contains(&t.as_str()));
                let external = attrs.get("TargetMode").is_some_and(|m| m == "External");
                (is_main && !external)
                    .then(|| {
                        attrs
                            .get("Target")
                            .map(|t| t.trim_start_matches('/').to_string())
                    })
                    .flatten()
            })
    });
    let main = from_rels.unwrap_or_else(|| "word/document.xml".to_string());
    if archive.index_for_name(&main).is_none() {
        return Err(AdmissionError::new(
            K::UnsupportedPackage,
            format!("main document part {main} is missing"),
        ));
    }
    if let Some(content_type) = content_type_of(types, &main)
        && !MAIN_CONTENT_TYPES.contains(&content_type.as_str())
    {
        return Err(AdmissionError::new(
            K::UnsupportedPackage,
            format!("{main} is {content_type}, not a Word document"),
        ));
    }
    Ok(main)
}
```

```rust
/// (`…/relationships/<kind>`, transitional or strict), falling back to
/// Word's conventional name. Other producers may name these parts freely.
pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
    let suffix = format!("/{kind}");
    pkg.main_document_part()
        .and_then(|main| {
            let rel = pkg.read_rels_for(&main)?.items.iter().find(|r| {
                r.rel_type.ends_with(&suffix) && r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
            })?;
            Some(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &rel.target))
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback.to_string())
}
```

```rust
fn part_xml_by_rel_kind(pkg: &PartFs, main: &str, kind: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(main) {
        let exact = format!("/{kind}");
        let by_type = rels.items.iter().filter(|i| i.rel_type.ends_with(&exact));
        let loose = rels
            .items
            .iter()
            .filter(|i| i.rel_type.ends_with(kind) || i.target.contains(kind));
        for item in by_type.chain(loose) {
            let path = pkg.resolve_rel_target(main, &item.target);
            if let Some(xml) = pkg.part_string(&path) {
                return Some(xml);
            }
        }
    }
```

```rust
fn process_part<F>(pkg: &mut crate::opc::PartFs, part: &str, f: F)
where
    F: FnOnce(&mut Dom, NodeId) -> Option<NodeId>,
{
    let Some(xml) = pkg.part_string(part) else {
        return;
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let Some(root) = dom.root(doc) else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(new_root) = f(&mut dom, root) else {
        return;
    };
    dom.replace_with(root, &[new_root]);
    pkg.set_part(part, dom.serialize_document(doc).into_bytes());
```

```
/// A main-document part found the OPC way, by relationship type
/// (`…/relationships/<kind>`, transitional or strict), falling back to
/// Word's conventional name. Other producers may name these parts freely.
pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
    let suffix = format!("/{kind}");
    pkg.main_document_part()
        .and_then(|main| {
            let rel = pkg.read_rels_for(&main)?.items.iter().find(|r| {
                r.rel_type.ends_with(&suffix) && r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
            })?;
            Some(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &rel.target))
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback.to_string())
}

fn settings_part(pkg: &PartFs) -> String {
    main_rel_part(pkg, "settings", "word/settings.xml")
}
```

```rust
pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
    let suffix = format!("/{kind}");
    pkg.main_document_part()
        .and_then(|main| {
            let rel = pkg.read_rels_for(&main)?.items.iter().find(|r| {
                r.rel_type.ends_with(&suffix) && r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
            })?;
            Some(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &rel.target))
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback.to_string())
```

**Settings relationship target is parsed unchecked** — `src/convert/mod.rs:6864-6891`

This concrete auxiliary consumer interprets related package bytes as XML and calls parse_xdocument without applying active limits. A non-XML-suffixed target can bypass the filename-based admission gate.

```
/// `word/settings.xml` parsed once per reader; `None` when the part is absent.
fn settings_dom(pkg: &PartFs) -> Option<ParsedSettings> {
    let xml = pkg.part_string(&settings_part(pkg))?;
    settings_dom_xml(&xml)
}

/// A parsed settings part and its root element.
type ParsedSettings = Rc<(Dom, NodeId)>;

/// `xml` parsed, memoised per thread on the text: a conversion asks a dozen
/// settings questions of the same part, and parsing it each time was 11% of
/// a one-page conversion (samply, fixtures_500 0081ba58).
fn settings_dom_xml(xml: &str) -> Option<ParsedSettings> {
    thread_local! {
        static LAST: RefCell<Option<(String, ParsedSettings)>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
    }
    if let Some(hit) = LAST.with_borrow(|last| {
        last.as_ref()
            .filter(|(text, _)| text == xml)
            .map(|(_, parsed)| Rc::clone(parsed))
    }) {
        return Some(hit);
    }
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc)?;
    let parsed = Rc::new((dom, root));
    LAST.set(Some((xml.to_string(), Rc::clone(&parsed))));
```

```
fn part_xml_by_rel_kind(pkg: &PartFs, main: &str, kind: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(main) {
        let exact = format!("/{kind}");
        let by_type = rels.items.iter().filter(|i| i.rel_type.ends_with(&exact));
        let loose = rels
            .items
            .iter()
            .filter(|i| i.rel_type.ends_with(kind) || i.target.contains(kind));
        for item in by_type.chain(loose) {
            let path = pkg.resolve_rel_target(main, &item.target);
            if let Some(xml) = pkg.part_string(&path) {
                return Some(xml);
            }
        }
    }
    pkg.part_string(&format!("word/{kind}.xml"))
```

**Content-type refusal inspects only the main document** — `src/admission.rs:828-870`

This validates the selected main part's Word content type; it does not reject or XML-scan an auxiliary font-table `.bin` override.

```
fn main_part<R: Read + std::io::Seek>(
    archive: &ZipArchive<R>,
    kept: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
) -> Result<String, AdmissionError> {
    use AdmissionErrorKind as K;
    let types = kept
        .get("[content_types].xml")
        .ok_or_else(|| AdmissionError::new(K::UnsupportedPackage, "no [Content_Types].xml"))?;
    let from_rels = kept.get("_rels/.rels").and_then(|rels| {
        elements(rels, "Relationship")
            .into_iter()
            .find_map(|attrs| {
                let is_main = attrs
                    .get("Type")
                    .is_some_and(|t| OFFICE_DOCUMENT_REL.contains(&t.as_str()));
                let external = attrs.get("TargetMode").is_some_and(|m| m == "External");
                (is_main && !external)
                    .then(|| {
                        attrs
                            .get("Target")
                            .map(|t| t.trim_start_matches('/').to_string())
                    })
                    .flatten()
            })
    });
    let main = from_rels.unwrap_or_else(|| "word/document.xml".to_string());
    if archive.index_for_name(&main).is_none() {
        return Err(AdmissionError::new(
            K::UnsupportedPackage,
            format!("main document part {main} is missing"),
        ));
    }
    if let Some(content_type) = content_type_of(types, &main)
        && !MAIN_CONTENT_TYPES.contains(&content_type.as_str())
    {
        return Err(AdmissionError::new(
            K::UnsupportedPackage,
            format!("{main} is {content_type}, not a Word document"),
        ));
    }
    Ok(main)
}
```

```rust
        .part_string(&main)
```

```rust
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {

        xml

    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

**Auxiliary targets may use arbitrary part names** — `src/convert/mod.rs:21308-21320`

A main-document relationship selects its auxiliary target regardless of filename extension; the resolved package name reaches the font-table XML consumer.

```rust
/// (`…/relationships/<kind>`, transitional or strict), falling back to
/// Word's conventional name. Other producers may name these parts freely.
pub(crate) fn main_rel_part(pkg: &PartFs, kind: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
    let suffix = format!("/{kind}");
    pkg.main_document_part()
        .and_then(|main| {
            let rel = pkg.read_rels_for(&main)?.items.iter().find(|r| {
                r.rel_type.ends_with(&suffix) && r.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
            })?;
            Some(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &rel.target))
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback.to_string())
}
```

#### Dataflow

DOCX auxiliary bytes and internal relationship target -\> suffix-only admission drains/counts bytes -\> normalized bounded PartFs -\> main_rel_part(theme/styles/numbering), part_xml_by_rel_kind(comments/notes), or header/footer target resolution -\> unchecked auxiliary parse_xdocument -\> unbounded recursive parse_element. The comment-thread consumer also reads commentsExtended through part_xml_by_rel_kind and parses it at :7688-7689; the relationship helper's fallback to word/{kind}.xml does not constrain a supplied renamed relationship target. DOCX bytes → admit suffix gate → PartFs → notes_part_names relationship target → unchecked notes DOM parse → recursive parse_element. Attacker package footnotes/endnotes relationship targets notes.dat -\> admission drains it as binary -\> get_revisions resolves authoritative relationship -\> pkg.part_string -\> permissive parse_xdocument -\> unchecked recursive parse_element. Comparison pre_process_markup resolves internal styles, notes and charts independent of extension and raw-parses the selected strings. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Attacker DOCX -\> valid main/relationships -\> auxiliary XML under .bin or another non-.xml/.rels name -\> suffix-based admission skips depth/tag policy -\> relationship-selected notes/header/footer -\> raw parse_xdocument -\> recursive parse_element -\> stack exhaustion.

- **Source:** Document supplier controls package names, relationships and auxiliary XML bytes.

- **Sink:** Parser::parse_element recursive call

- **Outcome:** Rendering process or WASM instance terminates from stack exhaustion.

```rust
fn notes_part_names(pkg: &PartFs) -> (String, String) {
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "word/document.xml".to_string());
    let mut fn_p = "word/footnotes.xml".to_string();
    let mut en_p = "word/endnotes.xml".to_string();
    if let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(&main) {
        for r in &rels.items {
            if r.target_mode.as_deref() == Some("External") {
                continue;
            }
            match r.rel_type.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or("") {
                "footnotes" => fn_p = pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &r.target),
                "endnotes" => en_p = pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &r.target),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    (fn_p, en_p)
```

```rust
fn part_xml_by_rel_kind(pkg: &PartFs, main: &str, kind: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(main) {
        let exact = format!("/{kind}");
        let by_type = rels.items.iter().filter(|i| i.rel_type.ends_with(&exact));
        let loose = rels
            .items
            .iter()
            .filter(|i| i.rel_type.ends_with(kind) || i.target.contains(kind));
        for item in by_type.chain(loose) {
            let path = pkg.resolve_rel_target(main, &item.target);
            if let Some(xml) = pkg.part_string(&path) {
                return Some(xml);
            }
        }
    }
```

#### Reachability

An untrusted document author controls auxiliary bytes and relationship targets. Default public rendering and enabled Rust/Python/WASM/CLI callers suffice; no local file/shell authority or privileged configuration is needed. The attacker controls document bytes processed by the public library/bindings; no network service exposure is assumed. Host availability is affected when the consumer processes the supplied document. Public document_comparer::get_revisions and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions accept these bytes. pre_process_markup is a second consumer of the same missing XML admission control. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Public PDF/PNG/render-report APIs and nonidentical document comparison process attacker-controlled auxiliary relationships after ordinary admission. No special configuration or note reference is needed for comparison's auxiliary parse.

- **Attacker:** Author of an untrusted document processed by a victim untrusted document supplier Supplier of untrusted input processed by a library consumer Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Document author controlling package part names, relationships and auxiliary XML.

- **Entry point:** convert::docx_to_pdf / render / PNG conversion and shared enabled bindings/CLI callers document_comparer::get_revisions and comparison notes parsing

- **Outcome:** Stack exhaustion/process termination or WASM trap

Preconditions:
- Victim processes attacker-controlled DOCX through the converter.
- Victim processes attacker-supplied DOCX with rendering/layout.
- Victim invokes the affected public API with attacker-controlled document input.
- Victim compares or renders attacker-controlled DOCX with a relationship-selected renamed auxiliary XML part.

Existing controls:
- Ordinary suffixes and checked parsing paths are protected; no special raised limits are needed for this alternate name.

Limitations:
- No code execution, data theft or remote deployment is established.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.

Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Stack exhaustion and availability loss of the caller process. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Processing host stack overflow/process termination.
- **Why:** Processing process can terminate; availability of other work depends on embedding. Availability of the hosting process or WASM instance.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** No privileged setting is required; only attacker-authored document processing. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Normal library input boundary with compact deeply nested XML and no unusual configuration.
- **Why:** Part naming and relationship values are document-controlled; no special option is needed. Direct public document-input boundary with no optional feature required.

#### Summary

The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its XML leak branch uses lossy UTF-8 and misses the retained copy, which a recipient can recover after sharing. Even the scanner's no-root fallback searches the already lossily decoded string, so it cannot recover a multi-character value split by UTF-16 NUL bytes.

#### Root Cause

Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes. The standalone leaks API and both prepared artifacts use this same branch; ordinary Transitional input does not require Strict normalization to rewrite the untouched auxiliary part. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `check_redactions()` relies on `scrub::leaks()` to detect retained text in both output packages. The scanner chooses its XML branch by suffix and lossy-decodes as UTF-8; its UTF-16LE raw-byte search runs only for non-XML. BOM-prefixed UTF-16 XML is accepted by admission but its NUL-separated characters evade the scan. The no-root fallback returns xml.contains(needle) after incompatible decoding rather than searching the original bytes; non-XML UTF-16LE test coverage exercises a different branch.

```rust
    fn check_redactions(&self, outputs: &[&[u8]]) -> Result<(), EditError> {
        for (op, operation) in self.plan.operations.iter().enumerate() {
            let OperationKind::Redact { find, .. } = &operation.kind else {
                continue;

            let parts: std::collections::BTreeSet<String> = outputs
                .iter()
                .flat_map(|doc| crate::scrub::leaks(doc, find))
                .collect();
            if parts.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let message = format!(
                "the redacted text still occurs in {}; redact every copy in the same plan, or remove the comment or part that holds it",
                parts.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
            );
            let mut error = self.conflict(op, &message);
```

```rust
/// Word opens it, so it is transcoded; other bytes decode lossily, as the
/// rest of the engine reads them.
fn part_text(xml: &[u8]) -> Cow<'_, str> {
    let utf16 = |rest: &[u8], unit: fn([u8; 2]) -> u16| {
        let units = rest.as_chunks::<2>().0.iter().map(|&pair| unit(pair));

                .collect(),
        )
    };

        [0xFF, 0xFE, rest @ ..] => utf16(rest, u16::from_le_bytes),
```

An ordinary multi-character secret in BOM UTF16LE/BE customXml survives raw package storage and serialization. UTF8-lossy decoding produces replacement/NUL-interleaved text; xml_holds either has no root and uses a UTF8 substring check or cannot match decoded ordinary text. Both final artifacts are checked with that same routine. Existing malformed-XML validation findings are baseline, not automatically introduced failures. Additional validated trace follows public edit preparation into both serialized artifacts, unchanged auxiliary bytes and xml_holds fallback. Ordinary Transitional main XML avoids normalization rewriting the auxiliary UTF-16 copy. Both LE/BE supported encodings and the standalone leaks API share the missing XML decoding control. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected admission.rs764-792 BOM decoding, strict_translation.rs769-837 zero-change/raw preservation, PartFs raw insertion, edit.rs5381-5424 untouched-part serialization and final scanner. An ASCII secret duplicated inside a valid BOM UTF16LE/BE customXml XML text node remains extractable in clean output while UTF8-lossy XML scanning cannot match it. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified admission's UTF-16LE/BE decoding and existing customXml admission test, output serialization preserving untouched parts, and both check_redactions call sites in prepared::produce. A body redaction can succeed while a same-text UTF-16 customXml/item1.xml remains recoverable. Source baseline validation reports do not automatically block unchanged source findings. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): BOM UTF16LE/BE XML is supported by admission. In a normal .xml entry, ASCII needle characters are separated by NUL bytes and cannot match in lossy UTF8. xml_holds cannot recover the XML and its fallback still misses the contiguous needle. strict translation's zero-churn path preserves such data, and PartFs::to_zip writes untouched parts unchanged. Custom XML is outside the edited story, so a copied secret can remain while visible text is redacted and check_redactions returns success.

Validation method: Preserved already-validated Standard source evidence and assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

```rust
            );
```

```
/// A part's text for scanning. Word writes UTF-8, but a part may be UTF-16
/// with a byte-order mark (SharePoint's `customXml` items often are) and
/// Word opens it, so it is transcoded; other bytes decode lossily, as the
/// rest of the engine reads them.
fn part_text(xml: &[u8]) -> Cow<'_, str> {
    let utf16 = |rest: &[u8], unit: fn([u8; 2]) -> u16| {
        let units = rest.as_chunks::<2>().0.iter().map(|&pair| unit(pair));
        Cow::Owned(
            char::decode_utf16(units)
                .map(|c| c.unwrap_or(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER))
                .collect(),
        )
    };
    match xml {
        [0xFF, 0xFE, rest @ ..] => utf16(rest, u16::from_le_bytes),
        [0xFE, 0xFF, rest @ ..] => utf16(rest, u16::from_be_bytes),
        _ => String::from_utf8_lossy(xml),
    }
```

### [43] Decoded relationship ampersands trigger quadratic target resolution

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Independent parent source review verified the input, transformations, effective controls and exact allocation/iteration/recursive operation. No runtime reproduction or platform-specific failure threshold was measured. |
| Category | Algorithmic complexity |
| CWE | CWE-407 |
| Affected lines | src/opc/mod.rs:222-235, src/opc/mod.rs:677-682, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:764-789, src/inspect.rs:766-776 |

#### Summary

A valid relationship Target containing N repeated &amp; values is decoded into N literal ampersands during metadata parsing. PartFs::resolve_rel_target decodes it again; unescape_xml_text searches the remaining suffix for a semicolon at every ampersand, causing about N(N-1)/2 probes before checking whether the target part exists.

#### Root Cause

An already decoded relationship target is decoded twice, and the permissive entity helper rescans the full remaining suffix after every unsuccessful ampersand.

**entity loop** — `src/xmllinq/parse.rs:764-789`

Valid .rels Target=&amp;... -\> oxml_opc Relationships::from_xml decoded Target -\> PartFs::resolve_rel_target -\> unescape_xml_text -\> repeated suffix searches. inspect::related and document_comparer note resolution consume the target before part lookup. This excerpt establishes entity loop.

```
pub fn unescape_xml_text(s: &str) -> String {
    if !s.contains('&') {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < chars.len() {
        if chars[i] == '&' {
            // find ';'
            if let Some(semi_rel) = chars[i + 1..].iter().position(|&c| c == ';') {
                let body: String = chars[i + 1..i + 1 + semi_rel].iter().collect();
                if let Some(decoded) = decode_entity(&body) {
                    out.push_str(&decoded);
                    i = i + 1 + semi_rel + 1;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            out.push('&');
            i += 1;
        } else {
            out.push(chars[i]);
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
```
