#### Summary

Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies an additional static eight-byte TEXTOUT framing with a 65535-byte claimed string and overlapping following bytes. About 1 MiB can request multiple gigabytes of retained text; valid whole-file reads, nonblank text and nonzero mapping extents remain required. No out-of-bounds memory read is asserted.

#### Root Cause

raster_wmf checks declared size\*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable. With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification. A seven-word EXTTEXTOUT record contains its six-byte header and eight-byte fixed fields but can start its 65535-byte text range at the next record, because only whole-file bounds are checked. Assigned discovery-0016 adds a same-function-header proof: repeated six-byte size=3/0x0A32 headers cause count at off+10 to read the next function (2610), options at off+12 to read size (3), and optional-rectangle text to start at off+22. Nonzero mapping extents, nonblank bytes and sufficient trailing data retain overlapping Strings; roughly 6 MB of records request about 2.6 GB of strings. These are source-derived estimates. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Text record handlers do not constrain field/string reads to the declared record extent, allowing small records to repeatedly materialize overlapping bytes as owned strings. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies an additional static eight-byte TEXTOUT framing with a 65535-byte claimed string and overlapping following bytes. About 1 MiB can request multiple gigabytes of retained text; valid whole-file reads, nonblank text and nonzero mapping extents remain required. No out-of-bounds memory read is asserted.

**EMF points are confined to record extent** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:1061-1082`

The sibling parser demonstrates the missing WMF boundary. Supplied discovery-0029 corroboration: The sibling EMF helper restricts point spans to each record end.

```rust
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
        }
    }
    Some(pts)
```

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

```rust
/// Windows-1252 text, one byte a character.
fn ansi_text(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    const HIGH: [char; 32] = [
        '€', '\u{81}', '‚', 'ƒ', '„', '…', '†', '‡', 'ˆ', '‰', 'Š', '‹', 'Œ', '\u{8d}', 'Ž',
        '\u{8f}', '\u{90}', '‘', '’', '“', '”', '•', '–', '—', '˜', '™', 'š', '›', 'œ', '\u{9d}',
        'ž', 'Ÿ',
    ];
    bytes
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| match b {
            0x80..=0x9F => HIGH[usize::from(b - 0x80)],
            _ => char::from(b),
        })
        .collect()
```

```rust
fn decode_image(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Option<ImageKind> {
    if let Some((width, height, rgb, texts)) = metafile::render(&bytes) {
```
```
        let raster = ImageKind::Rgb {
```
```rust
            width,
            height,
            bytes: rgb,
            alpha: None,
        };
        if texts.is_empty() {
            return Some(raster);
        }
        return Some(ImageKind::Metafile {
            raster: Box::new(raster),
            texts: texts.into(),
        });
```

```
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
```

**Text conversion retains copied string** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:692-718`

Every supplied text payload is decoded into a new string and retained in `MetaText`; a missing font does not reject it.

```rust
fn wmf_text(dc: &WmfState, map: &Map, x: i16, y: i16, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<MetaText> {
    let text = ansi_text(bytes);
    if text.trim().is_empty() || map.ext_x.abs() < f32::EPSILON || map.ext_y.abs() < f32::EPSILON {
        return None;
    }
    let font = dc.font.as_deref();
    let height = font.map_or(0, |f| f.height);
    Some(MetaText {
        text,
        x: (f32::from(x) - map.org_x) / map.ext_x,
        y: (f32::from(y) - map.org_y) / map.ext_y,
        // lfHeight 0 is the default font, 12pt at 96 dpi of a 1440 inch.
        size: if height == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            f32::from(height.unsigned_abs()) / map.ext_y.abs()
        },
        cell: height > 0,
        family: font.map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.face.clone()),
        bold: font.is_some_and(|f| f.weight >= 600),
        italic: font.is_some_and(|f| f.italic),
        color: dc.text_color,
        align: dc.text_align,
        aspect: (map.ext_x / map.ext_y).abs(),
    })
}

```

**Sibling EMF code enforces record-local bound** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:1061-1083`

The sibling EMF reader checks coordinate bytes against the current record end, demonstrating a record-local bound absent from WMF.

```rust
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
        }
    }
    Some(pts)
}
```

```rust
/// # Errors
///

pub fn docx_to_pdf_report(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<ConvertedPdf, ConvertError> {

        pdf: result?,
        font_report,
    })
}

    with_options(options, || docx_to_pdf_body(docx, options))
}

fn docx_to_pdf_body(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
```

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

```rust
fn ansi_text(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    const HIGH: [char; 32] = [
        '€', '\u{81}', '‚', 'ƒ', '„', '…', '†', '‡', 'ˆ', '‰', 'Š', '‹', 'Œ', '\u{8d}', 'Ž',
        '\u{8f}', '\u{90}', '‘', '’', '“', '”', '•', '–', '—', '˜', '™', 'š', '›', 'œ', '\u{9d}',
        'ž', 'Ÿ',
    ];
    bytes
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| match b {
            0x80..=0x9F => HIGH[usize::from(b - 0x80)],
            _ => char::from(b),
        })
        .collect()
```

```rust
fn wmf_text(dc: &WmfState, map: &Map, x: i16, y: i16, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<MetaText> {
    let text = ansi_text(bytes);
    if text.trim().is_empty() || map.ext_x.abs() < f32::EPSILON || map.ext_y.abs() < f32::EPSILON {
        return None;
    }
    let font = dc.font.as_deref();
    let height = font.map_or(0, |f| f.height);
    Some(MetaText {
        text,
        x: (f32::from(x) - map.org_x) / map.ext_x,
        y: (f32::from(y) - map.org_y) / map.ext_y,
        // lfHeight 0 is the default font, 12pt at 96 dpi of a 1440 inch.
        size: if height == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            f32::from(height.unsigned_abs()) / map.ext_y.abs()
        },
        cell: height > 0,
        family: font.map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.face.clone()),
        bold: font.is_some_and(|f| f.weight >= 600),
        italic: font.is_some_and(|f| f.italic),
        color: dc.text_color,
        align: dc.text_align,
        aspect: (map.ext_x / map.ext_y).abs(),
```

```rust
fn decode_image(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Option<ImageKind> {
    if let Some((width, height, rgb, texts)) = metafile::render(&bytes) {
        let raster = ImageKind::Rgb {
            width,
            height,
            bytes: rgb,
            alpha: None,
        };

            return Some(raster);

            raster: Box::new(raster),

        });
```

```rust
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;

            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;

            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
```

```
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
```

**Text conversion retains copied string** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:692-718`

Every supplied text payload is decoded into a new string and retained in `MetaText`; a missing font does not reject it.

```rust
fn wmf_text(dc: &WmfState, map: &Map, x: i16, y: i16, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<MetaText> {
    let text = ansi_text(bytes);
    if text.trim().is_empty() || map.ext_x.abs() < f32::EPSILON || map.ext_y.abs() < f32::EPSILON {
        return None;
    }
    let font = dc.font.as_deref();
    let height = font.map_or(0, |f| f.height);
    Some(MetaText {
        text,
        x: (f32::from(x) - map.org_x) / map.ext_x,
        y: (f32::from(y) - map.org_y) / map.ext_y,
        // lfHeight 0 is the default font, 12pt at 96 dpi of a 1440 inch.
        size: if height == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            f32::from(height.unsigned_abs()) / map.ext_y.abs()
        },
        cell: height > 0,
        family: font.map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.face.clone()),
        bold: font.is_some_and(|f| f.weight >= 600),
        italic: font.is_some_and(|f| f.italic),
        color: dc.text_color,
        align: dc.text_align,
        aspect: (map.ext_x / map.ext_y).abs(),
    })
}

```

**Sibling EMF code enforces record-local bound** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:1061-1083`

The sibling EMF reader checks coordinate bytes against the current record end, demonstrating a record-local bound absent from WMF.

```rust
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
        }
    }
    Some(pts)
}
```

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- MAX_SIDE=384 bounds raster dimensions; it does not restrict how often subsequent bytes are parsed.
- Safe slice reads eventually reject truncation, after earlier records have already performed amplified work.
- EMF read_emf_points has record-end bounds; it does not protect the WMF handlers.
- Whole-buffer slice checks prevent Rust memory unsafety; this is parser resource amplification.
- WMF object count is clamped and canvas MAX_SIDE is 384, but neither controls the texts vector.
- Valid record-local counts would consume input proportionally and would not produce this overlap.
- Canvas dimensions are capped at 384 per side and hostile coordinates are clipped; these controls do not bound retained strings.
- Record size must be at least three words and the cursor advances, preventing a zero-length infinite loop.
- Whole-file Rust slice bounds avoid arbitrary memory reads; the finding concerns invalid record extents and resource amplification.
- ZIP admission charges original media bytes rather than repeated decoding of overlapping record suffixes.
- Input compressed/inflated limits remain, but do not charge repeatedly allocated text.
- Canvas max384side constrains pixels, not texts.
- Image decoder default512MiB limit is later than metafile processing.
- Caller CPU/memory containment policy limits deployment impact.
- WMF canvas side is capped at 384 and record size arithmetic is checked; neither bounds retained strings.
- InputLimits bounds compressed/inflated package bytes and XML depth, not WMF logical text.
- An operator's process limits can contain impact; no production deployment was established.
- Checked outer multiplication and file bounds prevent file-offset wrap, but not cross-record payload consumption.
- Canvas capped at384 pixels/side, strokes clipped and arithmetic widened; text and repeated geometry remain unbounded by record size.
- EMF read_emf_points uses per-record bounds; finding limited to WMF.
- Archive budgets/process limits do not bound overlapping interpretations.
- Canvas sides are capped at384 and stroke lines are clipped; those do not cap counted string/point decoding.
- Counts are u16-bounded individually, but can be repeated many times against shared suffix data.
- Archive inflation limits bound original media bytes only.
- No out-of-bounds memory access or code execution is claimed.
- checked_mul prevents size/iterator wrap, not cross-record reads.
- Each n is u16-bounded; multiplicative aggregate retention remains.
- 384-pixel canvas cap and stroke clipping do not limit texts.
- Sibling EMF point parsing uses record bounds; this finding concerns the two WMF text branches.
- Checked multiplication bounds outer offset progression; this is not an out-of-buffer read.
- Canvas dimensions are capped at 384, but text storage is separate.
- ZIP admission bounds original media bytes, not overlapping text-copy work.
- All reads remain within the file buffer, so this is not an out-of-bounds memory-read finding.
- Record size arithmetic is checked and object count/raster dimensions are bounded.
- Blank strings or degenerate extents are skipped; a nondegenerate metafile with nonblank bytes reaches retention.
- All reads remain within the whole input slice, so no out-of-bounds memory disclosure is claimed.
- Canvas dimensions are capped at 384 and line endpoints are clipped; these protect raster work but do not bound copied text or cross-record point decoding.
- Original archive entry bytes remain bounded; the vulnerable amplification occurs after inflation.
- No EMF record-boundary flaw is claimed.
- WMF/EMF raster dimensions are capped at 384 pixels per side, and line/polygon painting clips coordinates to the canvas.
- Checked multiplication prevents WMF record-size overflow on wasm32.
- The sibling EMF read_emf_points helper checks point reads against off + size; that control is absent from the affected WMF operations.
- Input admission and image crate decoder limits do not inspect or constrain these internal WMF text allocations.
- Caller process resource limits can contain availability impact. No runtime reproduction was executed.
- Reads are within the media buffer; no out-of-bounds memory access is asserted.
- MAX_SIDE=384, clipping and bounded object slots limit canvases/state, not retained strings or repeated payload interpretation.

```rust
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {

            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;

        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
        }
```

#### Reachability

Victim renders a DOCX referencing attacker-controlled placeable WMF bytes. The attacker controls embedded media in a document consumed by the renderer, with no release credentials or nondefault configuration. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Public DOCX rendering decodes embedded WMF bytes from the package. A document author controls the record sizes and later bytes without needing host filesystem or release authority.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author untrusted document supplier Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: An untrusted document/image author.

- **Entry point:** Public PDF/PNG renderer convert public rendering APIs

- **Outcome:** Excessive allocation/work and host-process or WASM instance failure

Preconditions:
- Victim renders a DOCX referencing attacker-controlled placeable WMF bytes.
- Victim renders a DOCX containing a WMF with nondegenerate bounds and malformed text records.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.

Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Process memory exhaustion or termination.
- **Why:** Host processing availability can be lost; no confidentiality or code-execution gain is established. Host/instance availability loss.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Compact malformed records are accepted on ordinary embedded-image rendering paths.
- **Why:** A document supplier controls the triggering parser inputs with no privileged configuration. Malformed binary counts reach a built-in parser directly and bypass otherwise bounded stored input.

#### Remediation

Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

Tests:
- Short WMF polygon, polypolygon and polyline records claiming following-record points must refuse before processing points.
- Repeated malformed records must consume work proportional to declared bytes, with EMF behavior retained.
- Deterministic parser tests with short declared records and text counts extending into the next record must refuse safely.
- Cover EXTTEXTOUT options/rectangle, TEXTOUT padding and record-local geometry counts with small resource budgets.
- Reject EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT strings extending into the next record.
- Reject cross-record polygon/polypolygon/polyline coordinates and validate large valid records within aggregate text/geometry budgets.
- Use existing in-memory WMF fixtures to ensure six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT cannot read subsequent records.
- Verify repeated undersized records produce no retained text.
- Retain valid text rendering tests and exercise cumulative text-budget refusal.
- Small malformed EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT records must be rejected without reading following bytes.
- Repeated short records must remain within deterministic cumulative allocation/work limits.
- Verify valid WMF text still renders through public PDF/PNG APIs.
- Exercise short TEXTOUT, EXTTEXTOUT, POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE records with sufficient trailing bytes; require refusal without consuming the next record.
- Refuse textout/exttextout/polygon/polypolygon/polyline counts extending beyond their record despite sufficient following file bytes.
- Verify repeated small records cannot amplify trailing content into unbounded retained output.
- Refuse EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT whose counts or coordinate fields extend past their own record even when still inside the file.
- Ensure many valid records hit a bounded aggregate text budget and ordinary WMF text stays supported.
- Reject header-only TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT records even when later file bytes can satisfy their reads.
- Bound aggregate extracted text and test valid records exactly at declared boundaries.
- Exercise undersized text records using small harmless limits and assert refusal without reading following-record bytes.
- Verify aggregate text budgets and normal EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records; avoid allocating attacker-sized outputs.
- Undersized TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT refuses before text retention.
- POLYGON/POLYPOLYGON/POLYLINE counts cannot consume following records.
- Valid WMF and EMF rendering remains supported.
- Reject text counts extending beyond EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT record end even when bytes remain in the file.
- Reject polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts extending beyond their records.
- Verify repeated short records cannot copy overlapping trailing bytes into retained text.
- Keep valid WMF rendering and existing extreme-coordinate/record-size tests.
- Assert EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT counts beyond record end are refused even if the file has sufficient trailing bytes.
- Exercise polygon/polypolygon/polyline/font records with truncated declared payloads.
- Assert repeated small records cannot create decoded-text output disproportionate to valid payload bytes.
- Short TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT and geometry records whose counts extend into the next record must be rejected before copying or iteration.
- Reject short WMF records whose text or point counts reach into following otherwise valid records.
- Verify bounded decoded text across repeated EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT records.

Preventive controls:
- Bound the actual representation depth and processing work at the consuming boundary.
- Pass bounded record slices to all metafile handlers instead of exposing the entire backing file.

<a id="finding-45"></a>

### [45] Repeated HTML chunk references bypass conversion memory budgets

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent inspected admission order, relationship load, raw HTML acceptance, per-reference conversion and unlimited output append; no runtime reproduction. |
| Category | Unbounded post-admission document expansion Unbounded logical document expansion |
| CWE | CWE-409, CWE-770 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/altchunk.rs:15-43, src/convert/mod.rs:773-800, src/convert/mod.rs:773-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:15-40, src/convert/mod.rs:790-798, src/admission.rs:520-554 |

#### Summary

A DOCX can repeatedly reference one modest HTML part. The renderer admits the small original package, then copies and converts that chunk separately for every reference and concatenates all generated XML. The resulting allocation and work can exceed package budgets by orders of magnitude. For example, 10,000 short references to one 1 MiB ordinary HTML paragraph can imply roughly 10 GiB of generated XML; this is a static estimate, not a runtime measurement.

#### Root Cause

`with_layout` admits only the original ZIP. `altchunk::expand` treats each reference independently, reloads the same bytes, rebuilds its HTML as WML and appends the result to one String, without a reference/output budget. The package's original bytes and entries therefore do not bound its expanded representation. Each internal chunk occurrence adds its full converted content without cumulative import accounting. The original package-size budget applies to stored parts once, not their potentially multiplicative logical reuse. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Resource admission charges each physical package part once, but the embedded-content transformation can repeatedly materialize that part without charging generated bytes or structural work.

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

Verified a standard self-closing `w:altChunk r:id` form is repeatedly matched, the same existing internal relationship may be used each time, and normal HTML paragraphs can supply the repeated body. For example, thousands of small references to a roughly megabyte HTML body imply gigabytes of expanded XML although the package stores that body once. Conversion-result caching alone would not bound the accumulated String. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified expand (15-44), chunk loading/decoding, importer emission, original admission (admission.rs:516-554), with_layout ordering (mod.rs:773-798) and in-memory relationship lookup. A single text-rich 1MiB HTML chunk referenced 4096 times yields more than 4GiB generated XML without approaching original inflated-byte limits.

```rust
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
```

**chunk repeat** — `src/convert/altchunk.rs:15-43`

Each repeated altChunk is independently loaded and converted, and its entire WML result is appended to a growing output string without cumulative accounting.

```rust
pub(crate) fn expand(xml: &str, load: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(xml.len());
    let mut rest = xml;
    while let Some(at) = rest.find("<w:altChunk") {
        out.push_str(&rest[..at]);
        let tail = &rest[at..];
        let Some(open_end) = tail.find('>') else {
            // The prefix has already been copied; retain only the unfinished
            // chunk suffix when this diagnostic input cannot be expanded.
            out.push_str(tail);
            return out;
        };
        let open = &tail[..=open_end];
        let end = if open.ends_with("/>") {
            open_end + 1
        } else {
            tail.find("</w:altChunk>")
                .map_or(open_end + 1, |i| i + "</w:altChunk>".len())
        };
        let wml = attr(open, "id")
            .and_then(|rid| load(&rid))
            .and_then(|bytes| chunk_html(&bytes))
            .map(|html| html_to_wml(&html))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        out.push_str(&wml);
        rest = &tail[end..];
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
```

- Original ZIP budget, XML depth and entry limits remain effective on stored input but not the derived repeated string.
- This path needs no oversized table span and survives a per-span fix.
- ZIP inflated-byte and entry limits bound original package storage.
- No recursive altChunk expansion is required; ordinary repeated references suffice.
- The HTML conversion can operate on an internal part; no external retrieval is performed.
- Archive entry and inflated bytes are bounded before expansion.
- Only package part bytes are loaded, so this does not establish network or arbitrary file access.
- Repeated tags may reuse the same relationship; no duplicate archive part/relationship is required.
- Process memory/CPU limits mitigate host-wide impact; they do not bound generated XML.

Limitations:
- No dynamic reproduction or memory measurement; exact failure depends on platform and external resource limits.
- No dynamic reproduction or deployment-specific impact was measured.
- No runtime triggering input or deployed service verified.

#### Dataflow

Admitted original DOCX → repeated same-rId altChunk lookup → repeated HTML-to-WML conversion → out.push_str per reference → oversized DOM/layout. Untrusted document.xml repeats one internal chunk rid -\> with_layout admits original bytes -\> expand reloads and converts the same part per occurrence -\> out.push_str accumulates all copies -\> permissive DOM parse.

```rust
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)

        xml
    };

    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
```

#### Reachability

Document suppliers control both reference multiplicity and internal HTML content through the ordinary public renderer boundary. Public Rust render/PDF conversion APIs and their Python/WASM wrappers reach the same post-admission importer with default settings.

- **Attacker:** untrusted document supplier Supplier of untrusted input processed by a library consumer

- **Entry point:** convert public PDF/PNG/render/layout APIs

- **Outcome:** Memory or CPU exhaustion of the embedding process/instance

Preconditions:
- Victim invokes the affected public API with attacker-controlled document input.

Existing controls:
- Original package byte and XML-depth limits remain effective on physical input; external process limits can contain host-wide impact.

#### Severity

**Medium** — An untrusted document supplier can choose many tiny references and one ordinary HTML part that fit original byte/depth/entry limits. The direct outcome is memory/CPU exhaustion in the embedding process or WASM instance. No service deployment is assumed; process isolation limits collateral impact.

Shared unsandboxed upload processing increases impact; a cumulative expanded-byte/node budget enforced before append removes this path.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Availability loss.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** No optional configuration, large source input, or invalid HTML required.

#### Remediation

Make altChunk expansion fallible under active cumulative expanded-byte, node/element, depth, work and occurrence budgets. Check contributions before conversion/allocation/append, including repeated internal relationships and MIME-decoded chunks, and validate generated XML under active limits before DOM construction. Caching may reduce repeated conversion CPU but cannot replace the total-output budget.

Tests:
- Use small explicit expansion limits to test repeated references to one ordinary HTML part at and above the budget.
- Test distinct chunk parts and MIME-decoded chunks share the same cumulative budget.
- Use multiple references to one modest internal HTML part and a small expansion budget; assert refusal before cumulative growth.
- Verify normal repeated references and inclusive budget boundaries.

### [46] Rendering an admitted DOCX can retain gigabytes of duplicate embedded fonts

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent review confirms unconditional loading, bytes.to_vec() per alias and distinct retained map entries. Exact exhaustion thresholds were not executed. |
| Category | Unbounded expansion of shared embedded resources |
| CWE | CWE-409, CWE-400, CWE-789 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/font_table.rs:220-228, src/convert/font_table.rs:179-180, src/convert/mod.rs:806-807, src/convert/font.rs:1449, src/convert/font_table.rs:179-193, src/convert/font_table.rs:205-231, src/convert/mod.rs:806-809, src/convert/font.rs:1445-1449, src/convert/font.rs:1472-1477, src/convert/font.rs:1496-1504, src/convert/font_table.rs:205-231, src/convert/font_table.rs:179-193, src/convert/font_table.rs:82-125, src/convert/mod.rs:806-810, src/convert/font_table.rs:177-193, src/convert/mod.rs:806-808, src/convert/font_table.rs:70-81, src/convert/font_table.rs:205-232, src/convert/font_table.rs:179-195, src/convert/font.rs:1470-1478, src/convert/font_table.rs:205-231, src/convert/mod.rs:806-809, src/convert/font_table.rs:100-110 |

#### Summary

Distinct font-table aliases may all reference one embedded font part. Rendering eagerly loads every alias, copies the full font and retains a separate buffer for each name, multiplying a small admitted package into gigabytes of memory even if its body never uses those fonts.

#### Root Cause

`parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies. Fonts::for_document subsequently visits every retained alias; its later u16 face-index conversion does not prevent already retained per-alias payload copies. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A physical resource charged once by package admission is decoded and cloned into independent Arc allocations per attacker-chosen family/style alias without aggregate accounting. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` loads the whole font table before collecting used names. For every unknown family/style, `load_embedded_fonts()` resolves the part, copies/deobfuscates its entire bytes, validates it and inserts a new retained allocation. Aliases sharing a target have no deduplication or aggregate byte cap.

#### Validation

A valid ordinary font can be referenced by thousands of differently named `w:font` rows using the same `r:id`. The names need not occur in runs. Unknown family names bypass the installed-catalogue optimization and valid font parsing succeeds for every copy. Ten thousand aliases of an approximately 320 KB font request roughly 3.2 GB of retained payload bytes while archive admission charges the original part once. Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently traced DOCX fontTable unique names sharing embed r:id/key -\> load_embedded_fonts loops every entry -\> deobfuscate_odttf bytes.to_vec -\> new Arc per alias -\> retained EmbeddedFonts -\> Fonts::for_document. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read font table parse (76-129), plain/deobfuscation cloning (179-193), full embedded loader (205-232) and with_layout ordering (806-809). Names are not required to match internal font family or be used in document text. One ~1MiB valid font with 10000 distinct names can request ~10GiB retained bytes while physical input remains a few MiB. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified catalogue-known families are skipped but arbitrary distinct unknown names are accepted, plain sfnt data is allowed, and every alias can reference the same valid part. Unique keys retain all copies; the later extra-face index cap occurs after loading. Admission counts the physical part once, not aliases times font size. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Distinct family names produce distinct table entries. Non-catalogue aliases can share a single valid TTF relationship; plain sfnt input is still cloned by deobfuscate_odttf. Face::parse validates format, then data.into() transfers each separate Vec into the retained map. Rendering loads that map unconditionally and borrows it through Fonts::for_document. Native installed-font lookup does not retroactively bound allocations already retained.

Validation method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

- **Status:** validated

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Known catalogue families are skipped; use distinct unknown names.
- Invalid fonts are skipped; a single valid embedded font is sufficient.
- The map stores Arc values, but each iteration creates new data and a fresh Arc; there is no source-part sharing here.
- ZIP byte and XML depth/attribute limits do not charge multiplicity of font aliases.
- Catalogue family names are skipped, but attackers can choose rare names.
- Invalid fonts are rejected, but a single valid font can be reused.
- Arc values do not deduplicate separate Vec allocations.
- The later u16 face-index cap occurs after font bytes have already been cloned and retained.
- Fixed catalogue families skipped, but arbitrary distinct names are accepted.
- Face validity rejects malformed fonts; one valid reused font satisfies it.
- Arc ownership shares only each newly cloned allocation, not copies across aliases.
- Conversion-scoped lifetime prevents persistent leak but not in-call exhaustion.
- Archive byte limits and recommended process memory limits do not remove alias amplification.
- Physical-input/bounds checks and host process limits do not bound this derived output or per-character work.
- Exact catalogue families are skipped; distinct unknown family aliases avoid that optimization.
- Invalid fonts are rejected after cloning, so the retained amplification requires a valid font.
- Archive/part bounds apply to the single stored source part; process limits contain worker failure.
- Only parseable fonts survive and catalogue names are skipped; distinct noncatalogue aliases of a valid font satisfy those checks.
- Arc shares references after creation but does not deduplicate separate Vec copies.
- Per-document lifetime prevents a permanent leak, not peak exhaustion; face-index caps apply after eager allocation.
- Package byte/entry limits charge the shared part only once; caller process quotas contain host damage.

Limitations:
- Static validation only; no exploit document or measured allocation threshold.
- No application/test/PoC execution; no observed remote or shared deployment.
- No runtime input generated or executed.

- No font fixture or alias-heavy document was constructed or executed.

#### Reachability

Default public document rendering loads all embedded fonts before body run selection, so the supplier needs no operator-controlled configuration.

- **Attacker:** DOCX supplier

- **Entry point:** Public PDF/PNG/render APIs

- **Outcome:** Caller-process denial of service

#### Severity

**Medium** — A supplier-controlled DOCX crosses the public renderer boundary under ordinary options and predictably exhausts caller memory. Source establishes process availability impact, without assuming a remote deployment or confidentiality/code-execution gain.

Shared conversion services have greater availability impact; isolated memory-limited workers constrain host damage.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Memory exhaustion affects rendering process.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Valid small aliases to one ordinary font reach the eager loader under default options.

#### Remediation

Cache decoded font buffers by resolved package part and effective obfuscation key, share Arc values across aliases, and enforce an aggregate decoded-font allocation/work budget before copying. Enforce face-count limits before decoding/retention and load only used faces where possible; cover all four style slots and different effective keys.

Tests:
- Load many unique aliases referencing one valid embedded part and assert shared buffers and bounded aggregate allocation.
- Exercise distinct effective font keys and malformed fonts without bypassing aggregate budgets.
- Many aliases referencing one font/key must share decoded backing storage or remain within an aggregate budget.
- Cover distinct keys, four styles, unused aliases, catalogue skips, and malformed fonts.
- Many distinct noncatalogue aliases referencing one valid part must share backing storage or return a typed resource-limit refusal under a small configured budget.
- Many aliases of one part share one decoded payload.
- Distinct embedded fonts collectively respect a retained-byte budget.
- Unused font definitions do not trigger unnecessary whole-font copies.
- Reference one large font from many aliases and verify storage is shared or a typed budget refusal occurs.
- Preserve alias/style resolution and plain/obfuscated font support.
- Add deterministic bounded-input regression coverage around the broken control; for filesystem staging use isolated integration cases with pre-existing symlink entries and verify unrelated files remain unchanged.
- Many aliases to one part share a single allocation or refuse at a fixed aggregate budget.
- Distinct deobfuscation keys remain distinct; malformed font programs still refuse.

### [47] UTF-16 XML can retain confidential text after successful scrub or redaction

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Supported admission encoding, mismatched decoder, no-root behavior, extension-based fallback and final redaction consumer were independently traced; unmodified parts are explicitly preserved. |
| Category | Improper handling of Unicode encoding |
| CWE | CWE-176 |
| Affected lines | src/admission.rs:764-780, src/opc/mod.rs:561-564, src/scrub.rs:189-194, src/scrub.rs:467-475, src/scrub.rs:527-534, src/edit.rs:5380-5384, src/edit.rs:4727-4745, src/edit/prepared.rs:804, src/edit/prepared.rs:873 |

#### Summary

Jubarte accepts UTF-16 XML but scrub and leak detection read it as lossy UTF-8. Metadata transforms silently skip it, and redaction postchecks can miss a remaining confidential copy in UTF-16 custom XML while returning successful output.

#### Root Cause

Admission's `part_text` decodes UTF-16 BOMs, but `PartFs::part_string` and the XML branch of `leaks_within` apply `String::from_utf8_lossy`. A UTF-16 BOM becomes a leading replacement character and the permissive parser returns no root. Scrub skips that part, while `xml_holds` searches a string with interleaved NULs; the raw UTF-16 fallback is excluded for XML members. `check_redactions` trusts the empty result for both clean and redline outputs.

**Admission supports BOM-prefixed UTF-16 XML** — `src/admission.rs:764-780`

Accepted UTF-16LE/BE parts are transcoded for the input policy, establishing this as supported data.

```
/// A part's text for scanning. Word writes UTF-8, but a part may be UTF-16
/// with a byte-order mark (SharePoint's `customXml` items often are) and
/// Word opens it, so it is transcoded; other bytes decode lossily, as the
/// rest of the engine reads them.
fn part_text(xml: &[u8]) -> Cow<'_, str> {
    let utf16 = |rest: &[u8], unit: fn([u8; 2]) -> u16| {
        let units = rest.as_chunks::<2>().0.iter().map(|&pair| unit(pair));
        Cow::Owned(
            char::decode_utf16(units)
                .map(|c| c.unwrap_or(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER))
                .collect(),
        )
    };
    match xml {
        [0xFF, 0xFE, rest @ ..] => utf16(rest, u16::from_le_bytes),
        [0xFE, 0xFF, rest @ ..] => utf16(rest, u16::from_be_bytes),
        _ => String::from_utf8_lossy(xml),
```

**Redaction trusts an empty leak result** — `src/edit.rs:4727-4745`

The confidentiality postcondition treats no reported parts as success, so a missed UTF-16 copy avoids REDACTION_LEAK.

```
    fn check_redactions(&self, outputs: &[&[u8]]) -> Result<(), EditError> {
        for (op, operation) in self.plan.operations.iter().enumerate() {
            let OperationKind::Redact { find, .. } = &operation.kind else {
                continue;
            };
            let parts: std::collections::BTreeSet<String> = outputs
                .iter()
                .flat_map(|doc| crate::scrub::leaks(doc, find))
                .collect();
            if parts.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let message = format!(
                "the redacted text still occurs in {}; redact every copy in the same plan, or remove the comment or part that holds it",
                parts.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
            );
            let mut error = self.conflict(op, &message);
            error.code = "REDACTION_LEAK".into();
            error.outcomes[op].code = Some(error.code.clone());
```

#### Validation

Confirmed an ordinary ASCII secret in BOM-prefixed UTF-16 XML is not contiguous in the lossy UTF-8 string. The leading BOM decoding prevents a DOM root, so neither XML text scanning nor fallback substring matching finds it. Editing a visible UTF-8 copy leaves custom XML unchanged; prepared output paths call check_redactions at lines 804 and 873.

Validation method: independent offline static source trace

- **Status:** validated

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Archive reads/inflation fail closed, but successful byte retrieval does not establish successful decoding.
- The non-XML branch scans raw UTF-16LE needles; legitimate .xml/.rels parts bypass that branch.
- UTF-8 entity/text-run handling does not repair the encoding mismatch.
- Admission tests at src/admission.rs:1845-1863 explicitly accept UTF-16 custom XML; this is not an unsupported-encoding claim.

Limitations:
- No document was generated, edited or shared at runtime during review.

#### Dataflow

Accepted UTF-16 XML bytes -\> untouched package member -\> lossy UTF-8 privacy/leak decode -\> no DOM root -\> NUL-interleaved substring miss -\> empty leaks -\> successful clean/redline output.

#### Reachability

A document supplier can control accepted XML encodings. The legitimate scrub/redaction request supplies the sensitive needle and relies on the engine's promised whole-package refusal.

- **Attacker:** Document supplier or recipient of ostensibly sanitized output

- **Entry point:** scrub::scrub, scrub::leaks and edit Redact output validation

- **Outcome:** Disclosure of confidential text or identities retained in the package.

Preconditions:
- A confidential value remains in accepted UTF-16 XML.
- The resulting output is shared or otherwise relied on as sanitized.

#### Severity

**Medium** — The failure defeats an explicit whole-package redaction/privacy postcondition and can disclose confidential text when output is distributed. It requires an accepted UTF-16 copy and a sharing workflow; it does not provide ambient file access.

Encoding-aware fail-closed validation or removal of the retained copy prevents disclosure. Reliance on redaction before public sharing increases impact.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** An explicit redaction guarantee can fail for arbitrary confidential text present in the document.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Requires a particular accepted encoding and privacy workflow.

#### Remediation

Use one encoding-aware XML decoder for admission, privacy transformations and leakage checks. Fail closed when an accepted XML part cannot be decoded or parsed for a privacy operation; scan all supported encodings consistently before certifying redaction.

Tests:
- Cover UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE metadata scrubbing at conventional and alternate locations.
- Redact a visible UTF-8 occurrence while a second copy exists in UTF-16 custom XML and require REDACTION_LEAK for both clean/redline outputs.

```
        let cols = table
            .rows

```

**Every column is emitted to an in-memory String** — `src/convert/altchunk.rs:489-491`

Even a span of one billion, representable on 32-bit WASM and native platforms, demands billions of XML elements.

```
        for _ in 0..cols {

        }
```

#### Validation

Independently traced with_layout -\> admitted package -\> internal altChunk relationship -\> chunk_html/html_to_wml -\> Builder.start/end_cell/end_table. An ordinary table/tr/td closing sequence reaches the emission loop; no network fetching or special trusted options are needed.

Validation method: offline static source trace

- **Status:** validated

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- External relationships are not needed; the HTML part is internal.
- The archive and original XML are admitted first (src/convert/mod.rs:773-774), but HTML expansion occurs later at :790-793.
- All source fields are escaped in generated XML; this finding concerns resource expansion rather than XML injection.
- Caller CPU/memory isolation limits impact to its worker.

Limitations:
- No malicious input was created or executed.
- Actual peak memory and termination behavior were not measured.

#### Dataflow

Internal HTML chunk td/th colspan -\> usize cell.span -\> row span sum -\> cols -\> unbounded for loop appending gridCol elements to String.

#### Reachability

Public conversion/rendering accepts caller-controlled DOCX; a body w:altChunk with an internal HTML relationship is expanded before normal layout.

- **Attacker:** Supplier of a DOCX rendered by another user's process

Preconditions:
- Victim processes a DOCX with an HTML altChunk table.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A small supported document input causes deterministic process availability loss; no remote shared service is assumed, and external worker resource limits mitigate wider impact.

A shared long-lived conversion process increases blast radius; strict per-document worker limits reduce it.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Unbounded generated XML consumes memory and CPU until worker failure.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** The attacker controls the loop bound through a small numeric attribute on the supported import path.

#### Remediation

Bound colspan and the total table column count before iteration, use checked arithmetic, and enforce a cumulative generated-WML/output budget across each HTML chunk and document. Return a typed input-limit refusal before allocating oversized output.

Tests:
- Cover maximum allowed colspan, one above it, usize::MAX, and multiple spans whose sum overflows.
- Test small admitted packages with oversized HTML spans and repeated chunks; assert bounded refusal under default limits.

```rust
    let past = || LegacyDocError::new("a text piece points past the WordDocument stream");

    // the document would come out quietly shorter than it is.
    // The CPs only ever increase ([MS-DOC] 2.8.35): a piece that runs
    // backwards is corruption, wherever it sits.
    if pieces.iter().any(|piece| piece.cp_end < piece.cp_start) {

    for piece in pieces {
        if covered >= ccp_text {
            break;

        // An empty piece (fast-saved files carry them) covers nothing.
        if piece.cp_end == piece.cp_start {
            continue;
        }
        if piece.cp_start != covered {
            break;
        }
        covered = piece.cp_end;

            "the piece table does not cover the main story",
```

**CLI refusal hint parses legacy input too** — `src/bin/jubarte.rs:2740-2755`

The shared read_document helper invokes legacy_doc::read even to decide whether to suggest conversion after a format refusal, so a refused legacy input can reach the same expansion before a hint is returned.

```rust
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {
        // Only a .doc that converts gets the hint; an encrypted document
        // or another OLE file would be sent to a command that fails.
        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
            format!(
                "; a .doc converts with: jubarte convert {} -o {}",
                path.display(),
                path.with_extension("docx").display()
            )
        } else {
            String::new()
        };
        return Err(format!("{refused}{hint}"));
    }
```

```rust
fn main_text(word: &[u8], pieces: &[Piece], ccp_text: u32) -> Result<Vec<StoryChar>> {
    let past = || LegacyDocError::new("a text piece points past the WordDocument stream");
    // The pieces run from CP 0 through the main story without a gap, or
    // the document would come out quietly shorter than it is.
    // The CPs only ever increase ([MS-DOC] 2.8.35): a piece that runs
    // backwards is corruption, wherever it sits.
    if pieces.iter().any(|piece| piece.cp_end < piece.cp_start) {
        return Err(LegacyDocError::new("the piece table's CPs are decreasing"));
    }
    let mut covered = 0u32;
    for piece in pieces {
        if covered >= ccp_text {
            break;
        }
        // An empty piece (fast-saved files carry them) covers nothing.
        if piece.cp_end == piece.cp_start {
            continue;
        }
        if piece.cp_start != covered {
            break;
        }
        covered = piece.cp_end;
    }
    if covered < ccp_text {
        return Err(LegacyDocError::new(
            "the piece table does not cover the main story",
        ));
    }
    let mut out = Vec::new();
```

**Legacy document entry** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:180-225`

The public reader materializes main_text before story processing.

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
}
```

```rust
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {

        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
            format!(
                "; a .doc converts with: jubarte convert {} -o {}",
                path.display(),
                path.with_extension("docx").display()
```

```
            String::new()
        };
        return Err(format!("{refused}{hint}"));
```

```rust
        covered = piece.cp_end;
```

```rust
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {
        // Only a .doc that converts gets the hint; an encrypted document
        // or another OLE file would be sent to a command that fails.
        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
            format!(
                "; a .doc converts with: jubarte convert {} -o {}",
                path.display(),
                path.with_extension("docx").display()
            )
        } else {
            String::new()
        };
        return Err(format!("{refused}{hint}"));
    }
```

**Legacy document entry** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:180-225`

The public reader materializes main_text before story processing.

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
}
```

**Legacy document entry** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:180-225`

The public reader materializes main_text before story processing.

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
}
```

```rust
/// Reads an input document, refusing the OLE files Word alone can open and
/// RTF by their signature (`admission::sniff`, the check the library and
/// the bindings run too).
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {
        // Only a .doc that converts gets the hint; an encrypted document
        // or another OLE file would be sent to a command that fails.
        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
```

**Logical continuity without decoded-size budget** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:1148-1176`

```rust
fn main_text(word: &[u8], pieces: &[Piece], ccp_text: u32) -> Result<Vec<StoryChar>> {
    let past = || LegacyDocError::new("a text piece points past the WordDocument stream");
    // The pieces run from CP 0 through the main story without a gap, or
    // the document would come out quietly shorter than it is.
    // The CPs only ever increase ([MS-DOC] 2.8.35): a piece that runs
    // backwards is corruption, wherever it sits.
    if pieces.iter().any(|piece| piece.cp_end < piece.cp_start) {
        return Err(LegacyDocError::new("the piece table's CPs are decreasing"));
    }
    let mut covered = 0u32;
    for piece in pieces {
        if covered >= ccp_text {
            break;
        }
        // An empty piece (fast-saved files carry them) covers nothing.
        if piece.cp_end == piece.cp_start {
            continue;
        }
        if piece.cp_start != covered {
            break;
        }
        covered = piece.cp_end;
    }
    if covered < ccp_text {
        return Err(LegacyDocError::new(
            "the piece table does not cover the main story",
        ));
    }
    let mut out = Vec::new();
```

**Rejected input diagnostic fully parses DOC** — `src/bin/jubarte.rs:2740-2754`

The CLI calls the reader even when already refusing the input, only to generate a conversion hint.

```
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {
        // Only a .doc that converts gets the hint; an encrypted document
        // or another OLE file would be sent to a command that fails.
        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
            format!(
                "; a .doc converts with: jubarte convert {} -o {}",
                path.display(),
                path.with_extension("docx").display()
            )
        } else {
            String::new()
        };
        return Err(format!("{refused}{hint}"));
```

#### Reachability

A caller supplying an untrusted legacy DOC piece table. Victim must process the supplied file; no privileged configuration is needed. legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown and doc_to_docx are public byte APIs. CLI convert also dispatches legacy input; no privileged configuration is required. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Public `legacy_doc::read`, `doc_to_docx` and `doc_to_markdown` accept caller bytes; native `convert` detects compound-file input and invokes this path. The shared CLI read_document refusal-hint branch also invokes legacy_doc::read before returning its unsupported-input message. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Public legacy_doc::read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and native CLI conversion process caller-supplied .doc. read_document also invokes full legacy read merely to generate a refusal hint. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Public legacy_doc::read/doc_to_docx and native CLI conversion/refusal hints invoke the vulnerable reader before DOCX limits.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author Supplier of untrusted input processed by a library consumer Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: legacy document supplier Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: An untrusted legacy document author. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Document supplier

- **Entry point:** legacy_doc::read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI conversion Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: legacy_doc::read and native convert

- **Outcome:** loss of availability of the parsing process Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Host process denial of service

Preconditions:
- Victim invokes the affected public API with attacker-controlled document input.
- Victim accepts and processes the supplied Word 97-2003 document.
- Victim reads/converts or invokes a CLI document path on the attacker-controlled legacy DOC.
- Structurally readable unencrypted OLE/FIB/piece table with valid reused offsets.

Existing controls:
- Physical stream bounds remain enforced; they do not bound logical expansion.
- Sector traversal is bounded and source offsets use checked arithmetic/bounds checks.
- Logical CP continuity does not prevent repeating the same physical source bytes.
- DOCX ZIP budgets do not govern legacy expansion before conversion creates a DOCX.

Limitations:
- Memory-safe reads remain bounded; no arbitrary code execution or confidentiality impact is established.

#### Severity

**Medium** — An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): high
- **Rationale:** Host process memory exhaustion.
- **Why:** Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Resource exhaustion of the embedding process, without established data access or execution. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Allocation failure can terminate the processing host.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): medium
- **Rationale:** Supported format and ordinary public parsing paths; no unusual configuration.
- **Why:** The triggering structure and values are document-controlled and not rejected by existing guards. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Compact valid physical mappings permit several orders of magnitude logical expansion. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Requires victim ingestion; actual shared deployment unknown.

#### Remediation

### [50] Intern-pool saturation duplicates long namespace URIs per element

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent inspected the supplied-input consumer, parser/storage implementation and applicable budgets. Allocation multiplicity or recursion follows directly from source; no runtime trigger was executed. |
| Category | Namespace memory amplification |
| CWE | CWE-770 |
| Affected lines | src/xmllinq/parse.rs:129-135, src/xmllinq/mod.rs:66-90, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:704-729, src/xmllinq/mod.rs:175-185 |

#### Summary

A shallow valid XML input can first fill the 16,384-entry intern pool with distinct short names, then introduce a new 8,192-byte namespace URI and repeat tiny elements in that namespace. Once the pool is full, each element retains a fresh URI allocation. About 131,072 elements retain at least 1 GiB of URI bytes from less than 1 MiB of source.

#### Root Cause

The count-bounded global string pool falls back to Arc::from for every new string when saturated. Active namespace URIs are re-interned for each XName rather than sharing the parser scope's allocation, so bounded declarations are multiplied by element count.

**intern cap** — `src/xmllinq/mod.rs:66-90`

Checked XML -\> TagPolicy succeeds on shallow declarations -\> DOM parse -\> resolve -\> XNamespace::get(ns).name -\> XName::get -\> intern_str(full pool) -\> independent Arc namespace retained by every node. This source implements intern-cap.

```
/// Cap the intern pool so a pathological host (adversarial inputs) cannot grow
/// the thread-local set without bound (gemini #3584751169, CR #3584798246).
/// OOXML name vocabulary is far smaller; beyond the cap we still return a
/// correct `Arc<str>`, just without interning.
const STR_POOL_MAX: usize = 16_384;

/// Return a shared interned `Arc<str>` for `s`, allocating only on first sight.
/// Equality/hash of the result are byte-for-byte identical to a fresh `Arc::from`;
/// only storage is shared, so interning is behavior-preserving.
fn intern_str(s: &str) -> Arc<str> {
    STR_POOL.with(|pool| {
        {
            // Scope the shared borrow so it is released before `borrow_mut` below.
            let p = pool.borrow();
            if let Some(existing) = p.get(s) {
                return existing.clone();
            }
            if p.len() >= STR_POOL_MAX {
                return Arc::from(s);
            }
        }
        let arc: Arc<str> = Arc::from(s);
        pool.borrow_mut().insert(arc.clone());
        arc
    })
```

```
fn resolve(qn: &str, is_attr: bool, local_scope: &NsScope) -> XName {
    if let Some(colon) = qn.find(':') {
        let prefix = &qn[..colon];
        let local = &qn[colon + 1..];
        if prefix == "xmlns" {
            return XNamespace::xmlns().name(local);
        }
        if prefix == "xml" {
            return XNamespace::xml().name(local);
        }
        return match local_scope.get(prefix) {
            Some(ns) => XNamespace::get(ns).name(local),
            None => XName::get(local, ""),
        };
    }
    if qn == "xmlns" {
        return XName::get("xmlns", "");
    }
    // Attributes default to no namespace; elements use the default (xmlns="…").
    let def_ns: Option<&String> = if is_attr { None } else { local_scope.get("") };
    match def_ns {
        Some(ns) if !ns.is_empty() => XNamespace::get(ns).name(qn),
        _ => XName::get(qn, ""),
    }
}

```

```
impl XName {
    /// Construct an expanded name in the given namespace. `local_name` and
    /// `namespace_name` are interned through the thread-local pool
    /// (a no-op once the pool saturates). Pass `""` for the empty
    /// (no-namespace) namespace.
    pub fn get(local_name: &str, namespace_name: &str) -> XName {
        XName {
            local: intern_str(local_name),
            namespace: XNamespace::get(namespace_name),
        }
    }
```

#### Summary

An attacker-supplied DOCX can name an auxiliary styles part with a non-XML extension. Admission skips XML checks for that part, but rendering follows its styles relationship and passes the bytes to an unchecked recursive DOM parser. Deep nesting can exhaust the host stack despite normal admission.

Its recursive element parser has no local depth budget.

**EMF points are confined to record extent** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:1061-1082`

```rust
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
        }
    }
    Some(pts)
```

```rust
/// Render a DOCX package to PDF and return the font-resolution report for
/// it. The PDF is the `pdf` field of the result; the font report is the
/// entries the conversion made for that document.
```
