```rust
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`docx_to_pdf_with`].
pub fn docx_to_pdf_report(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<ConvertedPdf, ConvertError> {
    let (result, font_report) = font::with_font_report(|| docx_to_pdf_inner(docx, options));
    Ok(ConvertedPdf {
        pdf: result?,
        font_report,
    })
}

fn docx_to_pdf_inner(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_options(options, || docx_to_pdf_body(docx, options))
}

fn docx_to_pdf_body(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_pages(docx, |fonts, pages| pdf::emit(fonts, pages, options))
```

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

```rust
/// Windows-1252 text, one byte a character.
fn ansi_text(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    const HIGH: [char; 32] = [
        '€', '\u{81}', '‚', 'ƒ', '„', '…', '†', '‡', 'ˆ', '‰', 'Š', '‹', 'Œ', '\u{8d}', 'Ž',
        '\u{8f}', '\u{90}', '‘', '’', '“', '”', '•', '–', '—', '˜', '™', 'š', '›', 'œ', '\u{9d}',
        'ž', 'Ÿ',
    ];
    bytes
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| match b {
            0x80..=0x9F => HIGH[usize::from(b - 0x80)],
            _ => char::from(b),
        })
        .collect()
```

```
fn decode_image(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Option<ImageKind> {
    if let Some((width, height, rgb, texts)) = metafile::render(&bytes) {
        let raster = ImageKind::Rgb {
            width,
            height,
            bytes: rgb,
            alpha: None,
        };
        if texts.is_empty() {
            return Some(raster);
        }
        return Some(ImageKind::Metafile {
            raster: Box::new(raster),
            texts: texts.into(),
        });
```

```
fn wmf_text(dc: &WmfState, map: &Map, x: i16, y: i16, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<MetaText> {
    let text = ansi_text(bytes);
    if text.trim().is_empty() || map.ext_x.abs() < f32::EPSILON || map.ext_y.abs() < f32::EPSILON {
        return None;
    }
    let font = dc.font.as_deref();
    let height = font.map_or(0, |f| f.height);
    Some(MetaText {
        text,
        x: (f32::from(x) - map.org_x) / map.ext_x,
        y: (f32::from(y) - map.org_y) / map.ext_y,
        // lfHeight 0 is the default font, 12pt at 96 dpi of a 1440 inch.
        size: if height == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            f32::from(height.unsigned_abs()) / map.ext_y.abs()
        },
        cell: height > 0,
        family: font.map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.face.clone()),
        bold: font.is_some_and(|f| f.weight >= 600),
        italic: font.is_some_and(|f| f.italic),
        color: dc.text_color,
        align: dc.text_align,
        aspect: (map.ext_x / map.ext_y).abs(),
    })
```
```

fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;

            if p + 8 > off + size {

            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
```

**Text conversion retains copied string** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:692-718`

Every supplied text payload is decoded into a new string and retained in `MetaText`; a missing font does not reject it.

```rust
fn wmf_text(dc: &WmfState, map: &Map, x: i16, y: i16, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<MetaText> {
    let text = ansi_text(bytes);
    if text.trim().is_empty() || map.ext_x.abs() < f32::EPSILON || map.ext_y.abs() < f32::EPSILON {
        return None;
    }
    let font = dc.font.as_deref();
    let height = font.map_or(0, |f| f.height);
    Some(MetaText {
        text,
        x: (f32::from(x) - map.org_x) / map.ext_x,
        y: (f32::from(y) - map.org_y) / map.ext_y,
        // lfHeight 0 is the default font, 12pt at 96 dpi of a 1440 inch.
        size: if height == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            f32::from(height.unsigned_abs()) / map.ext_y.abs()
        },
        cell: height > 0,
        family: font.map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.face.clone()),
        bold: font.is_some_and(|f| f.weight >= 600),
        italic: font.is_some_and(|f| f.italic),
        color: dc.text_color,
        align: dc.text_align,
        aspect: (map.ext_x / map.ext_y).abs(),
    })
```
```rust
}
```

**Sibling EMF code enforces record-local bound** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:1061-1083`

The sibling EMF reader checks coordinate bytes against the current record end, demonstrating a record-local bound absent from WMF.

```rust
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
        }
    }
    Some(pts)
}
```

Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed. Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost. Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure. /// Render a DOCX package to PDF and return the font-resolution report for
```rust
/// it. The PDF is the `pdf` field of the result; the font report is the
/// entries the conversion made for that document.

/// # Errors
///
/// As [`docx_to_pdf_with`].
pub fn docx_to_pdf_report(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<ConvertedPdf, ConvertError> {
    let (result, font_report) = font::with_font_report(|| docx_to_pdf_inner(docx, options));

        pdf: result?,
        font_report,
    })
}

fn docx_to_pdf_inner(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {

}

fn docx_to_pdf_body(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_pages(docx, |fonts, pages| pdf::emit(fonts, pages, options))
```

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

```rust
/// Windows-1252 text, one byte a character.
fn ansi_text(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    const HIGH: [char; 32] = [
        '€', '\u{81}', '‚', 'ƒ', '„', '…', '†', '‡', 'ˆ', '‰', 'Š', '‹', 'Œ', '\u{8d}', 'Ž',
        '\u{8f}', '\u{90}', '‘', '’', '“', '”', '•', '–', '—', '˜', '™', 'š', '›', 'œ', '\u{9d}',
        'ž', 'Ÿ',
    ];
    bytes
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| match b {
            0x80..=0x9F => HIGH[usize::from(b - 0x80)],
            _ => char::from(b),
        })
        .collect()
```

**Metafile decoder retains decoded texts** — `src/convert/mod.rs:20247-20261`

```
fn decode_image(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Option<ImageKind> {
    if let Some((width, height, rgb, texts)) = metafile::render(&bytes) {
        let raster = ImageKind::Rgb {
            width,
            height,
            bytes: rgb,
            alpha: None,
        };
        if texts.is_empty() {
            return Some(raster);
        }
        return Some(ImageKind::Metafile {
            raster: Box::new(raster),
            texts: texts.into(),
        });
```

```
fn wmf_text(dc: &WmfState, map: &Map, x: i16, y: i16, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<MetaText> {
    let text = ansi_text(bytes);
    if text.trim().is_empty() || map.ext_x.abs() < f32::EPSILON || map.ext_y.abs() < f32::EPSILON {
        return None;
    }
    let font = dc.font.as_deref();
    let height = font.map_or(0, |f| f.height);
    Some(MetaText {
        text,
        x: (f32::from(x) - map.org_x) / map.ext_x,
        y: (f32::from(y) - map.org_y) / map.ext_y,
        // lfHeight 0 is the default font, 12pt at 96 dpi of a 1440 inch.
        size: if height == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            f32::from(height.unsigned_abs()) / map.ext_y.abs()
        },
        cell: height > 0,
        family: font.map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.face.clone()),
        bold: font.is_some_and(|f| f.weight >= 600),
        italic: font.is_some_and(|f| f.italic),
        color: dc.text_color,
        align: dc.text_align,
        aspect: (map.ext_x / map.ext_y).abs(),
    })
```

**Embedded images invoke metafile parser** — `src/convert/mod.rs:20247-20261`

An embedded image's supplied bytes enter the WMF/EMF parser before ordinary raster decoding; returned text is retained in the image representation.

```rust
fn decode_image(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Option<ImageKind> {
    if let Some((width, height, rgb, texts)) = metafile::render(&bytes) {
        let raster = ImageKind::Rgb {
            width,
            height,
            bytes: rgb,
            alpha: None,
        };
        if texts.is_empty() {
            return Some(raster);
        }
        return Some(ImageKind::Metafile {
            raster: Box::new(raster),
            texts: texts.into(),
        });
```

**Text conversion retains copied string** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:692-718`

Every supplied text payload is decoded into a new string and retained in `MetaText`; a missing font does not reject it.

```rust
fn wmf_text(dc: &WmfState, map: &Map, x: i16, y: i16, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<MetaText> {
    let text = ansi_text(bytes);
    if text.trim().is_empty() || map.ext_x.abs() < f32::EPSILON || map.ext_y.abs() < f32::EPSILON {
        return None;
    }
    let font = dc.font.as_deref();
    let height = font.map_or(0, |f| f.height);
    Some(MetaText {
        text,
        x: (f32::from(x) - map.org_x) / map.ext_x,
        y: (f32::from(y) - map.org_y) / map.ext_y,
        // lfHeight 0 is the default font, 12pt at 96 dpi of a 1440 inch.
        size: if height == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            f32::from(height.unsigned_abs()) / map.ext_y.abs()
        },
        cell: height > 0,
        family: font.map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.face.clone()),
        bold: font.is_some_and(|f| f.weight >= 600),
        italic: font.is_some_and(|f| f.italic),
        color: dc.text_color,
        align: dc.text_align,
        aspect: (map.ext_x / map.ext_y).abs(),
    })
```
```rust
}

```

**Sibling EMF code enforces record-local bound** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:1061-1083`

The sibling EMF reader checks coordinate bytes against the current record end, demonstrating a record-local bound absent from WMF.

```rust
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
        }
    }
    Some(pts)
}
```

- Safe slice reads eventually reject truncation, after earlier records have already performed amplified work.
- EMF read_emf_points has record-end bounds; it does not protect the WMF handlers.
- Whole-buffer slice checks prevent Rust memory unsafety; this is parser resource amplification.
- WMF object count is clamped and canvas MAX_SIDE is 384, but neither controls the texts vector.
- Valid record-local counts would consume input proportionally and would not produce this overlap.
- Canvas dimensions are capped at 384 per side and hostile coordinates are clipped; these controls do not bound retained strings.

- Whole-file Rust slice bounds avoid arbitrary memory reads; the finding concerns invalid record extents and resource amplification.

- Input compressed/inflated limits remain, but do not charge repeatedly allocated text.

#### Reachability

Victim renders a DOCX referencing attacker-controlled placeable WMF bytes. The attacker controls embedded media in a document consumed by the renderer, with no release credentials or nondefault configuration. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Public DOCX rendering decodes embedded WMF bytes from the package. A document author controls the record sizes and later bytes without needing host filesystem or release authority.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author untrusted document supplier Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: An untrusted document/image author.

- **Entry point:** Public PDF/PNG renderer convert public rendering APIs

- **Outcome:** Excessive allocation/work and host-process or WASM instance failure

Preconditions:
- Victim renders a DOCX referencing attacker-controlled placeable WMF bytes.
- Victim renders a DOCX containing a WMF with nondegenerate bounds and malformed text records.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.

Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Process memory exhaustion or termination.
- **Why:** Host processing availability can be lost; no confidentiality or code-execution gain is established. Host/instance availability loss.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Compact malformed records are accepted on ordinary embedded-image rendering paths.
- **Why:** A document supplier controls the triggering parser inputs with no privileged configuration. Malformed binary counts reach a built-in parser directly and bypass otherwise bounded stored input.

#### Remediation

Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

Tests:
- Short WMF polygon, polypolygon and polyline records claiming following-record points must refuse before processing points.
- Repeated malformed records must consume work proportional to declared bytes, with EMF behavior retained.
- Deterministic parser tests with short declared records and text counts extending into the next record must refuse safely.
- Cover EXTTEXTOUT options/rectangle, TEXTOUT padding and record-local geometry counts with small resource budgets.
- Reject EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT strings extending into the next record.
- Reject cross-record polygon/polypolygon/polyline coordinates and validate large valid records within aggregate text/geometry budgets.
- Use existing in-memory WMF fixtures to ensure six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT cannot read subsequent records.
- Verify repeated undersized records produce no retained text.
- Retain valid text rendering tests and exercise cumulative text-budget refusal.
- Small malformed EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT records must be rejected without reading following bytes.
- Repeated short records must remain within deterministic cumulative allocation/work limits.
- Verify valid WMF text still renders through public PDF/PNG APIs.
- Exercise short TEXTOUT, EXTTEXTOUT, POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE records with sufficient trailing bytes; require refusal without consuming the next record.
- Refuse textout/exttextout/polygon/polypolygon/polyline counts extending beyond their record despite sufficient following file bytes.
- Verify repeated small records cannot amplify trailing content into unbounded retained output.
- Refuse EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT whose counts or coordinate fields extend past their own record even when still inside the file.
- Ensure many valid records hit a bounded aggregate text budget and ordinary WMF text stays supported.
- Reject header-only TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT records even when later file bytes can satisfy their reads.
- Bound aggregate extracted text and test valid records exactly at declared boundaries.
- Exercise undersized text records using small harmless limits and assert refusal without reading following-record bytes.
- Verify aggregate text budgets and normal EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records; avoid allocating attacker-sized outputs.
- Undersized TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT refuses before text retention.
- POLYGON/POLYPOLYGON/POLYLINE counts cannot consume following records.
- Valid WMF and EMF rendering remains supported.
- Reject text counts extending beyond EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT record end even when bytes remain in the file.
- Reject polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts extending beyond their records.
- Verify repeated short records cannot copy overlapping trailing bytes into retained text.
- Keep valid WMF rendering and existing extreme-coordinate/record-size tests.
- Assert EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT counts beyond record end are refused even if the file has sufficient trailing bytes.
- Exercise polygon/polypolygon/polyline/font records with truncated declared payloads.
- Assert repeated small records cannot create decoded-text output disproportionate to valid payload bytes.
- Short TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT and geometry records whose counts extend into the next record must be rejected before copying or iteration.

Preventive controls:
- Bound the actual representation depth and processing work at the consuming boundary.
- Pass bounded record slices to all metafile handlers instead of exposing the entire backing file.

### [53] Public Strict-format probe inflates unbounded document headers

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Independent parent source tracing confirms the entrypoint, failing control and sensitive operation. No exploit or application code executed. |
| Category | Unbounded decompression |
| CWE | CWE-409, CWE-400 |
| Affected lines | src/strict_translation.rs:670-675, src/strict_translation.rs:682-703, src/strict_translation.rs:670-703, src/strict_translation.rs:721-728, src/strict_translation.rs:670-700, src/strict_translation.rs:719-727, src/strict_translation.rs:670-676, src/strict_translation.rs:682-703, src/lib.rs:144, src/lib.rs:138-146, src/strict_translation.rs:719-728, src/lib.rs:144, src/strict_translation.rs:670-704, src/strict_translation.rs:705-716 |

#### Summary

The public main_part_is_strict helper reads word/document.xml without admission or an inflation/preamble cap. A compressible oversized/unfinished root opening tag or long XML comment keeps the last '\<' at offset zero; the full growing head remains retained and is repeatedly scanned until the root tag completes or EOF, allowing memory/CPU exhaustion for direct library consumers. The assigned audit establishes direct public-library exposure and found no in-repository production caller; ordinary rendering is not claimed to call this detector.

#### Root Cause

Public ZIP-reading sibling bypasses admission and assumes bytes since the last '\<' remain small, without bounding an individual opening tag. The same accumulating buffer is unbounded during comments as well as a root opening tag: rposition('\<') remains zero, drain(..0) drops nothing, and root_open scans the entire retained preamble after every 16 KiB read. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A boolean format probe bypasses package resource admission and assumes retaining bytes since the last \< bounds state; a long comment invalidates that assumption. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `main_part_is_strict()` opens word/document.xml directly. It appends decompressed chunks to `head` until finding `>`, then retains from the last `<`. With an unfinished root tag followed by a long whitespace run, that position remains zero and no bytes are discarded. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `main_part_is_strict` opens the ZIP and `word/document.xml` directly, then reads the part in chunks into `head`. While an opening tag contains only its initial '\<' and no '\>', draining before the last '\<' removes nothing. Each read therefore increases retained decompressed bytes and repeats delimiter scans across the accumulated tag. A highly compressible long run of spaces within the root tag reaches both unbounded memory growth and superlinear scanning before a boolean is returned.

**Public probe has no admission and an accumulating chunk loop** — `src/strict_translation.rs:670-703`

A small compressed comment causes unbounded inflation and repeated full-buffer scanning.

```rust
pub fn main_part_is_strict(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let Ok(mut archive) = crate::opc::open_archive(Cursor::new(bytes)) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Ok(mut part) = archive.by_name("word/document.xml") else {
        return false;
    };
    // The root element's opening tag follows whatever preamble the part
    // carries — a comment, a DOCTYPE — however long: read until it
    // appears, bounded by the part's own size, not by a window a long
    // preamble can push the root past (#561). Only the tail since the
    // last `<` can still hold the tag, so the head stays small.
    let mut head: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    let mut chunk = vec![0u8; 16 * 1024];
    loop {
        let Ok(read) = part.read(&mut chunk) else {
            return false;
        };
        if read == 0 {
            break;
        }
        head.extend(chunk.iter().copied().take(read));
        let window = String::from_utf8_lossy(&head);
        if let Some((start, _)) = root_open(&window)
            && window.split_at(start).1.contains('>')
        {
            break;
        }
        match head.iter().rposition(|&b| b == b'<') {
            Some(lt) => {
                head.drain(..lt);
            }
            None => head.clear(),
        }
```

```
/// Where `head` opens its root element: the first `<` an element name
/// follows (a comment, PI or DOCTYPE `<!`/`<?` opens none).
fn root_open(head: &str) -> Option<(usize, char)> {
    head.char_indices().find(|&(i, c)| {
        c == '<'
            && head
                .get(i.saturating_add(1)..)
                .is_some_and(|rest| rest.starts_with(char::is_alphabetic))
    })
```
```rust
}
```

#### Reachability

Public strict_translation function accepts raw document bytes and documents no prerequisite gate. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `strict_translation` is a public module and the detector accepts arbitrary bytes without a required admitted-input type or an enforced admission precondition.

- **Attacker:** document supplier to a consumer using this API

- **Entry point:** strict_translation::main_part_is_strict

- **Outcome:** availability loss in that consumer

Preconditions:
- Consumer probes untrusted bytes directly without separately bounded admission.
- Victim calls the public detector on untrusted bytes; normal rendering does not call this function.

Existing controls:
- The normal strict_to_transitional reader limits input/inflation; this separate function does not call it.
- ZIP structural validation checks headers and extents, not the inflated XML preamble.
- Source policy excludes raw infallible XML parser guarantees, but this is an independently exposed archive probe rather than a direct raw parse call.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Medium process-availability impact with high likelihood when the public probe processes untrusted archives. No remote deployment assumed.

A separate caller-owned admission step constrains the path; direct public callers need explicit limits.

**Impact assessment:** Process memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Long compressible tag deterministically drives the unbounded public parser when invoked.

#### Remediation

Apply bounded admission before indexing/inflation and explicit cumulative inflated-byte/preamble/work limits to this public helper. Use a streaming lexical probe with bounded retained state for comments, declarations and chunk-spanning root tags; refuse excessive probes with a checked/limited API and safe default limits.

Tests:
- Test oversized compressed opening tags under a small budget and retain valid within-budget preambles.
- Long compressed comments must hit a deterministic input/work bound.
- A chunk-spanning legal prolog should be recognized with constant retained state.
- An unfinished oversized opening tag terminates classification within a bounded budget.
- Long legitimate preambles retain supported behavior without unbounded head growth.
- Feed an over-budget compressed opening tag and assert a bounded refusal/false result before large retention.
- Test long preambles and quote-aware delimiter parsing with explicit limits.
- Use a small deterministic document with extreme semantic values or alternate valid OPC paths and assert controlled refusal or complete selected sanitization before expensive processing.
- Refuse an oversized root start tag under a small configurable input policy without inflating it fully.
- Verify long bounded preambles and ordinary Strict/Transitional roots remain classified correctly.

Preventive controls:
- Require every public compressed-input probe to share admission and incremental work budgets.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Direct static trace and existing supported mixed-operation test establish source-context retention, report serialization and publication. No executable reproduction. |
| Category | Sensitive information exposure |
| CWE | CWE-200 |
| Affected lines | src/edit.rs:2695-2751, src/edit.rs:2931-2939, src/edit.rs:5709-5720, src/edit.rs:1131-1132, src/edit/prepared.rs:873-886, src/bin/jubarte.rs:1397, src/bin/jubarte.rs:1487, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:194-206, src/edit.rs:2522-2526, src/edit.rs:2931-2939, src/edit.rs:5709-5720, src/edit.rs:2695-2751, src/edit.rs:2476-2518, src/edit.rs:4727-4735, src/edit.rs:1131-1132, src/bin/jubarte.rs:1397, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:194-206 |

#### Summary

A successful plan that redacts sensitive text and edits nearby words can remove the text from both DOCX files while retaining it in the adjacent edit's source-context field. The generated report and report-bearing MCP response disclose that text despite the documented privacy guarantee.

#### Root Cause

All operations resolve against untouched source. A Replace context includes up to twenty original characters on each side. resolve_one sanitizes only Redact's own outcome, leaving nearby normal outcomes unchanged. report clones all outcomes, and final check_redactions scans only document bytes before returning and publishing the report.

Limitations:

#### Dataflow

Original secret -\> nearby normal operation source context -\> unfiltered EditOutcome -\> EditReport -\> JSONL/JSON/MCP response.

- **Source:** Sensitive source text within another operation's context window

- **Sink:** Generated edit reports and report-bearing responses

- **Outcome:** Recipient recovers text absent from the visibly redacted DOCX.

#### Reachability

Public apply_plan returns report data; native CLI bundles and MCP docx_edit publish it. A recipient needs access to the report, not the original document.

- **Attacker:** Recipient of a purportedly redacted output/report; a document author can position sensitive text near an expected edit

- **Entry point:** Mixed redaction and ordinary-edit plan

- **Outcome:** Confidentiality loss beyond intended redacted output.

Preconditions:
- A redaction and nearby ordinary operation share a plan.
- Generated report or report-bearing response reaches a party lacking the original secret.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Sensitive document text crosses the intended redaction boundary into artifacts/responses a consumer may share. Impact is high for confidential content, with medium likelihood requiring a mixed plan and report exposure.

Lower when reports remain under the original document's access controls and are never shared; higher likelihood where bundles/reports are automatically distributed.

#### Remediation

Apply redaction-aware sanitization to every report, refusal and diagnostic field after resolving the full plan, including other operations' contexts. Check the final serialized reports for all redaction needles before publication, omitting unsafe context when needed.

Tests:
- Extend the existing adjacent redact+replace test to inspect EditReport, JSONL, CLI report.jsonl and MCP report.json/response for the removed identifier.
- Check mixed-plan failure outcomes and diagnostics as well as successful reports.
- Extend tests/scrub_and_redact.rs:353 mixed redact/replace case to assert secret absence from report JSON, JSONL and failure outcomes.

### [55] Unbounded numbering levels drive billions of renderer operations

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent verified unrestricted u32 parsing, list_marker/next_revised dispatch, dense reverse search and counter population directly in source; no timing or payload execution. |
| Category | Excessive iteration from numbering metadata |
| CWE | CWE-834 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/mod.rs:12711-12715, src/convert/mod.rs:5518-5532, src/convert/mod.rs:5610-5627, src/convert/mod.rs:6618-6622, src/convert/mod.rs:12828-12879, src/convert/mod.rs:591-613 |

#### Summary

An admitted DOCX paragraph requesting ilvl=4294967295 with an ordinary level-0 numbering definition makes resolve_ilvl perform about 4.3 billion lookups. Declaring that huge level instead causes next_marker to populate counters for every preceding level, exhausting memory.

#### Root Cause

The renderer treats a numbering level as any u32 and enumerates all smaller integer levels, instead of bounding the Word numbering domain or considering only declared keys.

**Paragraph level accepts any u32** — `src/convert/mod.rs:12707-12720`

Document ilvl flows to Numbering through list_marker.

```rust

        return (None, 0);

    let ilvl = first_named(dom, num, "ilvl")
        .and_then(|n| dom.attribute(n, &W::val()))
        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u32>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let num_id = first_named(dom, num, "numId")
        .and_then(|n| dom.attribute(n, &W::val()))
        .map(str::to_string);

}
```

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Markdown's separate reader clamps levels to 8 and is excluded from this particular finding.
- The optional CLI process timeout and recommended host limits can contain impact, but do not bound library work.

Limitations:
- No runtime or deployment testing.

#### Dataflow

Paragraph w:numPr/w:ilvl -\> num_pr(u32) -\> list_marker -\> Numbering::next_revised/next_marker -\> resolve_ilvl reverse scan or lower-level counter inserts.

#### Reachability

Any caller that renders attacker-controlled DOCX using the public renderer can trigger this without filesystem or configuration control. Native/Python/WASM wrappers share the renderer.

- **Attacker:** Document supplier

- **Entry point:** convert::render

Preconditions:
- DOCX has a matching numId and numbering definition; paragraph requests an extreme ilvl.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A document supplier can reliably monopolize or exhaust a rendering process through a tiny ordinary input. No remote service is assumed; the impact is denial of service of the consuming process.

Shared rendering without worker limits increases availability impact; bounded isolated workers limit the failure to one job.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Billions of CPU operations or counter allocations can deny service to the process.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** The finite u32 maximum is practically unbounded and directly drives loops.

#### Remediation

Validate paragraph, style, abstract-level and override ilvl values against supported numbering levels before use. Find a parent by examining declared keys and avoid populating nonexistent levels. Return a normal refusal for unsupported values.

Tests:
- Render rejects u32::MAX paragraph and declared numbering levels before iteration.
- Undefined ordinary levels still resolve to supported parents; Markdown remains bounded.

### [56] Rendering an HTML chunk can allocate gigabytes from a single colspan value

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Both independent baseline and focused investigator identified the mechanism; parent verified input parsing, post-admission expansion and allocation loop statically. No runtime reproduction was executed. |
| Category | Uncontrolled resource allocation Unbounded allocation from HTML numeric input Unbounded generated markup expansion Unbounded allocation through HTML table expansion |
| CWE | CWE-789, CWE-400, CWE-770, CWE-834 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/mod.rs:772-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:33-39, src/convert/altchunk.rs:557-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-491, src/convert/mod.rs:789-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:34-39, src/convert/altchunk.rs:558-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-490, src/convert/altchunk.rs:558-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-490, src/convert/mod.rs:789-800, src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:34-39, src/convert/mod.rs:773-798, src/convert/mod.rs:422-460, src/convert/mod.rs:762-799, src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-493, src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-566, src/convert/mod.rs:769-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:463-490, src/convert/mod.rs:789-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-566, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-476, src/convert/altchunk.rs:488-491, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-490, src/convert/mod.rs:789-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:559-568, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-476, src/convert/altchunk.rs:489-493, src/convert/mod.rs:776-799, src/admission.rs:535-558 |

#### Summary

A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates colspan=1000000000 causing tens of gigabytes of generated XML and work before layout; rejecting invalid, negative or zero spans does not bound valid positive values. Assigned discovery-0032 supplies a static colspan=1000000000 framing of one billion 20-byte grid elements, about 20 GB of generated text before DOM construction; this is not a runtime measurement.

#### Root Cause

with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later. The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output. The XML output loop precedes layout/page raster bounds; rejecting only overflowing sums would leave a single enormous valid machine-integer span reachable. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates colspan=1000000000 causing tens of gigabytes of generated XML and work before layout; rejecting invalid, negative or zero spans does not bound valid positive values. Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): `with_layout()` admits the original package, then `altchunk::expand()` imports the relationship-backed HTML. `Builder::start()` parses `td`/`th` spans as unrestricted positive `usize` values. `Builder::end_table()` sums them and writes `cols` grid elements to a `String`. Neither the span nor generated bytes are bounded; admission cannot limit this post-admission amplification.

```rust
pub fn docx_to_pdf_with(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    Ok(docx_to_pdf_report(docx, options)?.pdf)

/// Render a DOCX package to PDF and return the font-resolution report for
/// it. The PDF is the `pdf` field of the result; the font report is the
/// entries the conversion made for that document.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`docx_to_pdf_with`].
pub fn docx_to_pdf_report(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<ConvertedPdf, ConvertError> {
    let (result, font_report) = font::with_font_report(|| docx_to_pdf_inner(docx, options));
    Ok(ConvertedPdf {
        pdf: result?,
        font_report,
    })
}

fn docx_to_pdf_inner(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_options(options, || docx_to_pdf_body(docx, options))
}

fn docx_to_pdf_body(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
```

```rust
fn with_pages<T>(

        .part_string(&main)

    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

```rust
pub(crate) fn expand(xml: &str, load: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(xml.len());
    let mut rest = xml;
```

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],

) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;

        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
```

```
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;

    let table = font_table::load_font_table(&pkg);
    let mut embedded = font_table::load_embedded_fonts(&pkg, &table);
```

**conversion public** — `src/convert/mod.rs:436-460`

```rust
pub fn docx_to_pdf_with(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    Ok(docx_to_pdf_report(docx, options)?.pdf)
}

/// Render a DOCX package to PDF and return the font-resolution report for
/// it. The PDF is the `pdf` field of the result; the font report is the
/// entries the conversion made for that document.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`docx_to_pdf_with`].
pub fn docx_to_pdf_report(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<ConvertedPdf, ConvertError> {
    let (result, font_report) = font::with_font_report(|| docx_to_pdf_inner(docx, options));
    Ok(ConvertedPdf {
        pdf: result?,
        font_report,
    })
}

fn docx_to_pdf_inner(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_options(options, || docx_to_pdf_body(docx, options))
}

fn docx_to_pdf_body(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_pages(docx, |fonts, pages| pdf::emit(fonts, pages, options))
```

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

**chunk repeat** — `src/convert/altchunk.rs:15-43`

Each altChunk reference is loaded, decoded to HTML and converted by html_to_wml.

```rust
pub(crate) fn expand(xml: &str, load: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(xml.len());
    let mut rest = xml;
    while let Some(at) = rest.find("<w:altChunk") {
        out.push_str(&rest[..at]);
        let tail = &rest[at..];
        let Some(open_end) = tail.find('>') else {
            // The prefix has already been copied; retain only the unfinished
            // chunk suffix when this diagnostic input cannot be expanded.
            out.push_str(tail);
            return out;
        };
        let open = &tail[..=open_end];
        let end = if open.ends_with("/>") {
            open_end + 1
        } else {
            tail.find("</w:altChunk>")
                .map_or(open_end + 1, |i| i + "</w:altChunk>".len())
        };
        let wml = attr(open, "id")
            .and_then(|rid| load(&rid))
            .and_then(|bytes| chunk_html(&bytes))
            .map(|html| html_to_wml(&html))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        out.push_str(&wml);
        rest = &tail[end..];
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
```

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
```

```rust
                );
```

```rust
            s.push_str("</w:tblBorders>");
        }
        s.push_str("<w:tblLayout w:type=\"fixed\"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid>");
        for _ in 0..cols {
```

**conversion layout** — `src/convert/mod.rs:759-804`

Admission happens before HTML expansion; the referenced chunk bytes are sent to altchunk::expand and resulting XML goes straight to a DOM.

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

#### Reachability

Default public PDF/PNG converter expands internal altChunk parts after admission. Attacker needs only control over a document processed by the victim. Untrusted document suppliers reach this importer whenever the public renderer processes their DOCX. The input need not be large, and no release/OS authority is needed. Public Rust PDF/render APIs and Python/WASM wrappers accept document bytes. A normal table in an internal HTML altChunk reaches this path after admission; no special host setting or raised input limits are required.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted DOCX author untrusted document supplier Provider of an untrusted document rendered by a victim/library consumer

- **Entry point:** convert::docx_to_pdf / render convert::docx_to_pdf and shared layout/render APIs convert::docx_to_pdf / convert::render and bindings

- **Outcome:** Memory/CPU exhaustion and process termination or WASM failure

Preconditions:
- Victim invokes document rendering on the supplied file.
- Victim renders a document containing the supplied chunk.
- Victim renders attacker-supplied DOCX containing an internal HTML/MHT altChunk.

Existing controls:
- Original archive and XML limits apply before conversion.
- External process resource limits can contain impact.

Limitations:
- No file disclosure or code execution established.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. Loss of embedding process/instance availability.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** No special feature option or external resource is needed; a small valid HTML chunk suffices. A small numeric HTML field directly determines work.

#### Remediation

Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/aggregate column counts before generating any table XML. Charge all HTML/MHT-generated WML, including repeated/nested tables, to a cumulative byte/work budget inside altChunk expansion and return a typed input-limit refusal before allocation or DOM construction. Additional retained remediation detail: Bound individual spans and aggregate columns before summation or iteration, use checked arithmetic, and impose a cumulative generated-WML byte/element budget shared across every HTML/MHT altChunk. Refuse excessive expansion with a typed input-limit error before allocation.

Tests:

- Check multi-cell aggregate span overflow and repeated/nested table expansion budgets.
- Excessive individual/cumulative colspan in HTML and MHT must fail with bounded output/work.

- Preserve valid small HTML tables.
- Unit tests with a small configured column cap cover the inclusive limit, one above it, oversized numeric values, and sums of several otherwise valid spans.
- Integration test through a DOCX altChunk confirms refusal occurs before grid generation.
- Use a tiny in-memory altChunk HTML with excessive td/th colspan and assert a prompt typed refusal without output growth.
- Exercise cumulative spans across multiple cells, numeric overflow and valid inclusive limits.
- A tiny altChunk with colspan 1000000000 must fail before large output allocation.
- Cover inclusive limits, cumulative spans across cells, integer overflow, nested tables, and both HTML and MHT import.
- Reject an oversized colspan in a small admitted DOCX without allocating proportional output.
- Cover aggregate spans across multiple cells and arithmetic overflow while preserving normal merged tables.
- A one-cell HTML table with an excessive numeric colspan returns a typed refusal without allocating proportional output.
- Multiple spans cannot overflow the cumulative count or bypass the generated-grid limit.
- Ordinary bounded colspan tables retain rendering behavior.
- Reject huge representable positive colspan through public rendering while retaining ordinary span behavior.
- Verify many bounded spans cannot exceed the cumulative table/output budget.
- Verify row-span sum overflow returns a refusal on native and wasm32.
- Exercise a compact HTML chunk with huge positive colspan and require bounded refusal before WML generation.
- Refuse a single td/th with colspan=4294967295 without allocating proportional output.
- Refuse rows whose individually valid spans exceed the aggregate column budget; preserve ordinary merged-cell rendering.

- Verify rendering a DOCX carrying the oversized altChunk returns a bounded error.

Preventive controls:
- Charge representation expansion to explicit output/work budgets rather than relying only on compressed/inflated input limits.
- Budget derived representations before materialization, including post-admission HTML/MHT expansion.

#### Summary

Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate.

#### Root Cause

raster_wmf checks declared size\*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable. With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification. A seven-word EXTTEXTOUT record contains its six-byte header and eight-byte fixed fields but can start its 65535-byte text range at the next record, because only whole-file bounds are checked. Assigned discovery-0016 adds a same-function-header proof: repeated six-byte size=3/0x0A32 headers cause count at off+10 to read the next function (2610), options at off+12 to read size (3), and optional-rectangle text to start at off+22. Nonzero mapping extents, nonblank bytes and sufficient trailing data retain overlapping Strings; roughly 6 MB of records request about 2.6 GB of strings. These are source-derived estimates. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Text record handlers do not constrain field/string reads to the declared record extent, allowing small records to repeatedly materialize overlapping bytes as owned strings.

```rust
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
        }
    }
    Some(pts)
```

```rust
/// Render a DOCX package to PDF and return the font-resolution report for
/// it. The PDF is the `pdf` field of the result; the font report is the
/// entries the conversion made for that document.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`docx_to_pdf_with`].
pub fn docx_to_pdf_report(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<ConvertedPdf, ConvertError> {
    let (result, font_report) = font::with_font_report(|| docx_to_pdf_inner(docx, options));
    Ok(ConvertedPdf {
        pdf: result?,
        font_report,
    })
}

fn docx_to_pdf_inner(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_options(options, || docx_to_pdf_body(docx, options))
}

fn docx_to_pdf_body(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_pages(docx, |fonts, pages| pdf::emit(fonts, pages, options))
```

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

```rust
/// Windows-1252 text, one byte a character.
fn ansi_text(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    const HIGH: [char; 32] = [
        '€', '\u{81}', '‚', 'ƒ', '„', '…', '†', '‡', 'ˆ', '‰', 'Š', '‹', 'Œ', '\u{8d}', 'Ž',
        '\u{8f}', '\u{90}', '‘', '’', '“', '”', '•', '–', '—', '˜', '™', 'š', '›', 'œ', '\u{9d}',
        'ž', 'Ÿ',
    ];
    bytes
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| match b {
            0x80..=0x9F => HIGH[usize::from(b - 0x80)],
            _ => char::from(b),
        })
        .collect()
```

```rust
fn decode_image(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Option<ImageKind> {
    if let Some((width, height, rgb, texts)) = metafile::render(&bytes) {
```
```
        let raster = ImageKind::Rgb {
```
```rust
            width,
            height,
            bytes: rgb,
            alpha: None,
        };
        if texts.is_empty() {
            return Some(raster);
        }
        return Some(ImageKind::Metafile {
            raster: Box::new(raster),
            texts: texts.into(),
        });
```

```
fn wmf_text(dc: &WmfState, map: &Map, x: i16, y: i16, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<MetaText> {
    let text = ansi_text(bytes);
    if text.trim().is_empty() || map.ext_x.abs() < f32::EPSILON || map.ext_y.abs() < f32::EPSILON {
        return None;
    }
    let font = dc.font.as_deref();
    let height = font.map_or(0, |f| f.height);
    Some(MetaText {
        text,
        x: (f32::from(x) - map.org_x) / map.ext_x,
        y: (f32::from(y) - map.org_y) / map.ext_y,
        // lfHeight 0 is the default font, 12pt at 96 dpi of a 1440 inch.
        size: if height == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            f32::from(height.unsigned_abs()) / map.ext_y.abs()
        },
        cell: height > 0,
        family: font.map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.face.clone()),
        bold: font.is_some_and(|f| f.weight >= 600),
        italic: font.is_some_and(|f| f.italic),
        color: dc.text_color,
        align: dc.text_align,
        aspect: (map.ext_x / map.ext_y).abs(),
    })
```

#### Validation

Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed. Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost. Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites. Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. /// Render a DOCX package to PDF and return the font-resolution report for
```rust
/// it. The PDF is the `pdf` field of the result; the font report is the
/// entries the conversion made for that document.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`docx_to_pdf_with`].
pub fn docx_to_pdf_report(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<ConvertedPdf, ConvertError> {
    let (result, font_report) = font::with_font_report(|| docx_to_pdf_inner(docx, options));
    Ok(ConvertedPdf {
        pdf: result?,
        font_report,
    })
}

fn docx_to_pdf_inner(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_options(options, || docx_to_pdf_body(docx, options))
}

fn docx_to_pdf_body(docx: &[u8], options: PdfOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConvertError> {
    with_pages(docx, |fonts, pages| pdf::emit(fonts, pages, options))
```

```rust
/// The shared layout pipeline: open, resolve fonts, lay out, then hand the
/// pages to `emit`.
fn with_pages<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page]) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    with_layout(docx, |fonts, pages, _| emit(fonts, pages))
}

/// [`with_pages`] that also hands `emit` the layout's page facts.
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
    let root = dom.root(doc).ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let body = dom
        .descendants(root, Some(&W::body()))
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
```

```rust
fn ansi_text(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    const HIGH: [char; 32] = [
        '€', '\u{81}', '‚', 'ƒ', '„', '…', '†', '‡', 'ˆ', '‰', 'Š', '‹', 'Œ', '\u{8d}', 'Ž',
        '\u{8f}', '\u{90}', '‘', '’', '“', '”', '•', '–', '—', '˜', '™', 'š', '›', 'œ', '\u{9d}',
        'ž', 'Ÿ',
    ];
    bytes
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| match b {
            0x80..=0x9F => HIGH[usize::from(b - 0x80)],
            _ => char::from(b),

        .collect()
```

**Independent text allocation retained in MetaText** — `src/convert/metafile.rs:692-716`

Independent text allocation retained in MetaText. This step carries attacker WMF bytes through outcome in the verified flow: embedded a:blip -\> resolve_media -\> decode_image -\> metafile::render -\> raster_wmf -\> full-file text ranges -\> MetaText Strings.

```
fn wmf_text(dc: &WmfState, map: &Map, x: i16, y: i16, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<MetaText> {
    let text = ansi_text(bytes);
    if text.trim().is_empty() || map.ext_x.abs() < f32::EPSILON || map.ext_y.abs() < f32::EPSILON {
        return None;
    }
    let font = dc.font.as_deref();
    let height = font.map_or(0, |f| f.height);
    Some(MetaText {
        text,
        x: (f32::from(x) - map.org_x) / map.ext_x,
        y: (f32::from(y) - map.org_y) / map.ext_y,
        // lfHeight 0 is the default font, 12pt at 96 dpi of a 1440 inch.
        size: if height == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            f32::from(height.unsigned_abs()) / map.ext_y.abs()
        },
        cell: height > 0,
        family: font.map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.face.clone()),
        bold: font.is_some_and(|f| f.weight >= 600),
        italic: font.is_some_and(|f| f.italic),
        color: dc.text_color,
        align: dc.text_align,
        aspect: (map.ext_x / map.ext_y).abs(),
    })
```

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- MAX_SIDE=384 bounds raster dimensions; it does not restrict how often subsequent bytes are parsed.
- Safe slice reads eventually reject truncation, after earlier records have already performed amplified work.
- EMF read_emf_points has record-end bounds; it does not protect the WMF handlers.
- Whole-buffer slice checks prevent Rust memory unsafety; this is parser resource amplification.
- WMF object count is clamped and canvas MAX_SIDE is 384, but neither controls the texts vector.
- Valid record-local counts would consume input proportionally and would not produce this overlap.
- Canvas dimensions are capped at 384 per side and hostile coordinates are clipped; these controls do not bound retained strings.
- Record size must be at least three words and the cursor advances, preventing a zero-length infinite loop.
- Whole-file Rust slice bounds avoid arbitrary memory reads; the finding concerns invalid record extents and resource amplification.
- ZIP admission charges original media bytes rather than repeated decoding of overlapping record suffixes.
- Input compressed/inflated limits remain, but do not charge repeatedly allocated text.
- Canvas max384side constrains pixels, not texts.
- Image decoder default512MiB limit is later than metafile processing.
- Caller CPU/memory containment policy limits deployment impact.
- WMF canvas side is capped at 384 and record size arithmetic is checked; neither bounds retained strings.
- InputLimits bounds compressed/inflated package bytes and XML depth, not WMF logical text.
- An operator's process limits can contain impact; no production deployment was established.
- Checked outer multiplication and file bounds prevent file-offset wrap, but not cross-record payload consumption.
- Canvas capped at384 pixels/side, strokes clipped and arithmetic widened; text and repeated geometry remain unbounded by record size.
- EMF read_emf_points uses per-record bounds; finding limited to WMF.
- Archive budgets/process limits do not bound overlapping interpretations.
- Canvas sides are capped at384 and stroke lines are clipped; those do not cap counted string/point decoding.
- Counts are u16-bounded individually, but can be repeated many times against shared suffix data.
- Archive inflation limits bound original media bytes only.
- No out-of-bounds memory access or code execution is claimed.
- checked_mul prevents size/iterator wrap, not cross-record reads.
- Each n is u16-bounded; multiplicative aggregate retention remains.
- 384-pixel canvas cap and stroke clipping do not limit texts.
- Sibling EMF point parsing uses record bounds; this finding concerns the two WMF text branches.
- Checked multiplication bounds outer offset progression; this is not an out-of-buffer read.
- Canvas dimensions are capped at 384, but text storage is separate.
- ZIP admission bounds original media bytes, not overlapping text-copy work.
- All reads remain within the file buffer, so this is not an out-of-bounds memory-read finding.
- Record size arithmetic is checked and object count/raster dimensions are bounded.
- Blank strings or degenerate extents are skipped; a nondegenerate metafile with nonblank bytes reaches retention.

Limitations:
- No application code, tests, exploit input or network activity executed.
- No runtime reproduction; exact heap growth/failure depends on String allocation and host limits.
- Geometry siblings also use full-file readers; only the text-allocation consequences are independently validated here.
- Source-derived construction only; no application, payload or memory measurement executed.
- No malicious WMF/DOCX generated or executed.
- The several-GiB estimate is derived from bytes copied and loop advancement, not measured.
- Final current-source check: every retained codeEvidence range exactly matched the live authorized checkout after its observed HEAD change; no historical revision was inspected.
- No malicious file was constructed and no application code was executed.
- No runtime malicious WMF constructed or executed; no remote deployment assumed.
- No crafted media or render execution; impact inferred from retained strings and counted loops.
- Actual OOM threshold and UTF8 size vary by host/bytes; no runtime reproduction.
- No malformed input or application code was executed.
- No vulnerability-triggering file was created or executed.
- Exact peak memory and runtime failure threshold are unmeasured; other metafile record variants were not exhaustively audited.
- No hostile WMF construction or application execution.
- Exact memory and timing thresholds unmeasured.

```rust
fn read_emf_points(data: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize, pts16: bool) -> Option<Vec<(i32, i32)>> {
    let count = read_u32(data, off + 24)? as usize;
    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(4096));
    let mut p = off + 28;
    for _ in 0..count {
        if pts16 {
            if p + 4 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            let x = read_i16(data, p)? as i32;
            let y = read_i16(data, p + 2)? as i32;
            pts.push((x, y));
            p += 4;
        } else {
            if p + 8 > off + size {
                break;
            }
            pts.push((read_i32(data, p)?, read_i32(data, p + 4)?));
            p += 8;
        }
    }
    Some(pts)
```
