#### Reachability

Victim renders a DOCX referencing attacker-controlled placeable WMF bytes. The attacker controls embedded media in a document consumed by the renderer, with no release credentials or nondefault configuration. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Public DOCX rendering decodes embedded WMF bytes from the package. A document author controls the record sizes and later bytes without needing host filesystem or release authority.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author untrusted document supplier Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: An untrusted document/image author.

- **Entry point:** Public PDF/PNG renderer convert public rendering APIs

- **Outcome:** Excessive allocation/work and host-process or WASM instance failure

Preconditions:
- Victim renders a DOCX referencing attacker-controlled placeable WMF bytes.
- Victim renders a DOCX containing a WMF with nondegenerate bounds and malformed text records.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.

Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Process memory exhaustion or termination.
- **Why:** Host processing availability can be lost; no confidentiality or code-execution gain is established. Host/instance availability loss.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Compact malformed records are accepted on ordinary embedded-image rendering paths.
- **Why:** A document supplier controls the triggering parser inputs with no privileged configuration. Malformed binary counts reach a built-in parser directly and bypass otherwise bounded stored input.

#### Remediation

Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

Tests:
- Short WMF polygon, polypolygon and polyline records claiming following-record points must refuse before processing points.
- Repeated malformed records must consume work proportional to declared bytes, with EMF behavior retained.
- Deterministic parser tests with short declared records and text counts extending into the next record must refuse safely.
- Cover EXTTEXTOUT options/rectangle, TEXTOUT padding and record-local geometry counts with small resource budgets.
- Reject EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT strings extending into the next record.
- Reject cross-record polygon/polypolygon/polyline coordinates and validate large valid records within aggregate text/geometry budgets.
- Use existing in-memory WMF fixtures to ensure six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT cannot read subsequent records.
- Verify repeated undersized records produce no retained text.
- Retain valid text rendering tests and exercise cumulative text-budget refusal.
- Small malformed EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT records must be rejected without reading following bytes.
- Repeated short records must remain within deterministic cumulative allocation/work limits.
- Verify valid WMF text still renders through public PDF/PNG APIs.
- Exercise short TEXTOUT, EXTTEXTOUT, POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE records with sufficient trailing bytes; require refusal without consuming the next record.
- Refuse textout/exttextout/polygon/polypolygon/polyline counts extending beyond their record despite sufficient following file bytes.
- Verify repeated small records cannot amplify trailing content into unbounded retained output.
- Refuse EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT whose counts or coordinate fields extend past their own record even when still inside the file.
- Ensure many valid records hit a bounded aggregate text budget and ordinary WMF text stays supported.
- Reject header-only TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT records even when later file bytes can satisfy their reads.
- Bound aggregate extracted text and test valid records exactly at declared boundaries.
- Exercise undersized text records using small harmless limits and assert refusal without reading following-record bytes.
- Verify aggregate text budgets and normal EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records; avoid allocating attacker-sized outputs.
- Undersized TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT refuses before text retention.
- POLYGON/POLYPOLYGON/POLYLINE counts cannot consume following records.
- Valid WMF and EMF rendering remains supported.

Preventive controls:
- Bound the actual representation depth and processing work at the consuming boundary.
- Pass bounded record slices to all metafile handlers instead of exposing the entire backing file.

#### Summary

An attacker-authored Word 97–2003 DOC can repeatedly begin fields and enter their result sections, leaving an increasingly long all-false field stack. Story::blocks scans the entire stack before every input character, giving quadratic CPU work during reading/conversion and even the native Word-input refusal hint. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a balanced result-state framing with approximately 100000 nested fields in a few hundred kilobytes, implying billions of boolean inspections. This is heap-stack scanning CPU cost, not recursive call-stack overflow.

#### Root Cause

The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec\<bool\> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec\<bool\> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a balanced result-state framing with approximately 100000 nested fields in a few hundred kilobytes, implying billions of boolean inspections. This is heap-stack scanning CPU cost, not recursive call-stack overflow.

**Control preservation** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:1115-1129`

cp1252 preserves ASCII-range field markers.

```rust
/// Windows-1252 bytes 0x80-0x9F as the spec's compressed-text table maps
/// them (MS-DOC 2.4.1); every other byte is its own code point.
fn cp1252(byte: u8) -> char {
    const HIGH: [u16; 32] = [
        0x20AC, 0x0081, 0x201A, 0x0192, 0x201E, 0x2026, 0x2020, 0x2021, 0x02C6, 0x2030, 0x0160,
        0x2039, 0x0152, 0x008D, 0x017D, 0x008F, 0x0090, 0x2018, 0x2019, 0x201C, 0x201D, 0x2022,
        0x2013, 0x2014, 0x02DC, 0x2122, 0x0161, 0x203A, 0x0153, 0x009D, 0x017E, 0x0178,
    ];
    match byte {
        0x80..=0x9F => HIGH
            .get(usize::from(byte.wrapping_sub(0x80)))
            .and_then(|&unit| char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)))
            .unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'),
        _ => char::from(byte),
    }
```

```rust
            papx: &papx,
            chpx: &chpx,
            styles: &[],
            lists: &lists,
            section_marks: Vec::new(),

        let texts: Vec<String> = story
            .blocks(&chars)
            .iter()
            .map(|b| match b {
                Block::Paragraph(p) => p.text(),
                Block::Table(_) => "table".into(),
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(texts, ["aoneb"]);
    }
```

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
}
```

#### Validation

Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -\> main_text -\> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection. Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -\> legacy_doc::read -\> main_text -\> Story::blocks -\> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops. Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For \[0x13,0x14\] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): For n nested begin/separator pairs left in their result state, each separator and subsequent character scans an increasing all-false vector. Closing them later or supplying n result characters preserves quadratic comparisons. No text reuse or physical-offset violation is required. Supplied discovery-0030 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Verified that legacy public read constructs Story and calls blocks on decoded main-text characters, and that CLI compound-file conversion reaches that API. For n begin/separator pairs the all-false scans cost 1+2+...+n; balanced end fields do not remove prior work. Supplied discovery-0029 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): After N begin/separator pairs the stack contains N false entries. Processing successive pairs examines prefixes of length 0..N, totaling Theta(N^2) boolean checks; N closing field markers can also scan decreasing false prefixes. A single physical text piece is sufficient, so bounding repeated physical ranges does not remediate this separate complexity failure.

Validation method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

**Control preservation** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:1115-1129`

cp1252 preserves ASCII-range field markers.

```rust
/// Windows-1252 bytes 0x80-0x9F as the spec's compressed-text table maps
/// them (MS-DOC 2.4.1); every other byte is its own code point.
fn cp1252(byte: u8) -> char {
    const HIGH: [u16; 32] = [
        0x20AC, 0x0081, 0x201A, 0x0192, 0x201E, 0x2026, 0x2020, 0x2021, 0x02C6, 0x2030, 0x0160,
        0x2039, 0x0152, 0x008D, 0x017D, 0x008F, 0x0090, 0x2018, 0x2019, 0x201C, 0x201D, 0x2022,
        0x2013, 0x2014, 0x02DC, 0x2122, 0x0161, 0x203A, 0x0153, 0x009D, 0x017E, 0x0178,
    ];
    match byte {
        0x80..=0x9F => HIGH
            .get(usize::from(byte.wrapping_sub(0x80)))
            .and_then(|&unit| char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)))
            .unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'),
        _ => char::from(byte),
    }
```

```rust
    fn a_field_nested_in_a_field_code_shows_only_the_outer_result() {

        // { IF { PAGE } = 1 "one" } displaying "one": the PAGE result "1"
        // sits in the outer field's code and is not shown.
        let chars = story_chars("a\u{13}IF \u{13}PAGE\u{14}1\u{15} = 1 \"one\"\u{14}one\u{15}b\r");

            chpx: &chpx,
            styles: &[],
            lists: &lists,
            section_marks: Vec::new(),

        let texts: Vec<String> = story
            .blocks(&chars)
            .iter()
            .map(|b| match b {
                Block::Paragraph(p) => p.text(),
                Block::Table(_) => "table".into(),
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(texts, ["aoneb"]);
```

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
}
```

#### Reachability

A legacy DOC author controls the story passed to legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown, doc_to_docx and native CLI convert. Native Word-input refusal also reads the DOC for its conversion hint. A valid OLE container, Word FIB and covering piece table are required; no privileged configuration is needed. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Caller-controlled legacy DOC is decoded by public read/doc conversion APIs and native CLI legacy conversion or diagnostic rejection-hint processing. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): The public reader invokes Story::blocks after decoding main text; conversion and native refusal hints share it.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: An untrusted legacy document author. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Legacy DOC supplier

- **Entry point:** legacy_doc::read / doc_to_markdown / doc_to_docx; native CLI convert and read_document refusal hint Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): legacy_doc::read/doc_to_docx/doc_to_markdown and native CLI

- **Outcome:** Quadratic CPU consumption

Preconditions:
- Victim processes a legacy DOC with deeply nested field-result state.
- Victim reads an unencrypted structurally valid DOC with nested field controls.

Existing controls:
- any() short-circuits for true code-state entries, but the producer puts every active field into false result state.
- No field depth cap or aggregate active-code counter is applied.
- The sequence can close every field after the payload; unmatched fields are unnecessary.

Limitations:
- Memory-safe reads remain bounded; no arbitrary code execution or confidentiality impact is established.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Small untrusted document input can cause disproportionate CPU consumption through public legacy conversion APIs. This affects host availability; shared-server exposure is not assumed and process CPU limits constrain impact.

Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): high
- **Rationale:** Processing-thread CPU exhaustion and conversion service degradation. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: CPU denial of service of processing host.
- **Why:** Repeated nested field beginnings followed by separators leave an increasingly long all-false field-state stack. Each subsequent character scans that stack. Approximately 300 KiB of balanced field delimiters at depth 100000 requires billions of Boolean examinations, consuming substantial CPU before returning. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Quadratic CPU consumption

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): medium
- **Rationale:** The algorithmic amplification requires only crafted field text, not privileged configuration. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Small input reaches quadratic logic on supported parser paths.
- **Why:** The triggering structure and values are document-controlled and not rejected by existing guards. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Victim must process attacker input through the cited public interface.

#### Remediation

Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work. Keep legacy diagnostic probes cheap and bounded, or enforce the same field/work budgets before invoking the full reader solely for a refusal hint.

- Assert work scales linearly for deeply nested balanced result-phase fields.
- Preserve nested-code suppression semantics, repeated separators and unmatched field-marker behavior.
- Extend existing nested-field fixtures with deeply nested balanced result fields.
- Assert linear parser operations with a deterministic counter rather than wall-clock timing.

### [59] Converting a small HTML altChunk can exhaust memory

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Source directly connects admitted document relationships to colspan parsing and the proportional output loop; no configuration prerequisite is needed. |
| Category | resource-exhaustion |
| CWE | CWE-400 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-567, src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-490, src/convert/mod.rs:773-798 |

#### Summary

An attacker-controlled HTML table colspan inside a DOCX altChunk is parsed as an unrestricted usize and expanded into one generated WML gridCol per column. A short decimal span can force billions of XML tags before rendering, bypassing admission limits on the original package.

#### Root Cause

with_layout admits the original ZIP, then expands internal HTML chunks. HTML td/th colspan values become usize cell spans with only a lower bound. end_table sums them and emits a gridCol tag for every column into a String. Package byte/XML budgets do not apply to this newly generated representation.

The attacker-controlled package's internal relationship bytes reach altChunk expansion after original-package admission. Generated output has no intervening budget.

A tiny input value expands into an unbounded String, exhausting memory or CPU before the WML table layout can reject it.

Limitations:
- No application code or malicious input was executed.
- The host's memory/CPU limits determine the final termination behavior.

#### Dataflow

untrusted internal HTML part -\> chunk_html -\> html_to_wml -\> td/th colspan -\> cell span sum -\> unbounded gridCol output String

#### Reachability

Public convert::render and its PDF/PNG/report wrappers share with_layout, which expands internal altChunks after admission.

- **Attacker:** document author

- **Entry point:** DOCX conversion APIs

- **Outcome:** processing-process memory or CPU exhaustion

Existing controls:
- Original ZIP size, inflated bytes and XML depth limits remain active, but the short HTML attribute fits within them.
- External resources are not fetched; this attack uses an internal part.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Document-supplied input deterministically triggers unbounded CPU and memory amplification in public conversion paths. Impact is availability of the processing process; no shared-service deployment is assumed.

Process memory/CPU isolation limits collateral impact. Enforcing bounded numeric spans and aggregate generated-output limits prevents the expansion.

#### Remediation

Reject excessive per-cell and aggregate HTML column spans using checked arithmetic before output generation, and charge all altChunk-generated XML against an explicit expansion budget.

Tests:
- Integration-test a tiny internal HTML chunk with a span above the configured cap and require a typed refusal before expansion.
- Test exact span/output-budget limits, multiple-cell sum overflow and ordinary colspan rendering.

#### Summary

An attacker-authored Word 97–2003 DOC can repeatedly begin fields and enter their result sections, leaving an increasingly long all-false field stack. Story::blocks scans the entire stack before every input character, giving quadratic CPU work during reading/conversion and even the native Word-input refusal hint. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a balanced result-state framing with approximately 100000 nested fields in a few hundred kilobytes, implying billions of boolean inspections. This is heap-stack scanning CPU cost, not recursive call-stack overflow.

#### Root Cause

The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec\<bool\> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec\<bool\> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a balanced result-state framing with approximately 100000 nested fields in a few hundred kilobytes, implying billions of boolean inspections. This is heap-stack scanning CPU cost, not recursive call-stack overflow.

**Control preservation** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:1115-1129`

cp1252 preserves ASCII-range field markers.

```rust
/// Windows-1252 bytes 0x80-0x9F as the spec's compressed-text table maps
/// them (MS-DOC 2.4.1); every other byte is its own code point.
fn cp1252(byte: u8) -> char {
    const HIGH: [u16; 32] = [
        0x20AC, 0x0081, 0x201A, 0x0192, 0x201E, 0x2026, 0x2020, 0x2021, 0x02C6, 0x2030, 0x0160,
        0x2039, 0x0152, 0x008D, 0x017D, 0x008F, 0x0090, 0x2018, 0x2019, 0x201C, 0x201D, 0x2022,
        0x2013, 0x2014, 0x02DC, 0x2122, 0x0161, 0x203A, 0x0153, 0x009D, 0x017E, 0x0178,
    ];
    match byte {
        0x80..=0x9F => HIGH
            .get(usize::from(byte.wrapping_sub(0x80)))
            .and_then(|&unit| char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)))
            .unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'),
        _ => char::from(byte),
    }
```

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
```
```
    })
```

```rust
    })?;

        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })

    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
```
```
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
```
```rust
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
```

```rust
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
}
```

```
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {
        // Only a .doc that converts gets the hint; an encrypted document
        // or another OLE file would be sent to a command that fails.
        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
            format!(
                "; a .doc converts with: jubarte convert {} -o {}",
                path.display(),
                path.with_extension("docx").display()
            )
        } else {
            String::new()
        };
        return Err(format!("{refused}{hint}"));
```

**Public legacy reader sends decoded characters to Story** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:180-216`

The file's main story becomes chars and is passed to Story::blocks.

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
```

#### Validation

Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -\> main_text -\> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection. Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -\> legacy_doc::read -\> main_text -\> Story::blocks -\> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops. Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For \[0x13,0x14\] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): For n nested begin/separator pairs left in their result state, each separator and subsequent character scans an increasing all-false vector. Closing them later or supplying n result characters preserves quadratic comparisons. No text reuse or physical-offset violation is required. Supplied discovery-0030 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Verified that legacy public read constructs Story and calls blocks on decoded main-text characters, and that CLI compound-file conversion reaches that API. For n begin/separator pairs the all-false scans cost 1+2+...+n; balanced end fields do not remove prior work. Supplied discovery-0029 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): After N begin/separator pairs the stack contains N false entries. Processing successive pairs examines prefixes of length 0..N, totaling Theta(N^2) boolean checks; N closing field markers can also scan decreasing false prefixes. A single physical text piece is sufficient, so bounding repeated physical ranges does not remediate this separate complexity failure.

Validation method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

**Control preservation** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:1115-1129`

cp1252 preserves ASCII-range field markers.

```rust
/// Windows-1252 bytes 0x80-0x9F as the spec's compressed-text table maps
/// them (MS-DOC 2.4.1); every other byte is its own code point.
fn cp1252(byte: u8) -> char {
    const HIGH: [u16; 32] = [
        0x20AC, 0x0081, 0x201A, 0x0192, 0x201E, 0x2026, 0x2020, 0x2021, 0x02C6, 0x2030, 0x0160,
        0x2039, 0x0152, 0x008D, 0x017D, 0x008F, 0x0090, 0x2018, 0x2019, 0x201C, 0x201D, 0x2022,
        0x2013, 0x2014, 0x02DC, 0x2122, 0x0161, 0x203A, 0x0153, 0x009D, 0x017E, 0x0178,
    ];
    match byte {
        0x80..=0x9F => HIGH
            .get(usize::from(byte.wrapping_sub(0x80)))
            .and_then(|&unit| char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)))
            .unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'),
        _ => char::from(byte),
    }
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn a_field_nested_in_a_field_code_shows_only_the_outer_result() {
        let (papx, chpx) = (FkpIndex { runs: Vec::new() }, FkpIndex { runs: Vec::new() });
        let lists = Lists::default();
        // { IF { PAGE } = 1 "one" } displaying "one": the PAGE result "1"
        // sits in the outer field's code and is not shown.
        let chars = story_chars("a\u{13}IF \u{13}PAGE\u{14}1\u{15} = 1 \"one\"\u{14}one\u{15}b\r");
        let story = Story {
            papx: &papx,
            chpx: &chpx,
            styles: &[],
            lists: &lists,
            section_marks: Vec::new(),
        };
        let texts: Vec<String> = story
            .blocks(&chars)
            .iter()
            .map(|b| match b {
                Block::Paragraph(p) => p.text(),
                Block::Table(_) => "table".into(),
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(texts, ["aoneb"]);
    }
```

```
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {
        // Only a .doc that converts gets the hint; an encrypted document
        // or another OLE file would be sent to a command that fails.
        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
            format!(
                "; a .doc converts with: jubarte convert {} -o {}",
                path.display(),
                path.with_extension("docx").display()
            )
        } else {
            String::new()
        };
        return Err(format!("{refused}{hint}"));
```

**Legacy reader caller** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:180-225`

Story processing is called on the decoded main text.

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
}
```

```
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {
        // Only a .doc that converts gets the hint; an encrypted document
        // or another OLE file would be sent to a command that fails.
        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
            format!(
                "; a .doc converts with: jubarte convert {} -o {}",
                path.display(),
                path.with_extension("docx").display()
            )
        } else {
            String::new()
        };
        return Err(format!("{refused}{hint}"));
```

### [61] Tolerated XML syntax can hide recursive elements from admission

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Source establishes the complete relevant branch/control/dataflow. Runtime execution and deployment-specific exposure were not tested. |
| Category | Parser interpretation conflict / XML depth bypass |
| CWE | CWE-436, CWE-674 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/mod.rs:773-798, src/admission.rs:788-820, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:233-241, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:555-585, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:531-548, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:660-663, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:950-955 |

#### Summary

A DOCX author can place nested element text inside an XML comment after an unquoted attribute. Admission counts only shallow quick-xml events, while the permissive DOM parser consumes that attribute differently and recursively interprets the hidden tags. The normal .xml path can therefore exhaust the host stack despite max_xml_depth.

#### Root Cause

Admission uses quick-xml events and TagPolicy::tolerant, which accepts unquoted attributes, and ignores comments/DTD events for element depth. The downstream parser assumes the first attribute-value character is a quote delimiter even when it is not a quote. It can consume across the start-tag boundary into a comment, then parse comment content as real elements. Its DOCTYPE skip also stops at the first \> rather than the end of an internal subset, creating a related interpretation gap.

```rust
fn check_xml_depth(name: &str, xml: &[u8], limits: InputLimits) -> Result<(), AdmissionError> {
    let invalid =
        |why: String| AdmissionError::new(AdmissionErrorKind::InvalidXml, format!("{name}: {why}"));
    let text = part_text(xml);
    let mut reader = Reader::from_str(&text);
    reader.config_mut().check_end_names = true;
    let max_depth = limits.max_xml_depth;
    let mut policy = crate::xmllinq::parse::TagPolicy::tolerant(limits);
    let mut depth = 0usize;
    loop {
        match reader.read_event() {
            Ok(Event::Start(tag)) => {
                policy.open(&tag).map_err(invalid)?;
                depth = depth.saturating_add(1);
                if depth > max_depth {
                    return Err(invalid(format!("XML nests deeper than {max_depth}")));
                }
            }
            Ok(Event::Empty(tag)) => {
                policy.empty(&tag).map_err(invalid)?;
            }
            Ok(Event::End(_)) => {
                depth = depth
                    .checked_sub(1)
                    .ok_or_else(|| invalid("end tag with no open element".to_string()))?;
                policy.close();
            }
            Ok(Event::Eof) if depth > 0 => {
                return Err(invalid(format!("{depth} element(s) left unclosed")));
            }
            Ok(Event::Eof) => return Ok(()),
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(e) => return Err(invalid(e.to_string())),
```

#### Validation

For the unquoted/comment route, `<r a=x><!-- x>` followed by nested tags and a comment close is a shallow root/comment sequence to admission; raw parse_element treats the first x as a quote and the x inside the comment as its close. It then reaches the nested tags without recognizing the comment opener it already consumed. No later depth guard exists before recursive parse_element. A DTD internal entity literal containing nested tags similarly falls under ignored DocType events but the raw skip consumes only the first \>. These are grammar interpretation issues, not external-entity fetching. Strict validate_xml uses quoted attributes and explicitly refuses DTDs, but rendering's package-admission path does not invoke that strict gate.

Validation method: independent offline static source trace

**Admission counts one parser's events** — `src/admission.rs:788-820`

The gate uses tolerant attributes and counts only element events; comments and DocType do not contribute depth.

```rust
fn check_xml_depth(name: &str, xml: &[u8], limits: InputLimits) -> Result<(), AdmissionError> {
    let invalid =
        |why: String| AdmissionError::new(AdmissionErrorKind::InvalidXml, format!("{name}: {why}"));
    let text = part_text(xml);
    let mut reader = Reader::from_str(&text);
    reader.config_mut().check_end_names = true;
    let max_depth = limits.max_xml_depth;
    let mut policy = crate::xmllinq::parse::TagPolicy::tolerant(limits);
    let mut depth = 0usize;
    loop {
        match reader.read_event() {
            Ok(Event::Start(tag)) => {
                policy.open(&tag).map_err(invalid)?;
                depth = depth.saturating_add(1);
                if depth > max_depth {
                    return Err(invalid(format!("XML nests deeper than {max_depth}")));
                }
            }
            Ok(Event::Empty(tag)) => {
                policy.empty(&tag).map_err(invalid)?;
            }
            Ok(Event::End(_)) => {
                depth = depth
                    .checked_sub(1)
                    .ok_or_else(|| invalid("end tag with no open element".to_string()))?;
                policy.close();
            }
            Ok(Event::Eof) if depth > 0 => {
                return Err(invalid(format!("{depth} element(s) left unclosed")));
            }
            Ok(Event::Eof) => return Ok(()),
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(e) => return Err(invalid(e.to_string())),
```

#### Reachability

supplier of a DOCX rendered through public conversion APIs must trigger the described input path.

- **Attacker:** supplier of a DOCX rendered through public conversion APIs

- **Entry point:** src/convert/mod.rs

- **Outcome:** Process availability through stack exhaustion.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A small crafted document can reliably cause disproportionate allocation or stack use in a public parser path; impact is process availability, likelihood high when consumed. No remote deployment is assumed.

Additional runtime or deployment evidence could raise or lower this severity.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** Process availability through stack exhaustion.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Correctly quoted ordinary XML without DTD/comment interpretation gaps receives the expected depth check. Standalone checked XML parsing rejects the unquoted route and DTD; the report concerns public package processing using tolerant admission and raw DOM construction. No external entity resolution, network/file access or entity expansion is claimed.

#### Remediation

Make admission and DOM construction consume the same grammar, reject unsupported DTDs at package admission, parse unquoted values correctly or refuse them, and enforce a hard depth budget inside DOM construction.

Tests:
- Package processing must safely refuse or correctly parse an unquoted attribute followed by a comment containing deeply nested tag text.
- A DTD containing markup inside a quoted entity literal must be refused before raw DOM parsing; no external fetch should occur.
- Run the same fixtures through admission and the actual consumer and assert matching structure/depth semantics.

<a id="finding-62"></a>

### [62] Windows Markdown image checks can contact an external share before rejecting it

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Repository dataflow and installed Rust platform source establish UNC join replacement and Windows canonicalize calling File::open_native before containment. Credential capture itself was not tested or claimed. |
| Category | Unintended remote filesystem access before resource authorization |
| CWE | CWE-918 |
| Affected lines | src/bin/jubarte.rs:3365-3375, src/markdown/write.rs:4244-4247, src/bin/jubarte.rs:2819-2848, src/bin/jubarte.rs:2864-2870, src/bin/jubarte.rs:2888-2898, src/bin/jubarte.rs:3031-3039, src/bin/jubarte.rs:2665-2679, src/bin/jubarte.rs:3042-3063 |

#### Summary

Document-controlled image paths are canonicalized before resource-root containment is checked. On Windows, a decoded UNC path replaces the trusted root and canonicalization opens the remote path, causing outbound filesystem contact even when the image is later refused.

#### Root Cause

image_policy decodes the destination and rejects URL schemes only for non-absolute paths. root.join(path).canonicalize executes before strip_prefix(root). Windows UNC paths are absolute/prefixed, replace the original root during join, and cause canonicalize to open a remote path. The subsequent capability-relative read cannot undo that earlier ambient operation.

**Canonicalization precedes containment** — `src/bin/jubarte.rs:2819-2848`

Percent-decoding constructs a path; absolute paths bypass the scheme rejection and are canonicalized before strip_prefix.

```
    while at < bytes.len() {
        let hex = bytes
            .get(at + 1..at + 3)
            .and_then(|h| std::str::from_utf8(h).ok())
            .and_then(|h| u8::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok());
        match (bytes[at], hex) {
            (b'%', Some(byte)) => {
                decoded.push(byte);
                at += 3;
            }
            (byte, _) => {
                decoded.push(byte);
                at += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    let named = std::str::from_utf8(&decoded).map_err(|_| "not found")?;
    let path = PathBuf::from(named);
    // Decoded first, so an encoded scheme (`file%3A%2F%2F…`, `DATA%3A`)
    // is judged as what it names, not as an opaque relative path.
    if !path.is_absolute() && url_scheme(named) {
        return Err("a URL scheme");
    }
    // Canonicalized, `..` and links resolve to what the name really
    // names; the prefix check keeps the read inside `root`.
    let target = root.join(path).canonicalize().map_err(|_| "not found")?;
    target
        .strip_prefix(root)
        .map(Path::to_path_buf)
        .map_err(|_| "outside the resource root")
```

#### Reachability

Native CLI conversion, comparison, paragraph patch and text-only image-refusal diagnostics share image_policy. The attacker controls the document destination, not --resource-path or host environment.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted Markdown author

- **Entry point:** Native Windows CLI Markdown resource loading and diagnostics

- **Outcome:** Contact with attacker-selected network share before rejection

Preconditions:
- Victim uses Windows native CLI on supplied Markdown.
- For authentication disclosure/relay: reachable remote share and Windows outbound-authentication policy that permits it.

#### Severity

**Medium** — An untrusted Markdown author can trigger a remote filesystem open through native Windows conversion and even text-diff diagnostics. Outbound authentication disclosure or relay requires reachable SMB/WebDAV and permissive Windows policy; those deployment facts are unknown. High potential impact with conditional likelihood is medium.

Confirmed outbound authentication/relay exposure raises impact confidence; blocked outbound shares or restrictive authentication policies reduce impact.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Depending on policy, outbound Windows authentication can be disclosed or relayed; direct established impact is unintended remote filesystem access.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Windows and network/authentication policy prerequisites apply; no concrete deployment provided.

#### Remediation

Reject decoded absolute, prefixed, UNC and root-relative destinations before any ambient filesystem operation, and resolve accepted relative resources through the held directory capability. Apply the same policy to diagnostic-only paths.

Tests:
- Verify encoded UNC, verbatim UNC and root-relative destinations are rejected before any filesystem resolver is called on Windows.
- Cover convert, compare, patch and text-diff diagnostics and preserve allowed in-root relative images.

### [63] Tracked-edit audit parses permission-bearing XML before admission

#### Summary

audit_tracked opens both packages and checks dropped permission ranges before reject_changes later admits edited bytes. #### Summary

An attacker-authored Word 97–2003 DOC can repeatedly begin fields and enter their result sections, leaving an increasingly long all-false field stack. Story::blocks scans the entire stack before every input character, giving quadratic CPU work during reading/conversion and even the native Word-input refusal hint.

#### Root Cause

The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec\<bool\> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec\<bool\> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

**Control preservation** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:1115-1129`

cp1252 preserves ASCII-range field markers.

```rust
/// Windows-1252 bytes 0x80-0x9F as the spec's compressed-text table maps
/// them (MS-DOC 2.4.1); every other byte is its own code point.
fn cp1252(byte: u8) -> char {
    const HIGH: [u16; 32] = [
        0x20AC, 0x0081, 0x201A, 0x0192, 0x201E, 0x2026, 0x2020, 0x2021, 0x02C6, 0x2030, 0x0160,
        0x2039, 0x0152, 0x008D, 0x017D, 0x008F, 0x0090, 0x2018, 0x2019, 0x201C, 0x201D, 0x2022,
        0x2013, 0x2014, 0x02DC, 0x2122, 0x0161, 0x203A, 0x0153, 0x009D, 0x017E, 0x0178,
    ];
    match byte {
        0x80..=0x9F => HIGH
            .get(usize::from(byte.wrapping_sub(0x80)))
            .and_then(|&unit| char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)))
            .unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'),
        _ => char::from(byte),
    }
```

**Legacy reader caller** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:180-225`

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
}
```

#### Validation

Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -\> main_text -\> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection. Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -\> legacy_doc::read -\> main_text -\> Story::blocks -\> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops. Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For \[0x13,0x14\] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): For n nested begin/separator pairs left in their result state, each separator and subsequent character scans an increasing all-false vector. Closing them later or supplying n result characters preserves quadratic comparisons. No text reuse or physical-offset violation is required.

Validation method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

**Control preservation** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:1115-1129`

cp1252 preserves ASCII-range field markers.

```rust
/// Windows-1252 bytes 0x80-0x9F as the spec's compressed-text table maps
/// them (MS-DOC 2.4.1); every other byte is its own code point.
fn cp1252(byte: u8) -> char {
    const HIGH: [u16; 32] = [
        0x20AC, 0x0081, 0x201A, 0x0192, 0x201E, 0x2026, 0x2020, 0x2021, 0x02C6, 0x2030, 0x0160,
        0x2039, 0x0152, 0x008D, 0x017D, 0x008F, 0x0090, 0x2018, 0x2019, 0x201C, 0x201D, 0x2022,
        0x2013, 0x2014, 0x02DC, 0x2122, 0x0161, 0x203A, 0x0153, 0x009D, 0x017E, 0x0178,
    ];
    match byte {
        0x80..=0x9F => HIGH
            .get(usize::from(byte.wrapping_sub(0x80)))
            .and_then(|&unit| char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)))
            .unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'),
        _ => char::from(byte),
    }
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn a_field_nested_in_a_field_code_shows_only_the_outer_result() {

        let lists = Lists::default();
        // { IF { PAGE } = 1 "one" } displaying "one": the PAGE result "1"
        // sits in the outer field's code and is not shown.
        let chars = story_chars("a\u{13}IF \u{13}PAGE\u{14}1\u{15} = 1 \"one\"\u{14}one\u{15}b\r");
        let story = Story {
            papx: &papx,
            chpx: &chpx,
            styles: &[],
            lists: &lists,
            section_marks: Vec::new(),

        let texts: Vec<String> = story
            .blocks(&chars)
            .iter()
            .map(|b| match b {
                Block::Paragraph(p) => p.text(),
                Block::Table(_) => "table".into(),
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(texts, ["aoneb"]);
    }
```

**Legacy reader caller** — `src/legacy_doc.rs:180-225`

Story processing is called on the decoded main text.

```rust
pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<LegacyDocument> {
    let file = CompoundFile::open(bytes)?;
    let word = file.stream("WordDocument").ok_or_else(|| {
        LegacyDocError::new(
            "no WordDocument stream: an encrypted document or not a Word file; open it in Word and save it as .docx without a password",
        )
    })?;
    let fib = Fib::parse(&word)?;
    let table = file
        .stream(if fib.table_one { "1Table" } else { "0Table" })
        .ok_or_else(|| LegacyDocError::new("the table stream the FIB names is missing"))?;
    let pieces = pieces(&table, fib.fc_clx, fib.lcb_clx)?;
    let chars = main_text(&word, &pieces, fib.ccp_text)?;
    let styles = heading_styles(&table, fib.fc_stshf, fib.lcb_stshf)?;
    let papx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_papx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_papx),
        Fkp::Paragraph,
    )?;
    let chpx = FkpIndex::new(
        &word,
        &table,
        (fib.fc_plcf_bte_chpx, fib.lcb_plcf_bte_chpx),
        Fkp::Character,
    )?;
    let lists = Lists::new(&table, fib.plf_lst, fib.plf_lfo)?;
    let story = Story {
        papx: &papx,
        chpx: &chpx,
        styles: &styles,
        lists: &lists,
        section_marks: section_marks(&table, fib.plcf_sed)?,
    };
    Ok(LegacyDocument {
        blocks: story.blocks(&chars),
    })
}
```

**Refusal hint also reaches field parsing** — `src/bin/jubarte.rs:2740-2754`

A rejected input is fully parsed merely to create a conversion hint.

```
fn read_document(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if let Some(refused) = jubarte::cli::refused_input(path, &bytes, false) {
        // Only a .doc that converts gets the hint; an encrypted document
        // or another OLE file would be sent to a command that fails.
        let hint = if jubarte::legacy_doc::read(&bytes).is_ok() {
            format!(
                "; a .doc converts with: jubarte convert {} -o {}",
                path.display(),
                path.with_extension("docx").display()
            )
        } else {
            String::new()
        };
        return Err(format!("{refused}{hint}"));
```

A legacy DOC author controls the story passed to legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown, doc_to_docx and native CLI convert. Native Word-input refusal also reads the DOC for its conversion hint. A valid OLE container, Word FIB and covering piece table are required; no privileged configuration is needed. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): The public reader invokes Story::blocks after decoding main text; conversion and native refusal hints share it.

Existing controls:

Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

- **Rationale:** Processing-thread CPU exhaustion and conversion service degradation. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: CPU denial of service of processing host.
- **Why:** Repeated nested field beginnings followed by separators leave an increasingly long all-false field-state stack. Each subsequent character scans that stack. The map-depth, paragraph-index and instruction-length controls apply to different structures and do not bound nested results.

```
fn result_end(text: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut depth = 0usize;
    let mut at = 0;
    while at < text.len() {
        let rest = &text[at..];
        if rest.starts_with("\\{") {
            // `\{DATE}`, `\{/}`: text, not a field nor an end.
            at += 2;
        } else if rest.starts_with(FIELD_END) {
            if depth == 0 {
                return Some(at);
            }
            depth -= 1;
            at += FIELD_END.len();
        } else if let Some(after) = rest.strip_prefix('{')
            && let Some(close) = super::critic::field_code_close(after.char_indices())
            && super::critic::is_field_code(&after[..close])
        {
            depth += 1;
            at += 1 + close + 1;
        } else {
            at += rest.chars().next().map_or(1, char::len_utf8);
        }
    }
    None
```

**Instruction length is bounded separately** — `src/markdown/critic.rs:1608-1626`

The existing 1024-character cap applies to each short instruction, so it does not bound the number of nested results.

```

/// Where the `}` that closes a field code sits, given the characters after
/// its `{` with their positions: a brace inside a quoted argument (`"a}b"`,
/// `\"` quoting a quote) belongs to the code. None at an unquoted `{`, a
/// line end, or no `}` within [`LONGEST_FIELD_CODE`].
pub(crate) fn field_code_close(chars: impl Iterator<Item = (usize, char)>) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut quoted = false;
    let mut backslash = false;
    for (at, c) in chars.take(LONGEST_FIELD_CODE) {
        match c {
            '\n' | '\r' => return None,
            '"' if !backslash => quoted = !quoted,
            '{' if !quoted => return None,
            '}' if !quoted => return Some(at),
            _ => {}
        }
        backslash = c == '\\' && !backslash;
    }
    None
```

#### Validation

Confirmed nested PAGE fields in one quoted scalar are restored and passed to runs; each matching coded result becomes another call. Repeated result matching also scans nested suffixes. Critic frontmatter handling excludes FIELD interpretation, leaving the story parser to process this syntax.

#### Summary

Paragraph and numbering-definition ilvl attributes accept arbitrary u32 values. Resolving an undefined high level scans every lower integer; defining the high level instead drives counter initialization and label substitution loops over the same enormous range. Abstract definitions and full lvlOverride records accept the same unchecked level IDs; both missing-level reverse search and defined-level counter/label work require bounded handling. Assigned discovery-0032 preserves the valid numbering-instance prerequisite and the distinct billion-level defined-counter variant as well as undefined-level backwards search.

#### Root Cause

List-level consumers iterate the numeric domain selected by untrusted attributes rather than a bounded supported-level domain or actual map keys. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Semantic numbering-level identifiers are accepted as unrestricted u32 values and reused as numeric iteration bounds instead of being validated or looked up among actual defined levels. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `num_pr()` parses unbounded u32 `ilvl`. Numbering fallback uses `(0..ilvl).rev().find(...)` to locate a lower defined level. Work scales with attacker-selected identifier magnitude rather than the number of actual definitions. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Numbering metadata is accepted as arbitrary u32 and used as the extent of dense scans and counter materialization, without validating the supported level range. Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): `num_pr()` accepts every u32 list-level value and numbering definitions accept the same unbounded identifier domain. `list_marker()` forwards it into `Numbering`. For a missing level, `resolve_ilvl()` and `ensure_level()` search descending integers. For an attacker-defined high level, `next_marker()` iterates every smaller integer and creates owned counter-map entries, even when those intermediate levels are absent. Marker rendering also iterates to `ilvl`. The numeric identifier is incorrectly treated as a count rather than a bounded Word numbering level.

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
```

#### Validation

Independently traced DOCX paragraph w:numPr/w:ilvl -\> num_pr -\> numbering lookup -\> resolve_ilvl reverse integer scan; defined high levels -\> next_marker lower-level counter insertion and render loop. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified num_pr -\> list_marker -\> next_revised/next_marker -\> resolve_ilvl. A request for u32::MAX with only level 0 defined causes about 4.3 billion reverse lookups. Defining a huge level bypasses that search but reaches lower-counter materialization for every level. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a paragraph level 4,000,000,000 with only level zero defined causes about four billion parent-level probes. Defining the high level moves the failure to lower-counter initialization; fixing only the fallback search leaves that independently reachable operation. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Traced paragraph numPr through list_marker/next_revised/next_marker to resolve_ilvl. A normal abstract list defining only level zero and a huge undefined requested level avoids the exact-key fast path and forces the reverse-range scan. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Paragraph numbering and style inheritance use num_pr without an ilvl cap (src/convert/mod.rs:12683-12718,12834-12879). An undefined u32-max paragraph level reaches resolve_ilvl's reverse scan with an ordinary level-zero parent. A defined high level bypasses that search but reaches the counters loop. Abstract levels and full overrides have no upper-bound check, so both paths remain reachable after admission. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified paragraph parsing, explicitly defined level parsing at 6618-6644, list_marker/next_revised/next_marker calls, fallback search, dense counter initialization and render placeholder scan. A tiny ordinary package passes byte/depth limits while carrying the oversized integer. Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Verified a real `numId` -\> `abstractNum` mapping is required and can be supplied in the same numbering part. Setting a large undefined ilvl causes a long backwards lookup; defining and using level 1,000,000,000 reaches the ancestor-counter loop without that lookup fallback and requests about a billion map entries. Admission's storage/depth checks do not constrain these semantic values.

Validation method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

**Render imports a related HTML chunk after admission** — `src/convert/mod.rs:769-798`

Untrusted DOCX bytes are admitted, then the related chunk bytes are passed to `altchunk::expand` before DOM construction.

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .or_else(|| {
            pkg.part_bytes("word/document.xml")
                .map(|_| "word/document.xml".to_string())
        })
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    let xml = pkg
        .part_string(&main)
        .ok_or(ConvertError::MissingDocument)?;
    // Word merges `w:altChunk` content (HTML / MHT) into the body on open.
    let xml = if xml.contains("<w:altChunk") {
        altchunk::expand(&xml, |rid| {
            rel_target_path(&pkg, &main, rid).and_then(|p| pkg.part_bytes(&p).map(<[u8]>::to_vec))
        })
    } else {
        xml
    };
    let mut dom = Dom::new();
    let doc = dom.parse_xdocument(&xml);
```
