#### Reachability

The attacker must influence the reference document selected by a caller. This is a public library and binding input boundary; no network service is assumed.

- **Attacker:** A document producer supplying an untrusted reference DOCX to a Markdown-to-DOCX conversion.

- **Entry point:** Markdown-to-DOCX reference parameter

- **Outcome:** Process abort or WASM trap from stack exhaustion.

Existing controls:
- PartFs bounds compressed size, entries, per-part inflation and aggregate inflation, preventing an unrestricted ZIP decompression path.
- The conventional document-processing entry points commonly perform admission; that control is absent from this particular reference-document path.
- Optional acceptance or rejection of revisions happens after package assembly, so any admission there occurs after the vulnerable parse.
- Hosts that independently admit every reference before calling this API can prevent this attack, but the public function and bindings do not require or enforce that precondition.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A caller processing an untrusted reference can lose its native/WASM conversion process. Supplying a reference is an additional workflow prerequisite, and no public service exposure or execution beyond denial of service is established.

A deployed unattended template-conversion service would raise operational impact; pre-admission of every reference or checked parsing prevents the path.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** The current conversion worker becomes unavailable.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Once the untrusted reference is selected, assembly parses its XML unconditionally.

#### Remediation

Admit options.reference before any reference inspection or assembly, return a typed reference refusal on failure, and use checked parsing when extracting section properties. Add a regression that supplies a normally named over-depth main document as reference through the Rust API and bindings.

Tests:
- Pass an over-depth reference with conventional word/document.xml through Rust and binding APIs and expect a typed refusal before parsing.
- Verify default template conversion remains unchanged.

#### Summary

Opening a package repairs identical duplicate relationship IDs. For n distinct IDs each repeated identically, each repair linearly searches an increasingly long Vec, producing quadratic CPU work on shallow metadata that fits existing byte and attribute limits. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies approximately 200000 shallow Relationship records with 100000 distinct identical duplicate pairs within a 64 MiB part, implying about five billion membership comparisons. Conflicting duplicates remain promptly refused; counts are static.

#### Root Cause

Duplicate reporting uses repaired.contains on a growing Vec even though first-occurrence lookup already uses a HashMap. Root and every part relationship set invoke this repair. N distinct IDs each duplicated identically require N(N-1)/2 prior-ID string comparisons despite first-occurrence hashing; byte/depth/attribute checks do not limit this product. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): An ordered report vector is also used as a membership set, so the first duplicate of each new ID scans all preceding repaired IDs. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read_relationships` preserves the record list and `PartFs::open_within` invokes `drop_repeated_relationships`. Its `seen` map finds duplicates efficiently, but each duplicate then uses `repaired.contains` over all previously repaired IDs. Repeating each of N distinct IDs twice requires roughly N(N-1)/2 string comparisons. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The duplicate-repair result is used as a linear membership set inside an attacker-sized loop, producing quadratic work over valid identical-duplicate relationship records. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies approximately 200000 shallow Relationship records with 100000 distinct identical duplicate pairs within a 64 MiB part, implying about five billion membership comparisons. Conflicting duplicates remain promptly refused; counts are static.

**Linear search for every distinct duplicate** — `src/opc/mod.rs:99-124`

Linear search for every distinct duplicate supports the validated source-to-sink trace.

```rust
fn drop_repeated_relationships(rels: &mut Relationships) -> Result<Vec<String>, OpcError> {
    let mut seen: HashMap<&str, &Relationship> = HashMap::new();
    let mut repaired: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut keep = Vec::with_capacity(rels.items.len());
    for item in &rels.items {
        match seen.get(item.id.as_str()) {
            None => {
                seen.insert(&item.id, item);
                keep.push(true);
            }
            Some(first) => {
                if first.rel_type != item.rel_type
                    || first.target != item.target
                    || first.target_mode != item.target_mode
                {
                    return Err(OpcError::InvalidRelationship);
                }
                if !repaired.contains(&item.id) {
                    repaired.push(item.id.clone());
                }
                keep.push(false);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut keep = keep.into_iter();
    rels.items.retain(|_| keep.next().unwrap_or(true));
```

**Retain all relationship records** — `src/opc/mod.rs:222-250`

```rust
fn read_relationships(xml: &[u8]) -> Result<Relationships, OpcError> {
    let mut rels = Relationships::new();
    let mut items = Vec::new();
    for record in metadata_records(
        xml,
        "Relationships",
        "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships",
        &["Relationship"],
    )? {
        for item in oxml_opc::Relationships::from_xml(&record)?.items {
            items.push(item);
        }
    }
    // Seed the private counter once: add_with_id removes existing IDs, so
    // calling it for every record would turn a linear read into a quadratic one.
    // A fresh collection also has no retained source XML: to_xml stays canonical.
    if let Some((_, item)) = items
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|item| {
            item.id
                .strip_prefix("rId")
                .and_then(|id| id.parse::<u32>().ok())
                .map(|id| (id, item))
        })
        .max_by_key(|(id, _)| *id)
    {
        rels.add_with_id(&item.id, &item.rel_type, &item.target);
    }
    rels.items = items;
```

```rust
fn drop_repeated_relationships(rels: &mut Relationships) -> Result<Vec<String>, OpcError> {
    let mut seen: HashMap<&str, &Relationship> = HashMap::new();
    let mut repaired: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut keep = Vec::with_capacity(rels.items.len());
    for item in &rels.items {
        match seen.get(item.id.as_str()) {
            None => {
                seen.insert(&item.id, item);
                keep.push(true);
            }
            Some(first) => {
                if first.rel_type != item.rel_type
                    || first.target != item.target
                    || first.target_mode != item.target_mode
                {
                    return Err(OpcError::InvalidRelationship);
                }
                if !repaired.contains(&item.id) {
                    repaired.push(item.id.clone());
                }
                keep.push(false);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut keep = keep.into_iter();
    rels.items.retain(|_| keep.next().unwrap_or(true));
    Ok(repaired)
}
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn a_repeated_relationship_id_is_repaired_when_identical_and_refused_otherwise() {
        let font = |id: &str, target: &str| {
            format!(
                r#"<Relationship Id="{id}" Type="{HYPERLINK}" Target="{target}" TargetMode="External"/>"#
            )

        let same = package_with_document_rels(&format!(
            "{}{}{}",
            font("rId1", "https://a.example/"),
            font("rId2", "https://b.example/"),
            font("rId1", "https://a.example/")
        ));
        let fs = PartFs::open(&same).unwrap();
        let rels = fs.read_rels_for("word/document.xml").unwrap();
        let ids: Vec<&str> = rels.items.iter().map(|r| r.id.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(ids, ["rId1", "rId2"]);
        assert_eq!(
            fs.repaired_duplicate_ids(),
            [("word/document.xml".to_string(), "rId1".to_string())]

            "{}{}",
            font("rId1", "https://a.example/"),
            font("rId1", "https://other.example/")
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            PartFs::open(&conflict),
            Err(OpcError::InvalidRelationship)
        ));
```

**Relationship records retained for repair** — `src/opc/mod.rs:222-251`

Relationship records retained for repair supports this input-to-CPU trace.

```
fn read_relationships(xml: &[u8]) -> Result<Relationships, OpcError> {
    let mut rels = Relationships::new();
    let mut items = Vec::new();
    for record in metadata_records(
        xml,
        "Relationships",
        "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships",
        &["Relationship"],
    )? {
        for item in oxml_opc::Relationships::from_xml(&record)?.items {
            items.push(item);
        }
    }
    // Seed the private counter once: add_with_id removes existing IDs, so
    // calling it for every record would turn a linear read into a quadratic one.
    // A fresh collection also has no retained source XML: to_xml stays canonical.
    if let Some((_, item)) = items
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|item| {
            item.id
                .strip_prefix("rId")
                .and_then(|id| id.parse::<u32>().ok())
                .map(|id| (id, item))
        })
        .max_by_key(|(id, _)| *id)
    {
        rels.add_with_id(&item.id, &item.rel_type, &item.target);
    }
    rels.items = items;
    Ok(rels)
```

**Linear repaired-ID membership** — `src/opc/mod.rs:99-125`

Every new duplicated ID searches all prior repaired IDs.

```rust
fn drop_repeated_relationships(rels: &mut Relationships) -> Result<Vec<String>, OpcError> {
    let mut seen: HashMap<&str, &Relationship> = HashMap::new();
    let mut repaired: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut keep = Vec::with_capacity(rels.items.len());
    for item in &rels.items {
        match seen.get(item.id.as_str()) {
            None => {
                seen.insert(&item.id, item);
                keep.push(true);
            }
            Some(first) => {
                if first.rel_type != item.rel_type
                    || first.target != item.target
                    || first.target_mode != item.target_mode
                {
                    return Err(OpcError::InvalidRelationship);
                }
                if !repaired.contains(&item.id) {
                    repaired.push(item.id.clone());
                }
                keep.push(false);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut keep = keep.into_iter();
    rels.items.retain(|_| keep.next().unwrap_or(true));
    Ok(repaired)
```

- **Rationale:** Uses ordinary shallow relationship XML and no optional configuration.

Optionally cap relationship-record/work totals before repair; test many distinct identical duplicate pairs while preserving deterministic repaired-ID order and conflicting-duplicate refusals. Apply an active relationship-record/work budget at metadata admission in addition to making duplicate membership near-linear.

### [83] Rendering a small DOCX table can allocate billions of columns

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | The unbounded gridSpan parser directly feeds row occupancy and vector allocations after admission. |
| Category | resource-exhaustion |
| CWE | CWE-789 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/mod.rs:14211-14215, src/convert/mod.rs:13601-13619, src/convert/mod.rs:14637-14644 |

#### Summary

The renderer accepts w:gridSpan and row grid skip values as unbounded usize counts. table_block sizes its column vectors from the summed spans, so a small admitted DOCX can request multi-gigabyte allocations or a capacity-overflow abort in PDF/PNG/report conversion.

#### Root Cause

The table parser interprets declared logical column spans as allocation counts, imposes only a minimum of one, and sums them without a table-width budget. table_block expands cols to occupancy and resolve_table_merges expands open to col+span. InputLimits bounds physical package/XML size rather than these numeric logical counts.

- **Entry point:** src/convert/mod.rs:769

- **Sink:** src/convert/altchunk.rs:489

Preconditions:
- A host renders/converts an attacker-controlled DOCX with a relationship to an HTML/MHT chunk.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Public render/convert APIs accept untrusted documents and a tiny accepted input produces arbitrarily large generated XML. Impact is availability of the processing host; remote/shared exposure depends on the embedding application.

Memory/CPU-limited isolated workers constrain impact; shared conversion service exposure increases affected availability.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium

#### Remediation

Reject or cap colspan before storing it, use checked totals, and enforce a total generated grid/output budget before expanding HTML/MHT chunks. Return a typed conversion refusal for oversized tables.

Tests:
- A tiny altChunk with colspan 1000000000 must fail before large output allocation.
- Cover inclusive limits, cumulative spans across cells, integer overflow, nested tables, and both HTML and MHT import.

#### Summary

accept_revisions and reject_revisions admit a DOCX, but the admission XML scan covers .xml/.rels names plus only the main part's alternate extension. A header/footer/notes/comments/styles relationship can point to header.dat containing deep XML; revision processing parses it without depth validation, permitting native stack exhaustion or a WASM trap.

#### Root Cause

Admission identifies XML by filename rather than all actual XML consumers. Relationship-selected auxiliary parts are subsequently passed to the permissive recursive DOM parser without the active XML depth/tag gate.

```
/// settles (#1223) between the notes and the styles.
pub(crate) fn revision_bearing_parts(pkg: &crate::opc::PartFs) -> Vec<(String, bool)> {
    let main = pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "word/document.xml".to_string());
    let mut headers = Vec::new();
    let mut footers = Vec::new();
    let mut endnotes = Vec::new();
    let mut footnotes = Vec::new();
    let mut comments = Vec::new();
    let mut styles = Vec::new();
    if let Some(rels) = pkg.read_rels_for(&main) {
        for r in &rels.items {
            if r.target_mode.as_deref() == Some("External") {
                continue;
            }
            let bucket = match r.rel_type.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or("") {
                "header" => &mut headers,
                "footer" => &mut footers,
                "endnotes" => &mut endnotes,
                "footnotes" => &mut footnotes,
                "comments" => &mut comments,
                "styles" => &mut styles,
                _ => continue,
            };
            bucket.push(pkg.resolve_rel_target(&main, &r.target));
        }
    }
    let mut out = vec![(main, false)];
    for p in headers
        .into_iter()
        .chain(footers)
        .chain(endnotes)
        .chain(footnotes)
        .chain(comments)
    {
        out.push((p, false));
    }
    for p in styles {
        out.push((p, true));
    }
    out
```

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- The main document's alternate extension is explicitly checked.
- ZIP inflation, CRC and entry budgets remain active.
- Raw parse_xdocument is intentionally unchecked; the bug is the admitted-package path missing the promised preceding gate.
- Inspect parse_part_within independently validates its selected XML.

Limitations:
- Offline static validation; application code and vulnerability-triggering inputs were not executed.

#### Dataflow

Attacker DOCX -\> accept_revisions/reject_revisions -\> admission extension scan -\> PartFs -\> revision_bearing_parts relationship targets -\> RevisionIds::new/process_part -\> raw parse_xdocument -\> recursive parse_element.

#### Reachability

A document supplier controls an internal auxiliary relationship and the part it names. The public accept/reject byte APIs parse selected parts even without a tracked revision in that part.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document supplier

Preconditions:
- Readable DOCX with a normal admitted main document and an internally related auxiliary part whose filename lacks .xml/.rels.
- Auxiliary part contains sufficiently deep XML within ZIP byte budgets.

Existing controls:
- The main document's alternate extension is explicitly checked.
- ZIP inflation, CRC and entry budgets remain active.
- Raw parse_xdocument is intentionally unchecked; the bug is the admitted-package path missing the promised preceding gate.
- Inspect parse_part_within independently validates its selected XML.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Attacker-controlled document input can deny service to the consuming process through the established parser/expansion path. No remote service is assumed; process isolation limits collateral impact.

A shared long-lived service without worker memory/CPU isolation increases availability impact; a bounded isolated job reduces impact to that job.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Host process CPU/memory/stack exhaustion can terminate or monopolize the worker.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** The attacker-controlled value reaches the identified operation through supported input APIs.

#### Remediation

Validate every actual XML part under active InputLimits immediately before DOM construction, or use content types/relationships to include all consumed XML in admission. Cover headers, footers, notes, comments and styles regardless filename.

Tests:
- Accept/reject refuse over-depth .dat auxiliary parts with the normal XML-depth error.
- The same refusal applies to excessive auxiliary tag/namespace fields while valid alternate filenames continue to work.

#### Summary

With docprops enabled, scrub removes metadata only from three conventional filenames. A document using alternate package relationship targets can retain creators, editors, dates, company/manager or custom properties while scrub returns success. The custom-properties branch additionally skips relationship/content-type removal when docProps/custom.xml is absent, leaving an active relationship to a relocated target such as metadata/private.xml.

#### Root Cause

`scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization. Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Sensitive metadata is selected by physical conventional filenames rather than its authoritative package relationships/content type. Structural before/after validation checks only newly introduced findings; it does not certify that selected privacy fields were removed. The assigned remediation includes supported Strict relationship variants and coexistence of conventional and relocated targets.

```rust
pub fn scrub(docx: &[u8], options: &ScrubOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ScrubError> {
    let mut pkg = PartFs::open(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .is_none_or(|main| pkg.part_bytes(&main).is_none())
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "the package has no main document part".into(),
        ));
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias
        && (alias.trim().is_empty() || alias.chars().any(char::is_control))
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "author_alias must be a nonempty name without control characters".into(),
        ));
    }
    let before = crate::validate::validate(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if options.comments {
        remove_comments(&mut pkg);
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias {
        alias_authors(&mut pkg, alias);
    }
    if options.rsids {
        remove_rsids(&mut pkg);
    }
    if options.docprops {
        scrub_properties(&mut pkg);
    }
    let out = pkg
        .to_zip()
        .map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    let after = crate::validate::validate(&out).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
```

```rust
    if let Some(mut core) = Part::load(pkg, CORE) {
        let names = [
            XName::get("creator", DC),

            XName::get("revision", CP),
            XName::get("lastPrinted", CP),
            XName::get("created", DCTERMS),
            XName::get("modified", DCTERMS),
        ];

            XName::get("Company", EXTENDED),

        if remove_children(&mut app, &names) {

        }

        pkg.remove_part(CUSTOM);
        pkg.remove_package_relationships_by_type(CUSTOM_REL);
        pkg.remove_content_type_override(&format!("/{CUSTOM}"));

}
```

**Scrub returns package after named operations** — `src/scrub.rs:109-155`

The operation invokes scrub_properties and only checks whether new validation errors were introduced.

```rust
pub fn scrub(docx: &[u8], options: &ScrubOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ScrubError> {
    let mut pkg = PartFs::open(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .is_none_or(|main| pkg.part_bytes(&main).is_none())
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "the package has no main document part".into(),
        ));
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias
        && (alias.trim().is_empty() || alias.chars().any(char::is_control))
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "author_alias must be a nonempty name without control characters".into(),
        ));
    }
    let before = crate::validate::validate(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if options.comments {
        remove_comments(&mut pkg);
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias {
        alias_authors(&mut pkg, alias);
    }
    if options.rsids {
        remove_rsids(&mut pkg);
    }
    if options.docprops {
        scrub_properties(&mut pkg);
    }
    let out = pkg
        .to_zip()
        .map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    let after = crate::validate::validate(&out).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    let new = introduced(&before, &after);
    if !new.is_empty() {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(format!(
            "scrubbing would introduce {}",
            new.join(", ")
        )));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// The findings `after` has more of than `before`, as `CODE in part`,
/// counted by code and part: removing elements shifts the paths of
/// findings that were already there.
```

#### Validation

A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact. Verified the scrub call chain, all three fixed-path branches, and preservation of surviving parts/package relationships. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue. Parent verified default docprops=true, fixed core/app/custom handling, unchanged-part serialization and Ok(out) after only introduced-finding checks. Python Document.scrub promises the same defaults. Recipient byte inspection establishes disclosure without requiring Word UI behavior. Additional validated trace gives a bounded well-formed metadata/core.xml selected by a root relationship and appropriate content type; absent conventional docProps/core.xml skips removal. Default public/CLI docprops scrub returns unchanged private bytes because general validation only rejects newly introduced findings, not failed privacy postconditions. Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected root relationship loading and raw-part preservation in opc/mod.rs365-376, property removal357-384 and scrub's before/after validation. For docprops-only scrub with an absent conventional CUSTOM file, no custom relationship/content removal occurs; unchanged retained metadata introduces no new validation finding and therefore returns successfully. This is a supported package-loader path, not a claim about an observed Word deployment. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified scrub contract (5-24), default docprops (68-75), public pipeline (109-150), fixed constants (39-47), complete scrub_properties (357-385) and relationship-aware custom_props_part (document_comparer.rs:6180-6188). Alternate related metadata remains unchanged; before/after validation only rejects newly introduced structural findings. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Scrub accepts packages by main document existence and returns the serialized output if validation introduced no new findings. Metadata processing loads only CORE, APP and CUSTOM constants. No alternative-target lookup occurs, and PartFs serializes every remaining raw part and package relationship. Consequently an alternate core/app target keeps its selected fields, while an alternate custom target also keeps its relationship.

Validation method: Preserved already-validated Standard source evidence and assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

```rust
pub fn scrub(docx: &[u8], options: &ScrubOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ScrubError> {
    let mut pkg = PartFs::open(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if pkg
        .main_document_part()
        .is_none_or(|main| pkg.part_bytes(&main).is_none())
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "the package has no main document part".into(),
        ));
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias
        && (alias.trim().is_empty() || alias.chars().any(char::is_control))
    {
        return Err(ScrubError::Invalid(
            "author_alias must be a nonempty name without control characters".into(),
        ));
    }
    let before = crate::validate::validate(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if options.comments {
        remove_comments(&mut pkg);
    }
    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias {
        alias_authors(&mut pkg, alias);
    }
    if options.rsids {
        remove_rsids(&mut pkg);
    }
    if options.docprops {
        scrub_properties(&mut pkg);
    }
    let out = pkg
        .to_zip()
        .map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    let after = crate::validate::validate(&out).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
```

```rust
    if let Some(mut core) = Part::load(pkg, CORE) {

        pkg.remove_part(CUSTOM);
```

```rust
        .is_none_or(|main| pkg.part_bytes(&main).is_none())

        ));

    let before = crate::validate::validate(docx).map_err(|e| ScrubError::Package(e.to_string()))?;
    if options.comments {
        remove_comments(&mut pkg);

    if let Some(alias) = &options.author_alias {
        alias_authors(&mut pkg, alias);
    }
    if options.rsids {
        remove_rsids(&mut pkg);
    }
    if options.docprops {
        scrub_properties(&mut pkg);

    let out = pkg
```

#### Reachability

Default ScrubOptions enables docprops. The public scrub API opens package relationships without constraining property filenames; no operator configuration is required. The recipient needs access to the shared scrubbed output, not the original source or victim machine. The owner must enable docprops, which the default scrub settings do. Public scrub with default options and Python Document.scrub default options expose the behavior.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document supplier or outgoing document recipient recipient of a scrubbed document

- **Entry point:** scrub with docprops enabled scrub::scrub with docprops enabled

- **Outcome:** Access to identifying property values intended to be removed

Preconditions:
- Metadata uses an alternate package target.
- User scrubs before distributing the resulting document.
- Document stores identifying properties in nonconventional internal part names.
- Owner requests metadata removal and later shares the output.

#### Severity

**Medium** — The user invokes a privacy operation before sharing, yet identifying or confidential property data remains. A supplier controls package names/relationships; no host privilege is needed. The selected scrub deterministically misses alternate targets.

Impact depends on metadata sensitivity and sharing. Resolving selected metadata through relationships/content types and verifying removal closes the gap.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Potential identifying/confidential document properties exposed to an outgoing-document recipient.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Requires alternate part layout, sensitive metadata and sharing after scrub.

#### Remediation

Resolve all core, extended and custom property parts through authoritative package relationships and content types, sanitize every applicable internal target according to docprops selection, and remove corresponding custom-property parts/relationships/content-type records coherently. Verify the selected privacy postcondition; refuse unsupported or ambiguous layouts rather than returning a successfully scrubbed copy. Preserve intentional title/subject/application and revision-date retention. Missing/invalid selected targets require explicit refusal or documented safe handling; default public and CLI callers must enforce the same postcondition. Include supported Strict property relationship variants and regression cases containing both conventional and relocated targets; every active property target must satisfy the requested postcondition.

Tests:
- Use alternate core/app/custom filenames and case variants with valid relationships/content types.
- Confirm selected fields/parts are absent and references coherent afterward.
- Keep intentional title/subject/application retention.
- Integration tests relocate each metadata part and update its relationship/content type, then verify the same fields are removed from outgoing package bytes.
- Cover multiple metadata relationships and conventional paths without losing unrelated intentional content.
- Relocate core/extended/custom parts with corresponding relationships and assert default scrub removes identifying values.
- Scrub core, extended and custom properties at relocated relationship-selected targets and assert requested identities are absent.
- Cover conventional paths, multiple metadata relationships and missing/invalid targets with explicit refusals or documented handling.
- Relocate each supported document-property part and relationship and assert docprops removes the selected metadata.
- Verify no stale custom-properties relationship or content-type override remains.
- Scrub core/app/custom metadata at alternate relationship targets and require equivalent removal.
- Cover multiple metadata targets and conventional-path decoys.
- Relocate each property class independently with matching relationship/content type and verify requested fields or entire custom part are absent.
- Cover packages with both conventional and relocated targets and verify no active property target survives unexpectedly.
- Cover relocated core, extended and custom property targets with default and explicit docprops options.
- Verify deliberate title/subject/application retention remains documented.

Preventive controls:
- Drive semantic metadata removal from OPC relationships/content types rather than conventional filenames.

<a id="finding-87"></a>

### [87] HTML selector groups multiply CSS values into excessive memory

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | HashMap\<String,String\> cloning occurs once per attacker-controlled selector before content use; ownership and lifetime are explicit in the full importer. |
| Category | Uncontrolled memory allocation |
| CWE | CWE-789, CWE-400 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/mod.rs:786-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:603-607, src/convert/altchunk.rs:152-170, src/convert/mod.rs:789-798, src/convert/altchunk.rs:34-39, src/convert/altchunk.rs:604-611, src/convert/altchunk.rs:149-170, src/convert/altchunk.rs:152-168, src/convert/altchunk.rs:604-610, src/convert/mod.rs:790-793 |

#### Summary

A DOCX HTML altChunk can combine one large CSS property value with thousands of grouped selectors. The importer deep-copies the complete property map into each selector, consuming gigabytes even if none of the rules are used. A supplied framing uses 4096 distinct selectors and one 1 MiB value for about 4 GiB of retained value storage, excluding overhead; this is a static estimate. Additional supplied static framing: 10000 distinct short selectors sharing a 1 MiB property imply about 10 GiB of retained values from approximately 1.1 MiB HTML; this is not a memory measurement.

#### Root Cause

parse_css stores an owned String per declaration, then props.clone deep-copies every value for each selector in the group. Selector count and declaration bytes are independent document-controlled quantities; no aggregate CSS allocation budget or declaration sharing is applied. Styles are collected before body interpretation, and arbitrary unused declaration keys/values retain these independent copies. Repeated identical selectors can reuse entries, so the proof uses distinct selectors.

#### Reachability

An untrusted document provider supplies a style block with grouped distinct selectors and a large declaration value; ordinary rendering parses it.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted DOCX/HTML provider

- **Outcome:** Memory exhaustion before content layout

#### Severity

**Medium** — A document sender directly controls both amplification factors in an admitted HTML part, making process memory exhaustion likely for a crafted document. No broader host compromise is inferred.

Sharing immutable declaration storage and enforcing aggregate rule/value budgets removes the amplification.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Rendering host availability loss.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Independent source-controlled factors directly multiply live allocations.

#### Remediation

Share immutable declaration maps/values across grouped selectors and enforce cumulative selector, rule and declaration-byte budgets before allocation. Enforce value-length limits and discard unsupported properties before retaining them; unused selectors and properties must still count toward the aggregate budget.

Tests:
- Parse large grouped selectors and verify declaration buffers are shared or a typed budget refusal occurs.
- Cover unused and unsupported CSS properties as well as normal cascading.
- Reject or boundedly process thousands of distinct selectors sharing a large declaration value.
- Ensure unused CSS rules are subject to the same storage budget and ordinary comma-separated selectors still render correctly.
- Assert that many selectors sharing a large declaration block remain bounded or are refused before multiplication.
- Cover unused selectors, unsupported property names, multiple style blocks, and valid boundary inputs.

Preventive controls:
- Account for multiplicative representation expansion at parser boundaries.

#### Summary

Untrusted direct OOXML gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter and imported HTML/MHT colspan values become unrestricted output column counts. Tiny metadata can request a billion columns, driving dense column/preference/merge vectors or pre-DOM gridCol XML generation before derived-output budgets. These independently reachable paths require controls before both import generation and layout; package byte/depth admission does not bound their semantic expansion.

#### Root Cause

DOCX gridSpan and imported HTML colspan are trusted as output column cardinalities with only a lower bound. Both document-table paths lack a shared grid/output budget before generation and allocation. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The renderer accepts cell spans and row skips as unbounded machine integers and expands sparse semantic counts into dense vectors without checked cumulative arithmetic or an allocation budget. The sibling HTML importer lacks the same column budget and performs span-sized XML emission. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The renderer treats document-controlled span counts as allocation sizes without a maximum semantic table width or checked aggregate occupancy. The HTML table importer likewise accepts unbounded colspan and materializes a grid proportional to it before DOM parsing.

```rust
fn with_layout<T>(
    docx: &[u8],
    emit: impl FnOnce(&Fonts, &[pdf::Page], &LayoutFacts) -> T,
) -> Result<T, ConvertError> {
    crate::document_comparer::admit_package(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let normalized = crate::strict_translation::strict_to_transitional_docx(docx)
        .map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(err.to_string()))?;
    let pkg =
        PartFs::open(&normalized).map_err(|err| ConvertError::OpenPackage(format!("{err:?}")))?;
```

#### Reachability

Public docx_to_png, render, report and PDF/layout paths call with_layout; attacker only needs to supply package bytes accepted by existing admission. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Public docx_to_pdf/docx_to_png/render/docx_render_report render caller-supplied DOCX bytes; the table is constructed before PDF/PNG output limits.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted DOCX supplier Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: A document author able to get a caller to render their DOCX.

- **Entry point:** src/convert/mod.rs:769

- **Sink:** src/convert/altchunk.rs:489 Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: cols.resize/vec allocation at src/convert/mod.rs:13606-13615

- **Outcome:** Memory exhaustion or renderer process termination.

Preconditions:
- A host renders/converts an attacker-controlled DOCX containing either a large w:gridSpan or an internal HTML/MHT chunk with a large colspan.
- Victim renders attacker-controlled DOCX content.

Existing controls:
- Admission limits archive/XML sizes and depth, but not numeric table spans.
- stretch_stale_spans skips rows whose used span already exceeds the grid; it does not clamp the attack.
- PNG raster limits occur after layout. SECURITY.md recommends external process limits, whose presence is not established.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Public render/convert APIs accept untrusted documents and a tiny accepted input produces arbitrarily large generated XML. Impact is availability of the processing host; remote/shared exposure depends on the embedding application.

Memory/CPU-limited isolated workers constrain impact; shared conversion service exposure increases affected availability.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Loss of availability of the rendering process.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Rationale:** A small document carries a representable large positive span; no unusual configuration is needed.

#### Remediation

Enforce practical per-cell span/row-skip and checked cumulative table/grid/output budgets across direct OOXML gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter and HTML/MHT colspan. Apply the common limit before HTML generation and before RawCell, column/preference/merge allocation or span-sized work; use checked sums and col+span arithmetic and return a typed conversion refusal. Neither importer-only nor later layout-only checking is sufficient. Use fallible allocation/reservation within those bounds so capacity failures become typed refusals. Carry the caller-configurable column/occupancy budget through every table source and enforce a generated-XML/output ceiling before altChunk materialization.

Tests:
- A tiny altChunk with colspan 1000000000 must fail before large output allocation.
- Cover inclusive limits, cumulative spans across cells, integer overflow, nested tables, and both HTML and MHT import.
- Cover direct OOXML gridSpan with tiny/no initial tblGrid, gridBefore/gridAfter variants, and merge bookkeeping as well as imported colspan.
- Test default public PDF and PNG/render entry points with small DOCX tables containing excessive gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter values; require typed refusal before allocation.
- Test cumulative multi-cell spans and machine-width boundary values, plus legitimate merged tables within the budget.
- Test boundary and over-limit gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter via public rendering APIs; assert bounded refusal without allocating attacker-sized storage.
- Test combined row spans and arithmetic overflow; preserve ordinary merged-cell rendering.
- Use small deterministic HTML fixtures to verify a large numeric colspan is rejected before output construction; test exact column-budget boundaries, overflow of aggregate spans, and normal merged-cell behavior.
- Test native gridSpan, gridBefore/gridAfter and combined-row occupancy at and beyond the budget, as well as aggregate arithmetic overflow.
- Use a small deterministic document with extreme semantic values or alternate valid OPC paths and assert controlled refusal or complete selected sanitization before expensive processing.

### [89] Flat LaTeX script chains bypass nesting limits and exhaust the writer stack

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Independent worker and parent verified the concrete input-to-sink control failure statically; exact runtime resource/failure thresholds were not measured. |
| Category | Uncontrolled recursion |
| CWE | CWE-674 |
| Affected lines | src/markdown/xml.rs:866-881, src/markdown/math.rs:831-841, src/markdown/math.rs:873-880, src/markdown/math.rs:929-942, src/markdown/math.rs:997-1013, src/markdown/math.rs:1571-1585, src/markdown/math.rs:1722-1736, src/markdown/math.rs:1762-1771, src/markdown/math.rs:1937-1947, src/markdown/math.rs:772-775 |

#### Summary

Converting untrusted Markdown with a long flat superscript/subscript chain builds an attacker-deep AST despite the parser's nesting limit. The recursive OMML writer then exhausts the native stack or traps a WASM instance.

#### Root Cause

The nesting guard tracks recursive parser calls. nested_list instead iteratively takes its previous output node as a new script base, preserving existing Scripts nodes through take_base. Each one-character script argument finishes before the next wrapper is added, so parse depth remains shallow while AST depth grows with input length. Writer::node recurses into that unbounded base through argument/nodes; no AST-depth or iterative traversal/destruction control intervenes.

**Markdown math reaches OMML** — `src/markdown/xml.rs:866-881`

The XML emitter passes the caller's LaTeX to math::omml.

```rust
    fn scripts(&mut self, base: Vec<Node>) -> Node {
```

```rust
fn take_base(out: &mut Vec<Node>) -> Vec<Node> {
    match out.pop() {
        None => Vec::new(),
        Some(Node::Group(nodes)) => nodes,
        Some(Node::Text(text, style, change)) => {
            let mut chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
            let last = chars.pop().map(String::from).unwrap_or_default();
            if !chars.is_empty() {
                out.push(Node::Text(chars.into_iter().collect(), style, change));
            }
            vec![Node::Text(last, style, change)]
        }
        Some(node) => vec![node],
    }
}
```

```rust
            let mut chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();

            if !chars.is_empty() {
                out.push(Node::Text(chars.into_iter().collect(), style, change));
            }
            vec![Node::Text(last, style, change)]
        }
        Some(node) => vec![node],
    }
}
```

#### Reachability

Victim converts attacker-controlled Markdown containing math.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document author

- **Entry point:** markdown::markdown_to_docx and shared binding/CLI callers

Preconditions:
- Victim converts attacker-controlled Markdown containing math.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Default processing of an untrusted document can exhaust worker CPU/stack; impact is availability, with blast radius dependent on process isolation.

Enforcing the missing input/derived-work boundary removes this path; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Host processing availability can be lost; no confidentiality or code-execution gain is established.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** A document supplier controls the triggering parser inputs with no privileged configuration.

#### Remediation

Bound actual AST depth and work when wrapping previous script/prime bases, and use iterative writing and safe nonrecursive destruction so rejection cannot itself drop an attacker-deep tree recursively.

Tests:
- A flat long a^1^1 chain must refuse or flatten within a fixed AST-depth budget.
- Exercise subscript/superscript alternation and prime wrapping, including writer and destruction after refusal.

Preventive controls:
- Bound the actual representation depth and processing work at the consuming boundary.

#### Summary

A drawing: image destination in ordinary Markdown is base64-decoded and deserialized into a dependency graph without validation. Package materialization recursively follows each dep.rels.part before writing the dependent part and has no active-node or completed-node map. A one-node self-reference causes indefinite recursion and stack exhaustion, even with default Markdown conversion options and no image loader. Header/footer drawing payloads also reach this same materializer through view_stories::story_part. Capture memoizes a part before descending, so even capture-produced envelopes can encode a cycle; capture count/byte limits do not establish an acyclic imported graph.

#### Root Cause

Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it. The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes. Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The deserialization boundary accepts arbitrary graph edges, while materialization assumes acyclic capture output and tracks names rather than graph traversal state. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `picture` recognizes a caller-authored `drawing:` destination and `decode` base64-decodes it into serde graph structs. Package assembly invokes `materialize`, which follows a root `part` index into `deps`. `dep_part` reserves a fresh name and clones XML, then follows every dependent `part` index by calling itself before writing or memoizing the current part. A root pointing to dependency 0 whose own relationship points to 0 repeats indefinitely. Capture's 64-part limits are not validated by decode and would not rule out a one-node cycle anyway.

```rust
/// Write dependent part `index` and its own dependency closure; its new
/// part name.
fn dep_part(
    drawing: &Drawing,
    index: usize,
    package: &mut PartFs,
    existing: &HashSet<String>,
    used: &mut HashSet<String>,
    next_doc_pr: &mut u32,
) -> Option<String> {
    let dep = drawing.deps.get(index)?;
    let name = name_for(&dep.name, existing, used);
    used.insert(name.clone());
    // The part's own relationships name the parts the recursion is writing;
    // their ids land in a rewrite of its `d{index}.{n}` symbols.
    let mut xml = dep.xml.clone();
    for (n, rel) in dep.rels.iter().enumerate() {
        let (kind, target, external) = match (&rel.u, rel.part, &rel.raw) {
            (Some(url), _, _) => (rel.kind.clone(), url.clone(), true),
            (_, Some(inner), _) if inner < drawing.deps.len() => {
                let inner_name = dep_part(drawing, inner, package, existing, used, next_doc_pr)?;
                (
                    rel.kind.clone(),
                    relative_rel_target(&name, &inner_name),
                    false,
                )
            }
```

```rust
) -> Option<String> {

        xml = xml.replace(&format!("\"{}\"", rel.sym), &format!("\"{rid}\""));
```

DOCX capture memoizes a part before descending, so cycles can be encoded even by the trusted writer; capture limits do not protect materialization.

```rust
    /// first use; `None` when the part is absent.
    fn dep_for(&mut self, package: &mut Package<'_>, target: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        if let Some(&index) = self.index.get(target) {
            return Some(index);
        }
        if self.parts.len() >= MAX_DEPS {
            self.failed = Some(format!("more than {MAX_DEPS} dependent parts"));
            return None;
        }
        let bytes = match package.read(target) {
            Ok(Some(bytes)) if bytes.len() as u64 <= MAX_DEP_BYTES => bytes,
            Ok(Some(_)) => {
                self.failed = Some(format!("{target} exceeds {MAX_DEP_BYTES} bytes"));
                return None;
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
        let index = self.parts.len();
        self.parts.push(Dep::default());
        self.index.insert(target.to_string(), index);
        let rels = package.rels(target).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut pay_rels = Vec::new();
```

```rust
/// Write dependent part `index` and its own dependency closure; its new
/// part name.
fn dep_part(
    drawing: &Drawing,
    index: usize,
    package: &mut PartFs,
    existing: &HashSet<String>,
    used: &mut HashSet<String>,
    next_doc_pr: &mut u32,
) -> Option<String> {
    let dep = drawing.deps.get(index)?;
    let name = name_for(&dep.name, existing, used);
    used.insert(name.clone());
    // The part's own relationships name the parts the recursion is writing;
    // their ids land in a rewrite of its `d{index}.{n}` symbols.
    let mut xml = dep.xml.clone();
    for (n, rel) in dep.rels.iter().enumerate() {
        let (kind, target, external) = match (&rel.u, rel.part, &rel.raw) {
            (Some(url), _, _) => (rel.kind.clone(), url.clone(), true),
            (_, Some(inner), _) if inner < drawing.deps.len() => {
                let inner_name = dep_part(drawing, inner, package, existing, used, next_doc_pr)?;
                (
                    rel.kind.clone(),
                    relative_rel_target(&name, &inner_name),
                    false,
                )
            }
            (_, _, Some(raw)) => (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(&name, raw), false),
            _ => return None,
        };
```

```rust
pub(crate) fn materialize(
    drawing: &Drawing,
    package: &mut PartFs,
    part: &str,
    existing: &HashSet<String>,
    used: &mut HashSet<String>,
    next_doc_pr: &mut u32,
) -> Option<String> {
    let mut xml = drawing.xml.clone();
    for rel in &drawing.rels {
        let (kind, target, external) = match (&rel.u, rel.part, &rel.raw) {
            (Some(url), _, _) => (rel.kind.clone(), url.clone(), true),
            (_, Some(index), _) if index < drawing.deps.len() => {
                let name = dep_part(drawing, index, package, existing, used, next_doc_pr)?;
                (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(part, &name), false)
            }
            (_, _, Some(raw)) => (rel.kind.clone(), relative_rel_target(part, raw), false),
            _ => return None,
        };
        let rid = relate(package, part, &kind, &target, external);
        xml = xml.replace(&format!("\"{}\"", rel.sym), &format!("\"{rid}\""));
```

**Syntax-only Drawing decoding** — `src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs:1395-1408`

Base64 is parsed as a Drawing without validating graph topology or graph budgets.

```rust
/// Decode the payload of `![label](drawing:PAYLOAD)`; `dest` is what
/// [`at`] returns (`drawing:…`).
pub(crate) fn decode(dest: &str) -> Result<Drawing, String> {
    let encoded = dest
        .strip_prefix("drawing:")
        .ok_or_else(|| "not a drawing: destination".to_string())?;
    use base64::Engine;
    let bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
        .decode(encoded)
        .or_else(|_| {
            base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE.decode(encoded.trim_end_matches('='))
        })
        .map_err(|e| format!("drawing payload is not base64: {e}"))?;
    serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|e| format!("drawing payload is not its JSON: {e}"))
```

**Capture permits graph cycles** — `src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs:591-612`

DOCX capture memoizes a part before descending, so cycles can be encoded even by the trusted writer; capture limits do not protect materialization.

```rust
    /// first use; `None` when the part is absent.
    fn dep_for(&mut self, package: &mut Package<'_>, target: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        if let Some(&index) = self.index.get(target) {
            return Some(index);
        }
        if self.parts.len() >= MAX_DEPS {
            self.failed = Some(format!("more than {MAX_DEPS} dependent parts"));
            return None;
        }
        let bytes = match package.read(target) {
            Ok(Some(bytes)) if bytes.len() as u64 <= MAX_DEP_BYTES => bytes,
            Ok(Some(_)) => {
                self.failed = Some(format!("{target} exceeds {MAX_DEP_BYTES} bytes"));
                return None;
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
        let index = self.parts.len();
        self.parts.push(Dep::default());
        self.index.insert(target.to_string(), index);
        let rels = package.rels(target).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut pay_rels = Vec::new();
```

#### Reachability

Public markdown_to_docx with default DocxOptions accepts drawing: destinations independently of image-loader callbacks; Rust/Python/WASM consumers processing that Markdown reach the same importer. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Public markdown::markdown_to_docx accepts the Markdown directly; CLI and bindings wrap this library boundary. No image-loader callback or filesystem authority is needed.

- **Attacker:** Supplier of untrusted input processed by a library consumer Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: untrusted Markdown document producer

- **Entry point:** markdown::markdown_to_docx

- **Outcome:** converter availability loss

Preconditions:
- Victim invokes the affected public API with attacker-controlled document input.
- A victim converts the supplied Markdown.

Existing controls:
- Valid serde types and in-range dependency indices are checked, but a self-reference satisfies them.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Medium process-availability impact with high likelihood when an application processes attacker-controlled document bytes. No remote service or host-wide compromise is assumed.

Shared in-process deployments may suffer broader availability loss; external process resource limits contain host impact but still permit worker termination.

**Impact assessment:** Stack overflow or equivalent runtime resource failure terminates conversion and can abort a native in-process host.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** A small shallow JSON envelope can express the required integer cycle.

#### Remediation

Validate dependency indices, count/byte/depth limits and graph shape at import. Materialize with an active/completed traversal state and index-to-output map, rejecting cycles or reserving identities to support cycles without recursive expansion. Memoize shared subgraphs. Enforce explicit dependency-edge and traversal-work budgets before assembly; when rejecting active-node revisits return a typed conversion refusal. Apply the same graph validation and traversal state to header/footer drawing materialization, not only body drawings.

Tests:
- Use one-node and two-node cyclic dependency graphs and assert refusal or bounded supported materialization.
- Test repeated acyclic shared dependencies and import count/depth limits.
- Convert a self-cycle and a two-node cycle and assert a typed refusal without recursion.
- Convert a deeply nested chain and a shared-dependency DAG under bounded work and ensure valid parts retain expected identity.
- Assert a self-cycle and a two-node cycle return a typed refusal without stack overflow.
- Assert a shared acyclic dependency materializes once and preserves relationships.
- Apply decode-side dependency/edge/byte budgets to external Markdown envelopes.
- Reject a self-reference and a two-node dependency cycle through public Markdown conversion.
- Verify shared acyclic dependencies materialize once and valid captured drawings round-trip.
- Self-cycles and two-node cycles in valid base64 Drawing payloads must return a typed error without recursion.
- A bounded shared-child DAG should reconstruct each node once and ordinary captured drawings should round-trip.
- Reject a one-node self-cycle and a two-node cycle without aborting the process.
- Preserve shared acyclic dependencies and reject over-budget dependency graphs.
- Cover one-node self-cycles, multi-node cycles, deep chains and repeated DAG edges.
- Assert either bounded rejection or correct shared-part materialization without process termination.
- Convert an inline drawing envelope with a self-cycle and assert a bounded typed refusal.
- Cover a two-node cycle, deep acyclic chain, repeated shared dependency and over-budget graph.

Preventive controls:
- Treat integer-indexed serialized graphs as untrusted graphs rather than assuming capture-produced invariants.

#### Summary

A successful plan that redacts sensitive text and edits nearby words can remove the text from both DOCX files while retaining it in the adjacent edit's source-context field. The generated report and report-bearing MCP response disclose that text despite the documented privacy guarantee.

#### Root Cause

All operations resolve against untouched source. A Replace context includes up to twenty original characters on each side. resolve_one sanitizes only Redact's own outcome, leaving nearby normal outcomes unchanged. report clones all outcomes, and final check_redactions scans only document bytes before returning and publishing the report.

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- The Redact operation's own context/refusal fields are explicitly sanitized.
- Both DOCX outputs are scanned for retained text; this does not cover report objects.
- Recipient exposure depends on sharing/logging the report or report-bearing response.
- Redact outcome itself is sanitized; the problem is another operation's source context.
- Both DOCX artifacts are scanned, and existing mixed-plan test demonstrates document secrecy but omits a report assertion.

Limitations:
- No application/test execution; the example identifier is existing test data.
- No application code or tests were executed.
- Actual unauthorized disclosure requires later sharing or logging to a less trusted recipient.

#### Dataflow

Original secret -\> nearby normal operation source context -\> unfiltered EditOutcome -\> EditReport -\> JSONL/JSON/MCP response.

- **Source:** Sensitive source text within another operation's context window

- **Sink:** Generated edit reports and report-bearing responses

- **Outcome:** Recipient recovers text absent from the visibly redacted DOCX.

#### Reachability

Public apply_plan returns report data; native CLI bundles and MCP docx_edit publish it. A recipient needs access to the report, not the original document.

- **Attacker:** Recipient of a purportedly redacted output/report; a document author can position sensitive text near an expected edit

- **Entry point:** Mixed redaction and ordinary-edit plan

- **Outcome:** Confidentiality loss beyond intended redacted output.

Preconditions:
- A redaction and nearby ordinary operation share a plan.
- Generated report or report-bearing response reaches a party lacking the original secret.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Sensitive document text crosses the intended redaction boundary into artifacts/responses a consumer may share. Impact is high for confidential content, with medium likelihood requiring a mixed plan and report exposure.

Lower when reports remain under the original document's access controls and are never shared; higher likelihood where bundles/reports are automatically distributed.

#### Remediation

Apply redaction-aware sanitization to every report, refusal and diagnostic field after resolving the full plan, including other operations' contexts. Check the final serialized reports for all redaction needles before publication, omitting unsafe context when needed.

Tests:
- Extend the existing adjacent redact+replace test to inspect EditReport, JSONL, CLI report.jsonl and MCP report.json/response for the removed identifier.
- Check mixed-plan failure outcomes and diagnostics as well as successful reports.
- Extend tests/scrub_and_redact.rs:353 mixed redact/replace case to assert secret absence from report JSON, JSONL and failure outcomes.
- Extend the existing mixed redact/replace fixture to assert serialized reports omit the removed value.
- Cover sibling-operation refusals and MCP/native/Python/WASM report serialization.

### [92] Repeated compressed-image references can exhaust renderer memory

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Parent source trace confirms independent decode inside the reference loop, owned retained buffers and later cloning; allocation arithmetic does not require an observed deployment. |
| Category | Missing aggregate decoded-media resource budget |
| CWE | CWE-770, CWE-400 |
| Affected lines | src/convert/mod.rs:18396-18404, src/convert/mod.rs:18425-18428, src/convert/mod.rs:20289-20312, src/convert/mod.rs:27564-27577, src/convert/mod.rs:769-786, src/convert/mod.rs:18396-18407, src/convert/mod.rs:20009-20012, src/convert/mod.rs:20289-20304, src/convert/mod.rs:18425-18429, src/convert/mod.rs:27564-27577, src/convert/mod.rs:18400-18408, src/convert/mod.rs:18425-18433, src/convert/mod.rs:20009-20013, src/convert/mod.rs:20289-20314, src/convert/mod.rs:773-798 |

#### Summary

A DOCX can reference one highly compressible embedded image many times. Conversion independently decodes and retains an owned pixel buffer per reference, then clones buffers into page operations. Package byte limits and per-page pixel limits do not bound this aggregate decoded memory. The assigned source confirms image 0.25.10's default 512 MiB allocation limit applies separately to each decode. A 4096x4096 RGBA raster requires about 64 MiB per occurrence and a hundred references retain gigabytes; authored drawing/page extents do not cap intrinsic decoded storage. These are supplied static counts. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a static 1000-reference framing for one ordinary solid 2048x2048 PNG: about 11.7 GiB of retained RGB alone before page painting. Group-picture, VML-preview and picture-bullet paths also independently decode resources; destination MAX_PAGE_PIXELS and per-decode limits do not bound aggregate retention.

#### Root Cause

Image collection visits each drawing/blip independently, resolves its part and calls `decode_image()`. Non-JPEG raster decoding returns owned intrinsic-size RGB/alpha vectors. Each reference retains that ImageKind in a LaidImage; painting clones the vectors again into page operations. No shared decoded cache or conversion-wide pixel/byte accounting exists on this path, so repeated references amplify one compressed part without increasing archive inflation correspondingly. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Per-decode decoder limits reset on each image::load_from_memory call and cannot replace a render-wide decoded-memory budget. Retained RGB/alpha layout buffers and subsequent display-list clones both require accounting. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a static 1000-reference framing for one ordinary solid 2048x2048 PNG: about 11.7 GiB of retained RGB alone before page painting. Group-picture, VML-preview and picture-bullet paths also independently decode resources; destination MAX_PAGE_PIXELS and per-decode limits do not bound aggregate retention.

**Destination page limit applies later** — `src/convert/raster.rs:24-42`

The pixel ceiling guards the later destination page allocation; it does not bound previously decoded source images or report-only text grouping.

```rust
/// Largest page raster, in pixels (1 GiB of RGBA): Letter and A4 fit at
/// 1200 dpi. A failed allocation would abort the process, Python host included.
const MAX_PAGE_PIXELS: u64 = 1 << 28;

/// Paint one laid-out page at `dpi` into RGBA pixels. Returns `None` for a
/// degenerate page size or one over [`MAX_PAGE_PIXELS`].
pub(crate) fn paint_page(fonts: &Fonts<'_>, page: &Page, dpi: f32) -> Option<Pixmap> {
    let scale = dpi / PT_PER_INCH;
    let (out_w, out_h) = if page.vertical {
        (page.height, page.width)
    } else {
        (page.width, page.height)
    };
    let width = (out_w * scale).ceil().max(1.0) as u32;
    let height = (out_h * scale).ceil().max(1.0) as u32;
    if u64::from(width) * u64::from(height) > MAX_PAGE_PIXELS {
        return None;
    }
    let mut pixmap = Pixmap::new(width, height)?;
```

#### Validation

Parent verified the loop, decoder and display-list copy. One 4096x4096 RGB buffer is 50,331,648 bytes; 100 references retain about 4.7 GiB before later copies. Small authored extents avoid large output pages without reducing intrinsic buffers. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): image 0.25.10 load_from_memory uses ImageReader with a default 512 MiB per-decode allocation limit. That limit resets for each call. A 4096x4096 RGBA raster is below that limit yet requires about 64 MiB per occurrence; a hundred references to one compressed image retain gigabytes while encoded package size remains small. The same paragraph's out vector retains all occurrences before returning.

Validation method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.

- **Status:** validated

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Per-decode dependency limits constrain one image, not aggregate retained samples.
- Output page raster cap at src/convert/raster.rs:26-42 applies after layout and does not count intrinsic image buffers.
- PDF image interning at src/convert/pdf.rs:506-566 happens after collection/display-list allocation.
- Package admission bounds original part bytes.
- A default decoder limit exists; this is not an unlimited single-image decode claim.
- ZIP admission limits compressed/inflated package bytes and the PNG page painter caps output-page pixels, but neither measures decoded source images across occurrences.
- Markdown media extraction separately checks a 50-million-pixel header limit and is a different path.
- SECURITY.md assigns host process limits to callers.
- Package inflated-byte budgets apply to media entry bytes, not decoded pixels per reference.
- Dependency per-decode limits do not stop repetition of ordinary 2048x2048 images.
- MAX_PAGE_PIXELS bounds later destination canvases rather than already retained source images.

Limitations:
- No high-memory document was executed.
- Static reasoning only; no large allocation or attack input was executed.
- No dynamic exploit or application tests were run; exact failure thresholds depend on architecture, allocator and host process limits.

#### Reachability

Shared public rendering/layout conversion automatically collects images; no privileged option or remote deployment is required for the library boundary. Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF/PNG rendering enters with_layout then collect_images for document paragraphs and stories. No remote deployment is required to establish the byte-input boundary.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted DOCX supplier Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): DOCX supplier

- **Entry point:** Public rendering and layout-report APIs Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Native/Python/WASM rendering APIs and their CLI/MCP adapters

- **Outcome:** Allocation failure terminates or traps the processing host

Preconditions:
- Victim renders attacker DOCX with many image occurrences and no sufficiently strict process memory quota.

#### Severity

**Medium** — A modest document can exhaust the rendering process; wider service impact depends on a downstream deployment and isolation.

Additional runtime or deployment evidence could raise or lower this severity.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Why:** Memory exhaustion can terminate the native process or WASM instance.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** medium
- **Why:** Requires victim rendering of supplied document; shared deployment unknown.

#### Remediation

Apply a conversion-wide decoded-pixel/byte budget before decoding or retaining media, cache decoded parts by source and transformation, and use shared immutable samples in layout/display operations. Count transformed and temporary buffers against the same budget. Apply the same sharing and aggregate accounting to group-picture, VML-preview and picture-bullet consumers, keyed by effective transformation; retain all earlier display-list/temporary-buffer accounting.

Tests:
- Assert repeated references share decoded sample storage and remain under an aggregate budget.
- Refuse a compressed image set exceeding total decoded limits before retaining copies; cover transforms and alpha intermediates.
- Render repeated references with a small decoded-byte budget and verify a typed refusal before large allocations.
- Confirm repeated references share decoded storage and per-image limits remain effective.
- Repeated references to one image must share immutable pixels and remain within an explicit aggregate decoded-byte budget.

### [93] Identical duplicate relationship repair performs quadratic scans

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Severity | medium |
| Confidence | high |
| Confidence rationale | Independent parent source review verified the input, transformations, effective controls and exact allocation/iteration/recursive operation. No runtime reproduction or platform-specific failure threshold was measured. |
| Category | Algorithmic complexity |
| CWE | CWE-407 |
| Affected lines | src/opc/mod.rs:222-235, src/opc/mod.rs:520-543, src/opc/mod.rs:99-125 |

#### Summary

A relationship part with K distinct IDs followed by an identical second copy of each causes K(K-1)/2 membership comparisons in drop_repeated_relationships. For K=50,000 this is about 1.25 billion comparisons, despite fitting the configured XML part budget. Public PartFs opening performs this repair automatically.

#### Root Cause

The duplicate detector uses a HashMap but separately tracks already repaired IDs in a growing Vec searched with contains for every identical duplicate.

**dedup loop** — `src/opc/mod.rs:99-125`

DOCX .rels records -\> per-record metadata parser preserving duplicates -\> PartFs::open/open_within -\> drop_repeated_relationships -\> growing repaired.contains scans. This excerpt establishes dedup loop.

```
fn drop_repeated_relationships(rels: &mut Relationships) -> Result<Vec<String>, OpcError> {
    let mut seen: HashMap<&str, &Relationship> = HashMap::new();
    let mut repaired: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut keep = Vec::with_capacity(rels.items.len());
    for item in &rels.items {
        match seen.get(item.id.as_str()) {
            None => {
                seen.insert(&item.id, item);
                keep.push(true);
            }
            Some(first) => {
                if first.rel_type != item.rel_type
                    || first.target != item.target
                    || first.target_mode != item.target_mode
                {
                    return Err(OpcError::InvalidRelationship);
                }
                if !repaired.contains(&item.id) {
                    repaired.push(item.id.clone());
                }
                keep.push(false);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut keep = keep.into_iter();
    rels.items.retain(|_| keep.next().unwrap_or(true));
    Ok(repaired)
```

```
    pub(crate) fn open_within(
        bytes: &[u8],
        limits: crate::admission::InputLimits,
    ) -> Result<Self, OpcError> {
        let mut fs = read_package(bytes, limits)?;
        let mut repaired_duplicate_ids: Vec<(String, String)> =
            drop_repeated_relationships(&mut fs.package_rels)?
                .into_iter()
                .map(|id| (String::new(), id))
                .collect();
        let mut owners: Vec<&String> = fs.part_rels.keys().collect();
        owners.sort();
        let owners: Vec<String> = owners.into_iter().cloned().collect();
        for owner in owners {
            if let Some(rels) = fs.part_rels.get_mut(&owner) {
                let part = owner.trim_start_matches('/').to_string();
                repaired_duplicate_ids.extend(
                    drop_repeated_relationships(rels)?
                        .into_iter()
                        .map(|id| (part.clone(), id)),
                );
            }
        }
        fs.repaired_duplicate_ids = repaired_duplicate_ids;
```

Counterevidence and remaining uncertainty:
- Conflicting duplicate records are refused immediately.
- ZIP entry-count caps do not cap relationship count inside a single part.
- Repeating one ID alone does not create the growing-vector worst case; the distinct-ID sequence does.

Limitations:
- Offline static validation; application code and vulnerability-triggering inputs were not executed.

#### Dataflow

DOCX .rels records -\> per-record metadata parser preserving duplicates -\> PartFs::open/open_within -\> drop_repeated_relationships -\> growing repaired.contains scans.

#### Reachability

A document supplier only needs a readable OPC package; package and part relationships are automatically repaired during open, before callers inspect the resulting package.

- **Attacker:** Untrusted document supplier

Preconditions:
- Many distinct relationship IDs each have an identical duplicate, rather than repeating only one ID.

Existing controls:
- Conflicting duplicate records are refused immediately.
- ZIP entry-count caps do not cap relationship count inside a single part.
- Repeating one ID alone does not create the growing-vector worst case; the distinct-ID sequence does.

#### Severity

**Medium** — Attacker-controlled document input can deny service to the consuming process through the established parser/expansion path. No remote service is assumed; process isolation limits collateral impact.

A shared long-lived service without worker memory/CPU isolation increases availability impact; a bounded isolated job reduces impact to that job.

Impact assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** Host process CPU/memory/stack exhaustion can terminate or monopolize the worker.

Likelihood assessment:
- **Level:** high
- **Rationale:** The attacker-controlled value reaches the identified operation through supported input APIs.

#### Remediation

Track repaired membership with a HashSet or a flag in the existing seen map, retaining the Vec solely for deterministic output order.

Tests:
- Many distinct identical duplicates repair with linear membership work.
- Conflicting duplicates still refuse and deterministic repaired-ID reporting is unchanged.

A DOCX containing an HTML/MHT altChunk can pass normal admission and then expand a short attacker-controlled `colspan` into one WordprocessingML grid column per declared column. The HTML conversion loop has no span, output-byte or work budget.
